items.body:
so, not entirely sure if this is a chaptarr issue or a unpackerr issue, but here goes.. 

unpackerr supports readarr and someone at their discord said this when i asked about chaptarr support:
```Assuming the api is staying as readarr should be able to plug it in as readarr for now```

items.title: [BUG] SQLite: memory grows to 8.2 GiB during initial library scan until the app stops answering HTTP
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

On a fresh Docker install using the default SQLite backend, container memory grew to 8.2 GiB during the initial library scan of a large existing library. It was never OOM killed (`OOMKilled=false`, `RestartCount=0`) and the container stayed `Up`, but the app stopped answering HTTP. The port was still bound and TCP connections were accepted, they just never got a response, including `wget http://127.0.0.1:8789/` run from inside the container itself. From outside it looks exactly like a reverse proxy or DNS fault, which is what I spent an hour chasing before I looked at memory.

The host is a Docker Desktop WSL2 VM with 11.69 GiB of RAM. By the time I checked it was down to 151 MiB available with 6.8 GiB of swap in use, so the whole VM was thrashing.

Setting `mem_limit: 4g` and recreating fixed it immediately. It now idles around 550 MiB anonymous and responds normally, and the VM went from 151 MiB to 8.7 GiB available.

**To Reproduce**

1. Fresh Docker install on the default SQLite backend, no `mem_limit` set.
2. Add root folders pointing at a large existing library and let the initial scan run.
3. Have several indexers enabled so RSS sync runs alongside it. Mine processes 1200 releases per cycle across 9 indexers.
4. Watch `docker stats` over a few hours. Memory climbs and does not come back down.
5. Eventually HTTP stops responding while the container still looks healthy.

**Expected behavior**

Memory plateaus at something bounded. If the host really is exhausted, failing visibly would be better than going silently unresponsive while every external signal still reports healthy.

**System Information:**
 - OS: Docker Desktop on Windows 11, WSL2 backend
 - Chaptarr Version: `0.9.911.0`
 - Installation Method: Docker, published `chaptarr/chaptarr:latest` image (Ubuntu 24.04, .NET 10.0.10)
 - Database: SQLite

**Additional context**

Two caveats on the 8.2 GiB so it is not read for more than it is worth. That figure is `docker stats` MemUsage, which includes page cache, and I did not capture the anon/cache split at the peak. Later, at 1.275 GiB reported, the split was 597 MiB anon against 1.7 GiB cache, so some real part of the peak was probably reclaimable cache from walking the library over a 9p bind mount. Against that, 6.8 GiB of swap was in use and page cache does not swap, so there was genuine anonymous memory in there.

While looking for a cause I found something in the SQLite path I cannot fully evaluate, so I would rather ask about it than assert it.

`BasicRepository.cs` raises the page cache ceiling inside bulk operations:

```csharp
prevSync = conn.ExecuteScalar<int>("PRAGMA synchronous");
conn.Execute("PRAGMA temp_store = MEMORY", transaction: tran);
conn.Execute("PRAGMA cache_size = -64000", transaction: tran);
```

The matching `finally` restores `synchronous` but not `cache_size` or `temp_store`:

```csharp
finally
{
    if (prevSync.HasValue)
    {
        try { conn.Execute($"PRAGMA synchronous = {prevSync.Value}"); } catch { }
    }
}
```

`cache_size = -64000` is 62.5 MiB and both pragmas are per connection. `ConnectionStringFactory.cs` sets `Pooling = true` with `Cache = SqliteCacheMode.Private`, and Microsoft.Data.Sqlite defaults to a max pool size of 100, so every pooled connection carries its own page cache.

So my question is whether a connection returned to the pool keeps the raised `cache_size` ceiling. I could not find anything in the Microsoft.Data.Sqlite docs or in Brice Lambson's 6.0 pooling post that states whether per-connection state is reset on return, and I did not want to report a mechanism I could not confirm. If it does persist, a large scan that touches many pooled connections would have a lot of headroom to grow into before the GC has any reason to collect, which fits the shape of what I saw.

The runtimeconfig also has no `System.GC.Server` entry, so an uncapped container sizes its heap budget against total host RAM rather than a cgroup limit. That on its own could explain the growth without anything being retained at all, in which case this is a docs fix rather than a bug.

Either way, would you consider adding a `mem_limit` to the published `docker-compose.yml`, or a line in the README? Uncapped, this failure is silent, and the symptom it presents (healthy container, bound port, no HTTP response) points away from the actual cause.

comments.body:
We hit this exact failure twice this week on a large library (six-figure file count, Postgres backend, so it's not SQLite-specific) and can add the mechanism behind what you observed.

**Why it goes unresponsive without being OOM-killed:** .NET sizes its GC heap from the container's cgroup memory limit. With no `mem_limit`, it sees the whole host/VM (your 11.69 GiB) and permits a heap of roughly 75% of that. A large initial scan legitimately grows the heap toward that ceiling — and as the runtime approaches it, collections become near-continuous: every thread spends most of its time paused for GC, so TCP accepts (kernel-level) but requests never get serviced. Container stays "healthy", port stays bound, `wget` from inside hangs — exactly your symptom. Meanwhile the VM swaps underneath, which makes each GC pass slower and compounds the spiral.

Your `mem_limit: 4g` fix works precisely because the runtime then self-bounds at ~3 GiB and collects aggressively instead of sprawling.

**What has held up for us in production:** an explicit `mem_limit` sized for what the host can actually spare, plus `DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimitPercent: "85"` so the heap boundary is explicit rather than the 75% heuristic. On our library the app needs several GiB of real heap during mass scans, and with the limit in place it stays responsive at sustained 100%+ CPU instead of dying silently. Worth documenting a recommended `mem_limit` in the example compose - the failure mode looks so much like a reverse-proxy fault that it costs people hours (it cost us a power-cycle before we understood it).

**One compounding allocator on large libraries:** `GET /api/v1/bookFile?unmapped=true` materializes every unmapped row in one response - on a library with a six-figure unmapped count (exactly the state a large initial scan produces) that's a substantial burst on top of scan memory, and the Unmapped Files page issues it on load. We run a paging patch for that endpoint + UI locally (page went from timing out/OOM to sub-second) and are happy to PR it if there's interest.

Adding a data point to this one, since I think it partially answers the GC-sizing question raised at the end — and my case is the opposite of yours on the memory-exhaustion side.

## Setup

- Chaptarr `0.9.911.0` (build 2026-08-08), .NET 10.0.10, Ubuntu 24.04
- Docker Compose, published `chaptarr/chaptarr:latest`
- SQLite backend
- Unprivileged Proxmox LXC (CT), Docker inside the CT
- Symptom matches yours: TCP connects to `8789` and never returns a response, container stays `Up`, no `OOMKilled`, no restart count. Recovered only with a CT reboot. Twice, ~12h apart.

## The observation

**Memory consumption tracks the container's memory allocation roughly 1:1.**

- CT allocated 2 GB -> Chaptarr's consumption grew to fill ~2 GB.
- Raised the CT to 6 GB -> consumption grew again, this time to ~6 GB.
- Swap usage scaled along with it in both cases.

The host is not under pressure in either case; there is plenty of free RAM and the LXC limit is the thing being hit. So the runtime is being told, in effect, "there is this much memory available," and it grows into all of it.

I suspect this is the mechanism you flagged at the end:

> The runtimeconfig also has no `System.GC.Server` entry, so an uncapped container sizes its heap budget against total host RAM rather than a cgroup limit. That on its own could explain the growth without anything being retained at all, in which case it is a docs fix rather than a bug.

Relevant detail specific to Proxmox unprivileged LXCs: these generally do **not** get a cgroup memory limit unless lxcfs is enabled. `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max` inside the CT prints `max`, so there is no container limit for the runtime to detect, and the heap budget is sized against what it can see. That would account for the 1:1 tracking, and it's consistent with `mem_limit:` in compose being the fix that works, since that is what actually creates a limit the runtime respects.

So I lean toward your "docs fix" reading rather than a retention bug. Adding a cgroup limit is what changes the behaviour, and bumping host/LXC RAM does the opposite of what you'd want here.

## On the `cache_size` question

I could not answer your actual question either — whether a connection returned to the pool keeps the raised ceiling. I don't have a way to inspect connection state in the running container. But the arithmetic is worth recording, since it lines up suspiciously well with the numbers people are seeing:

```csharp
conn.Execute("PRAGMA temp_store = MEMORY", transaction: tran);
conn.Execute("PRAGMA cache_size = -64000", transaction: tran);
```

`cache_size = -64000` is 62.5 MiB per connection, `ConnectionStringFactory` sets `Pooling = true`, and Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's default max pool size is 100. If that state does persist across pooled returns, the ceiling available to a library-scan workload is on the order of 6.25 GiB of page cache before the GC has any reason to collect — which is the right order of magnitude for the 8.2 GiB and 20 GiB figures in this issue and #290.

The `finally` restores `synchronous` but not `cache_size` or `temp_store`.

## Questions

1. Does the shipped image set `DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimitPercent` (or `DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimit`)? If not, is there a reason not to ship a default so an uncapped deployment still collects instead of filling whatever it can see?
2. Would restoring `cache_size` and `temp_store` in the `finally` alongside `synchronous` be safe? It looks like an oversight rather than a deliberate choice.
3. Given #12's fix and mine are both "create a real memory limit," would it be worth documenting the LXC/systemd case specifically? The Docker Desktop advice doesn't obviously extend to a container inside an LXC, where the limit people naturally reach for is the wrong layer.

For reference, the combination that actually keeps it stable for me is `mem_limit` plus a GC percent, rather than raising the LXC allocation:

```yaml
mem_limit: 4g
environment:
  - DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimitPercent=60
```

I don't have long-run numbers on that yet — it stopped the hangs within a day, but I haven't stressed it the way a fresh large scan would.

items.title: Native build artifacts omit the web UI
items.body:
### Description

The native artifacts generated by the Build Chaptarr workflow contain the published .NET application and Tools, but no `UI` directory or `index.html`. Chaptarr resolves the root UI from `<startup>/<UiFolder>/index.html`, so native packages cannot serve the web interface.

### Reproduction

1. Use successful `develop` run https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/actions/runs/31283656908.
2. Download the macOS artifact:

   ```powershell
   gh run download 31283656908 --repo Chaptarr/chaptarr --name chaptarr-osx --dir .\_temp\junior-bug-repro
   ```

3. Inspect it recursively:

   ```powershell
   Get-ChildItem .\_temp\junior-bug-repro -Recurse -Directory -Filter UI
   Get-ChildItem .\_temp\junior-bug-repro -Recurse -File -Filter index.html
   ```

### Actual behavior

The artifact contains 364 files totaling 144,563,965 bytes, but:

```text
UI_DIR_COUNT=0
INDEX_HTML_COUNT=0
```

### Expected behavior

Each native artifact should include the production frontend at `Chaptarr/UI`, as documented by the source-build instructions (`yarn build`, followed by copying `_output/UI` into the publish directory).

### Cause

`.github/workflows/build.yml` publishes the backend and updater and copies `Tools`, then uploads `./publish`. It never installs frontend dependencies, runs `yarn build`, or copies `_output/UI` into `./publish/Chaptarr/UI`. Release zips are produced directly from those artifacts.

The application expects the UI entry point at `<startup>/<UiFolder>/index.html` in `IndexHtmlMapper`.

### Environment and evidence

- Chaptarr version: `0.9.914`
- `develop` commit: `bdacfc28f1d1e83a7c5404e1a83440b6bb277b12`
- Successful Actions run: https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/actions/runs/31283656908
- Reproduced independently by downloading and inspecting the generated `chaptarr-osx` artifact

items.title: Bookshelf “Monitor Author” changes silently monitor every existing book
items.body:
### Description

Updating only **Monitor Author** from the Bookshelf also changes every existing book for the selected author to monitored.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have an author with at least one existing unmonitored audiobook or eBook.
2. Open Bookshelf and select the author.
3. Leave **Monitor Existing Books** and **Monitor New Books** at **No Change**.
4. Change only **Monitor Author** and click **Update Selected**.

### Actual behavior

The author setting changes, but all existing audiobooks and eBooks are also marked monitored.

### Expected behavior

Changing only **Monitor Author** must not modify existing book monitoring.

### Reproduction evidence

The frontend-equivalent request serializes as:

```json
{"authors":[{"id":42,"monitored":false}],"monitoringOptions":{}}
```

A disposable focused NUnit test passed this exact JSON through the production `NzbDrone.Common.Serializer.Json.Deserialize<BookshelfResource>`, `BookshelfController.UpdateAll`, and `BookMonitoredService`, with one unmonitored audiobook and one unmonitored eBook.

```text
Passed monitor_author_only_silently_monitors_every_existing_book [310 ms]
Test Run Successful.
Total tests: 2
     Passed: 2
```

The test observed:

- `MonitoringOptions.Monitor == MonitorTypes.All` after deserialization
- the requested author became unmonitored
- the audiobook's `AudiobookMonitored` value changed from `false` to `true`
- the eBook's `EbookMonitored` value changed from `false` to `true`

The focused suite was run with the repository's .NET 10 target using:

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "C:\Code\chaptarr:/repo" -w /repo mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 dotnet test _temp/junior-bug-repro-tests/JuniorBugRepro.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --logger "console;verbosity=detailed"
```

### Cause

The Bookshelf footer omits `monitor` when **Monitor Existing Books** is unchanged, but `bookshelfActions.js` always constructs `monitoringOptions: { monitor }`. JSON serialization drops the undefined member and leaves `{}`. The enum's zero value is `MonitorTypes.All`; `BookshelfController` always calls `SetBookMonitoredStatus`, and the `All` branch monitors every book.

### Impact

An author-only bulk edit can silently opt every existing book into monitoring, potentially causing unwanted wanted/search/download activity across both formats.

### Affected version

- Chaptarr `0.9.914`
- `develop` commit `bdacfc28f1d1e83a7c5404e1a83440b6bb277b12`

### Possible fix

Do not send `monitoringOptions` when **Monitor Existing Books** is unchanged, and/or make the backend reject or ignore an options object with no explicit monitor selection. Add a regression test for author-only bulk edits.

items.title: Bookshelf “Monitor New Books” is ignored and can change existing books instead
items.body:
### Description

The Bookshelf bulk-edit control **Monitor New Books** submits a value and receives a successful response, but the backend does not apply it to the author's future-monitoring settings. With **Monitor Existing Books** left at **No Change**, the same request can monitor all existing books instead.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Select an author whose future audiobook/eBook monitoring is disabled and whose existing books are unmonitored.
2. In Bookshelf, leave **Monitor Author** and **Monitor Existing Books** at **No Change**.
3. Set **Monitor New Books** to **All Books** and click **Update Selected**.
4. Inspect the author's future-monitoring flags and existing books.

### Actual behavior

The request is accepted, but `AudiobookMonitorFuture` and `EbookMonitorFuture` remain `false`. Existing books are set monitored because the request also includes an empty `monitoringOptions` object.

### Expected behavior

The chosen future-monitoring policy should be applied without changing existing-book monitoring. If this legacy global control is no longer supported by the per-media-type model, the UI/API should be replaced with explicit audiobook/eBook future controls rather than silently accepting and ignoring it.

### Reproduction evidence

A disposable focused NUnit test sent the exact frontend-shaped request through the production serializer, `BookshelfController.UpdateAll`, and `BookMonitoredService`:

```json
{"authors":[{"id":42}],"monitoringOptions":{},"monitorNewItems":"all"}
```

Initial state:

- `AudiobookMonitorFuture=false`
- `EbookMonitorFuture=false`
- one existing audiobook and one existing eBook, both unmonitored

Observed output:

```text
Passed monitor_new_books_is_ignored_and_existing_books_are_changed_instead [5 ms]
Test Run Successful.
Total tests: 2
     Passed: 2
```

The production deserializer read `MonitorNewItems == NewItemMonitorTypes.All`, but after controller execution both future flags remained `false`; both existing books changed from unmonitored to monitored.

The focused suite was run against the repository's .NET 10 target using:

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "C:\Code\chaptarr:/repo" -w /repo mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 dotnet test _temp/junior-bug-repro-tests/JuniorBugRepro.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --logger "console;verbosity=detailed"
```

### Cause

The frontend exposes and submits `monitorNewItems`, and `BookshelfResource` accepts it. In `BookshelfController`, all handling for `request.MonitorNewItems` is commented out, with no replacement mapping to `AudiobookMonitorFuture` or `EbookMonitorFuture`.

The unintended existing-book change is the separate empty-`monitoringOptions` behavior reported in #15.

### Affected version

- Chaptarr `0.9.914`
- `develop` commit `bdacfc28f1d1e83a7c5404e1a83440b6bb277b12`

### Possible fix

Map the bulk selection to the current per-media-type future flags with explicit scope, or remove/replace the nonfunctional control. Also avoid emitting an empty `monitoringOptions` object and add a controller regression test.

items.title: Book search finds indexer releases but 0 ever download - V5MatchingService rejects every candidate
items.body:
**Chaptarr version:** 0.9.911.0 (develop branch, build 2026-08-08)

**Bug:** Book search finds releases via a configured indexer, but downloads 0 of them every time. `V5MatchingService` logs `Response was null or contained no matches` for every candidate release, with no further detail.

**Reproduction:** Added 3 different books (Robert Jackson Bennett's Ana and Din Mysteries, books 1 through 3) via `POST /api/v1/book`, set `audiobookMonitored: true`, then ran `BookSearch` via `POST /api/v1/command`. Logs for all three:

```
ReleaseSearchService: Searching indexers for [Robert Jackson Bennett - The Tainted Cup]. 1 active indexers
DownloadDecisionMaker: Processing 4 releases
[Warn] V5MatchingService: [V5-MATCHING] Response was null or contained no matches   (x4, one per release)
BookSearchService: Book search completed. 0 reports downloaded.
```

Same pattern for book 2 (3 releases found, 0 downloaded) and book 3 (2 releases found, 0 downloaded), so it's not specific to one book's metadata.

Indexer is one of Chaptarr's native (non-Torznab) indexer implementations. Download client is qBittorrent. Both are configured and otherwise working (connection tests pass).

**Follow-up on a possible cause:** wondered if this was tied to a series/edition rename on one of the books, so I checked further. Books 1 (The Tainted Cup) and 2 (A Drop of Corruption) both logged a separate warning right before their searches:

```
[Warn] BookInfoProxy: [SERVER-BUG-CANDIDATE] V5 returned 2 books with provider id(s) appearing in multiple pockets: [...] for author 'Robert Jackson Bennett'
```

That's consistent with those two books having been re-cataloged or merged into the series after initial listing. But book 3 (A Trade of Blood) never logged that warning at all, and it still failed the same way (2 releases found, 0 downloaded). So the duplicate-pocket/rename issue looks real for books 1 and 2, but it isn't the root cause of the match failure, since book 3 hits the same 0-downloaded outcome with clean, non-duplicated metadata. `V5MatchingService` appears to reject valid candidates for a more general reason, not just as a side effect of the rename/duplicate-edition data.

Happy to provide full logs or config if useful.

comments.body:
Follow-up reproduction on the same build (0.9.911.0), 2026-08-10. Replacing my earlier comment with a tighter repro.

Isolated to a single book/edition: "Full Measures" by Rebecca Yarros, ebook edition (bookId 8746). Confirmed via the interactive search endpoint that a valid release exists and is approved:

    GET /api/v1/release?bookId=8746

Two hits, both `approved:true, rejected:false, downloadAllowed:true`, one marked `isPreferredChoice:true` with `autoPickReasons:["Preferred final file format for 'E-Book' profile"]`. So matching/ranking works fine for this book.

Then triggered the automated search while tailing live container logs (docker logs -f), not just the /api/v1/log table, since that table turned out to miss Info-level entries even for successful runs:

    POST /api/v1/command {"name":"BookSearch","bookIds":[8746]}

Log output for that run, in full:

    [Info] ReleaseSearchService: Searching indexers for [Rebecca Yarros - Full Measures]. 1 active indexers
    [Info] DownloadDecisionMaker: Processing 2 releases
    [Info] BookSearchService: Book search completed. 0 reports downloaded.

Two releases found and processed, then nothing. No rejection reason logged at all this time, not even a V5MatchingService warning. (V5MatchingService warnings did appear elsewhere in the same log capture, from an unrelated RssSyncService run processing 500 releases from the indexer feed, all rejected with "Response was null or contained no matches" same as the original report. So that failure mode is still present in the RSS-sync path. But it did not fire for this on-demand search's 0-download outcome, which instead has no logged reason at all.)

New finding: the audiobook edition of the same book (bookId 17868) got grabbed automatically by that RSS-sync process during the same log capture, hit a 409 conflict on qBittorrent (the torrent already existed there from a manual add I'd done minutes earlier), and Chaptarr correctly handled the conflict, treated it as already added, and imported the existing files (28 files, matching what's on disk). So the grab-to-import pipeline does work end to end via the RSS-feed matching path. The failure seems specific to the on-demand paths (interactive release search and the BookSearch command), which find and approve releases but never convert that into an actual grab, with no error logged.

Happy to capture more live-log traces on other books if that's useful.

Update: confirmed the workaround, and it's not `V5MatchingService` at all in this path (that title was based on an earlier guess before I had DEBUG logs).

With `logLevel: debug`, the real rejection chain for interactive `BookSearch` is:

```
MonitoredMediaTypeSpecification: Rejecting audiobook quality M4B/MP3 - audiobook monitoring is disabled for this author
MonitoredBookSpecification: Author is not monitored for the release's media type. Rejecting
```

It's checking the **author-level** `monitored` flag, not the book-level one. In my case the author had `monitored: false` even though the specific books were `audiobookMonitored: true` - because `POST /api/v1/book` always adds a new author unmonitored, and there's no book-level PUT that touches the author.

**Workaround:** manually toggle the author to monitored through the web UI's author page. That stuck and immediately unblocked downloads - re-tested with debug logging on 3 different books by this author, all releases went from rejected to `Release accepted` and downloaded successfully.

**The underlying bug is still present on the API side**, separate from the original rejection symptom above: `PUT /api/v1/author/{id}` with `monitored: true` (tried both the single-author endpoint and bulk `/api/v1/author/editor`) returns 200 with the field echoed back as changed, but a follow-up `GET` shows it reverted to `false`. No error, no validation message. So anyone adding books purely through the API (no manual UI step) will get silently stuck in this state with no API-only way out.

Happy to share the full debug log excerpt if useful.

Correction/refinement to my comment above, after more testing.

Turns out part of my setup was the real culprit for the "PUT is silently ignored" claim: my root folder's **"Monitor Audiobooks"** setting (the dropdown described as "How to monitor audiobooks when adding new authors") was blank/unset. Once I gave it a real value, `PUT /api/v1/author/{id}` with `monitored: true` started persisting correctly - confirmed on a completely untouched author (0 files, 0 monitored books, never touched before) as a clean test.

However, it's **one-directional**. Same clean author, immediately after confirming `true` stuck: `PUT` with `monitored: false` does not persist. The response body itself already echoes back `true` (not the `false` I sent), and a follow-up `GET` 20+ seconds later still shows `true`.

So the accurate bug description is: **you can monitor an author via the API, but you cannot un-monitor one via the API.** Not a blanket silent-ignore in both directions like I said above - my apologies for the noise, wanted to correct it since it's a meaningfully different (and probably easier to track down) bug than what I originally described.

One more update tying this together.

**Likely root cause of the "monitored: true now persists" fix, found and filed separately as #31:** my root folder was originally created via a direct `POST /api/v1/rootfolder` API call (not the UI wizard), and that endpoint doesn't require or default the audiobook/ebook "Monitor Existing" fields - so both sat completely blank since day one. Once populated, `PUT monitored: true` started working. Details and a second, unrelated real-world impact (63 pre-existing library books silently never catalogued by the folder scanner) are in #31.

**Confirmed the fix is a complete, working fix, not just a partial one:** all 3 previously-stuck books were re-searched after the author-monitored change, all grabbed, imported, and landed correctly organized in Audiobookshelf (`Author/Series/Book - Narrator/`, correct author/narrator/series metadata) within minutes. So the workaround genuinely unblocks the full pipeline end to end, not just the search/decision step.

**Still open and unexplained, isolated cleanly:** `PUT monitored: false` does not persist, even on a completely untouched author (0 files, 0 monitored books, picked specifically to rule out any file-related side effects). The PUT response itself echoes back `true` instead of the `false` that was sent, and it's still `true` 20+ seconds later on a fresh `GET`. This is a clean, easy repro if anyone wants to chase it: pick any unmonitored author, `PUT monitored: true` (works), then immediately `PUT monitored: false` on the same author (doesn't work).

Corroborating data from a different install (large library with a six-figure file count, Postgres backend, currently 0.9.929), because our logs strongly support the server-side theory for the part of this that's still open:

**The multi-pocket warning is systemic, not your setup.** We count **hundreds** of `[SERVER-BUG-CANDIDATE] ... provider id(s) appearing in multiple pockets` warnings across our catalog (thousands of authors). Examples: *Daemon* (Daniel Suarez) returned as 2 books sharing 7 identical `az:` ids across pockets; *The Boys in the Boat* returned as **3 books — two of them with byte-identical providerId sets** (`az:1101925868, az:B00SI02G7Y, gr:53919505, hc:2499301`, 10 editions each). So the V5 server is returning duplicated/inconsistently-pocketed book records at scale.

**Why that plausibly produces "0 downloaded":** each release candidate does a V5 lookup during download decision-making. When the server's record for that book is missing or its pockets are inconsistent (exactly the state a recent re-catalog/merge leaves behind), every candidate comes back `Response was null or contained no matches` and the decision-maker rejects all of them. We log thousands of those V5-null lines, heavily correlated with authors/books the server hasn't (re)served yet.

**Timing context that fits your repro window:** per the pinned message in the project Discord, there's been major server-side rework recently and the author-ingestion bot has been paused around it. We've also observed the server 202-queueing author adds ("isn't available yet on the metadata server") and long gaps where queued items don't materialize. And 0.9.928's changelog fixed a client bug where authors that *became* available weren't imported when queued - worth being on ≥0.9.928 for any retest.

Happy to pull specific log excerpts for any author/book if useful for the server-side investigation.

Retested the monitoring half of this against develop at `fb1a55b`. It still reproduces after the per-format monitoring rework. Recording the exact path here, along with why I do not think it can be fixed in isolation, because I built the fix first and then hit the blocker.

### What still reproduces

`PUT /api/v1/author/{id}` with `monitored: false` does not persist. Two payload shapes, both broken:

1. **Bare update:** `{"id": 5, "authorName": "...", "monitored": false}`, no per-format fields.
2. **GET, modify, PUT:** fetch the author, flip `monitored` to `false`, send the whole object back. This echoes `audiobookMonitored: true` alongside `monitored: false`.

Both leave the author monitored.

### Trace

1. `AuthorResource.cs:610`: `NormalizeLegacySingleFields` returns early unless `qualityProfileId`, `metadataProfileId` or `rootFolderPath` is present, so shape 1 never reaches the legacy cascade at all.
2. `AuthorResource.cs:628` and `:641`: when it does run, the cascade is `resource.AudiobookMonitored ??= resource.Monitored`. Shape 2 echoes a non-null `audiobookMonitored`, so the `??=` is a no-op.
3. `Author.cs:335`: `ApplyChanges` copies the per-format gates only when `.HasValue`, so the stored `true` survives.
4. `AuthorService.cs:650`: `UpdateAuthor` then runs `author.Monitored = author.IsMonitoredFromMediaSettings()`, recomputing the flag from the untouched gates and discarding what the client sent.

`PUT /api/v1/author/{id}/monitor/{mediaType}` works correctly and is a fine workaround.

### Why there is no patch attached

I wrote the obvious fix: cascade a genuinely changed `monitored` into the format gates the request left alone, comparing against the stored values rather than mere presence so the echo case in shape 2 is caught. Nine new tests passed, and it broke `should_not_wipe_binary_monitoring_fields_when_not_provided_on_put_update`. That test is right to fail it.

`AuthorResource.Monitored` is a non-nullable `bool` (`AuthorResource.cs:57`). A request that omits `monitored` deserializes to `false`, which is indistinguishable from one that explicitly sends `false`. Any cascade on `false` would therefore silently unmonitor both formats on every partial PUT that does not mention monitoring, which is considerably worse than the bug being fixed. The blocker is that ambiguity, not the cascade logic.

This is the same "JSON cannot distinguish omitted from explicitly set" problem as #88, from the other direction.

### Suggested enabling change

Make `AuthorResource.Monitored` a `bool?` and cascade only when `HasValue`. There is precedent in `BookEditorResource.Monitored` (`BookEditorResource.cs:8`), already `bool?` and gated on `.HasValue` at `BookEditorController.cs:33`. It is wire compatible for responses since `ToResource` always populates the field, and every read site is inside `AuthorResource.cs`, so the change is contained.

Happy to send that as a PR if you want it. It changes the request contract on one of the most widely used *arr fields, so it seemed like your call rather than mine. Closing #87, which was written against the old tri-state model and is obsolete either way.

items.title: ImportList minRefreshInterval cannot be changed via the API (PUT is silently ignored)
items.body:
Chaptarr version 0.9.911.0.

An import list's `minRefreshInterval` field (e.g. 12:00:00 on a Goodreads Bookshelves list) cannot be changed through the API. The request is accepted without any validation error, but the change never actually applies.

Steps to reproduce:

1. `GET /api/v1/importlist/{id}` shows `minRefreshInterval: "12:00:00"`.
2. `PUT /api/v1/importlist/{id}` with the full object, changing only `minRefreshInterval` to `"00:05:00"`.
3. Response is HTTP 202. The response body already shows `minRefreshInterval: "12:00:00"`, not even echoing the requested value back.
4. A follow-up `GET /api/v1/importlist/{id}` confirms the stored value is still `"12:00:00"`.

Expected: either the field updates to the requested value, or the API returns a clear validation error explaining that the field is fixed/has a minimum.

Actual: the request is silently accepted (202, no error) and the change is discarded.

Impact: there is no way via the API to lower an import list's refresh interval, or to force a fresh source re-fetch ahead of schedule. Manually triggering `POST /api/v1/command {"name":"ImportListSync"}` before the interval elapses also does not force a real fetch, it returns `"message":"No list items to process"}` and does nothing.

Happy to provide more detail if useful.

comments.body: Related: #122 makes the Goodreads list refresh interval a per-list setting, which covers the use case behind this.

Thanks, #122 covers the practical need here: being able to lower the Goodreads shelf refresh from 12h.

The API bug in this issue is separate, though. A `PUT` that changes top-level `minRefreshInterval` still returns 202 and silently discards the change, and #122 doesn't touch that path. #86 makes that `PUT` return a 400 that explains the field is read-only. I just updated its message to point at a per-list refresh setting when the list type has one. The two PRs don't conflict: the UI echoes back the `minRefreshInterval` from its last GET, so saving a new Goodreads interval passes the check. I'd suggest keeping this open until one of them lands.

items.title: RSS-sync auto-grab silently relocates files for a torrent it didn't download, even when already organized elsewhere
items.body:
Chaptarr version 0.9.911.0.

A monitored book's audiobook torrent (Full Measures by Rebecca Yarros, bookId 17868, foreignBookId hc:548728) was added directly to qBittorrent at a custom save path outside Chaptarr, using the same indexer release Chaptarr itself would have picked (tid 358907, hash 90D53FE5BBADA9AD7D418E4AFC498369266DDF5C). The file finished downloading and was organized/matched by an external tool at that custom path.

Some time later, Chaptarr's own RssSyncService independently found the same release in the indexer's RSS feed and attempted to grab it. Its POST to qBittorrent's add-torrent API returned 409 Conflict, since the torrent already existed. Log sequence:

    [Warn] HttpClient: HTTP Error - Res: HTTP/1.1 [POST] http://<qbit>/api/v2/torrents/add: 409.Conflict (8 bytes)
    Conflict
    [Info] QBittorrent: Torrent '90D53FE5BBADA9AD7D418E4AFC498369266DDF5C' already exists in qBittorrent, treating as added.
    [Info] DownloadService: Report sent to qBittorrent from indexer. Full Measures
    [Warn] ImportApprovedBooks: [BATCH-DEBUG] No files collected for batch insertion for book 'Full Measures'
    [Info] ImportApprovedBooks: [NOTIFY] Published BookImportedEvent for 'Full Measures' (BookId=17868, Files=28, NewDownload=True)

As a side effect of treating the existing torrent as its own grab, Chaptarr's import step moved the actual files on disk out of their original location and into Chaptarr's own folder-naming convention path, with no check for whether the original location was already in use by anything else. The original folder was left with just a couple of stray leftover files (a `.cue` and a cover image) that weren't part of the move, and the audio landed in a new, differently-named folder.

Expected: Chaptarr should not silently relocate files it did not itself download into its managed path, or at minimum should log a clear warning when this kind of relocation happens as a result of recognizing an "already exists" torrent.

Actual: the relocation happens silently, with no warning that a "successful" grab actually moved files that were already placed and in use elsewhere.

This is a different failure mode from #17 (that one is 0 downloads ever completing); this is the "already downloaded, but Chaptarr's own automated recognition still mutates the file layout" case.

Happy to provide more detail if useful.

items.title: POST /api/v1/rootfolder allows creating a root folder with no audiobook/ebook monitor defaults, causing silent DiscoveryWorker failures
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

`POST /api/v1/rootfolder` accepts a root folder with no audiobook AND no ebook "Monitor Existing" defaults configured (the web UI's "Monitor Audiobooks"/"Monitor Ebooks" dropdowns, exposed via API as `audiobookMonitorExisting`/`ebookMonitorExisting`). If a root folder is created without going through the UI wizard - e.g. a direct API call, which is how mine was originally set up - both fields are simply left unset/absent from the resource, and the create call succeeds with no validation error and no default applied for either media type.

This isn't just cosmetic. `AuthorLibraryService.NormalizeMonitoringConfigForMediaType` DOES validate for this elsewhere in the app - specifically inside `DiscoveryWorker` (the streaming library-folder scanner that matches pre-existing files on disk to author/book catalog entries and auto-creates the author record) - and throws:

```
AudiobookRootFolderPath: Selected root folder '<path>' does not have audiobook defaults configured
EbookRootFolderPath: Selected root folder '<path>' does not have ebook defaults configured
```

But that validation only fires in that one code path. It's silently logged as a `warn`-level entry in `/api/v1/log` (never surfaced in the UI as a health-check warning), and other write paths (e.g. `POST /api/v1/book`) don't validate for it at all - they just silently add the author unmonitored instead.

**Real-world impact (from my own instance):** I pointed Chaptarr at a large pre-existing audiobook/ebook library. During the very first library scan at startup, `DiscoveryWorker` tried to auto-create author/book records for folders it didn't recognize yet, and hit this validation error 86 times across 63 distinct books, all within the same 2-minute window at container startup (82 failures citing the missing audiobook default, 4 citing the missing ebook default). None of those 63 were retried on later scans, and all 63 are still completely un-cataloged in Chaptarr 3+ days later - the files are untouched on disk (this doesn't affect other software reading the same library), but Chaptarr has no record of them and never surfaced any indication that anything failed. I only found this by manually paging through `/api/v1/log`.

Separately, this same root-folder gap is very likely the underlying cause of an author-monitoring issue I filed as #17 - `POST /api/v1/book` adds a new author unmonitored with no validation error, and (before I set real values on both this root-folder's audiobook and ebook settings) `PUT /api/v1/author/{id}` couldn't persist `monitored: true` either. Once I filled in both root-folder defaults, the author-monitored PUT started working correctly for the `true` direction (still broken for `false` - noted separately on #17).

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a root folder via `POST /api/v1/rootfolder` without specifying `audiobook.monitorExisting`/`ebook.monitorExisting` (or the equivalent top-level fields).
2. Confirm via `GET /api/v1/rootfolder` that both fields are absent from the response (not `0`/`null` - just missing).
3. Point that root folder at an existing library with some files Chaptarr hasn't catalogued yet, and let it run a library scan (or restart the container, which triggers one at startup).
4. Check `/api/v1/log` - `DiscoveryWorker` validation failures for "does not have audiobook/ebook defaults configured", author/book never gets created, no visible error, and it's not retried on subsequent scans.

**Expected behavior**

Either: `POST /api/v1/rootfolder` should require/default these fields (both audiobook and ebook) at creation time so this state is unreachable via the API, or: a root folder missing either default should surface a visible warning/health check in the UI, since right now failures caused by it are only visible by manually paging through the log API - and once a folder fails this way during a scan, it's silently never retried.

**Environment**
Chaptarr `0.9.911.0`, Docker (`chaptarr/chaptarr:latest`).

items.title: [BUG] Readarr/Seerr book add does not preserve monitoring or automatic search
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
When adding an eBook to Chaptarr through a Readarr-compatible client (SeerrNG Bookshelf), the book is added successfully but remains unmonitored and the requested automatic search does not run.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Configure SeerrNG Bookshelf to use Chaptarr through its Readarr-compatible API.
2. Request an eBook for an author already present in Chaptarr.
3. SeerrNG submits the request with:

```
monitored: true
addOptions.searchForNewBook: true
```

4. Open the newly added book in Chaptarr.
5. The book is shown as Not Monitored, and no automatic search occurs.

The Chaptarr API reports:

```
{
  "monitored": false,
  "ebookMonitored": false,
  "addOptions": {
    "searchForNewBook": false
  },
  "mediaType": "ebook",
  "hasFiles": false
}
```

Manually changing the book to Monitored works but does not initiate a search. Manually triggering an automatic search afterward successfully completes the normal search → download → import workflow.

**Expected behavior**
A Readarr-compatible request with monitored: true and searchForNewBook: true should monitor the requested eBook and initiate an automatic search.

**Screenshots**
None required at this time. I can provide screenshots if useful.

**System Information:**
- OS: Debian 13 host / Chaptarr container reports Ubuntu 24.04
- Chaptarr Version: 0.9.911.0
- Branch: develop
- Installation Method: Docker
- Browser: Brave

**Docker Information (if applicable):**
- Docker version: 29.7.2
- Docker Compose version: 5.4.0
- Image: chaptarr/chaptarr:latest
- Database: SQLite
- Container logs: No relevant Chaptarr error was observed when the request was added; the book was added silently but remained unmonitored and was not searched.

**Additional context**
This was reproduced with an author already present in Chaptarr, which may be relevant to the affected code path.

SeerrNG was running ghcr.io/snapetech/seerrng:main.

Troubleshooting and API inspection were performed with AI assistance. I am not a developer, but wanted to provide a reproducible report.


**Logs**
No relevant Chaptarr or Docker error was produced during the failed add/search operation. 
The main evidence is the resulting Chaptarr API state shown above. 
I can provide additional Chaptarr logs if requested.

I believe this is fixed in v0.9.936 by c14abf3 and b021e8c. When the author already exists, adding a book with `searchForNewBook: true` now monitors the book and its media type on the author, and starts a search.

You're on `:latest`, which is still 0.9.911. Can you switch to `chaptarr/chaptarr:develop` and retest?

items.title: Series name/position come from stale denormalized fields (wrong language, wrong numbers, mismatched pairs)
items.body:
Chaptarr 0.9.879 · SQLite · Docker

My library is all English/German, but lots of books show a series in a language I don't own, with the wrong number:

| Book (English audiobook) | Shows | Should be |
|---|---|---|
| Dust of Dreams | `La caduta di Malazan #28` | Malazan Book of the Fallen #9 |
| Gardens of the Moon | `Das Spiel der Götter #1` | Malazan Book of the Fallen #1 |
| Cryptonomicon | `Criptonomicón #1` | — |

Two aren't even series: Wuthering Heights → `Jardín Secreto #1`, Lichtspiel → `Historical World War II & Holocaust Fiction`. 30 of 262 series strings in my library are affected.

**Third symptom, same field: the name comes from one series and the number from another.** Checked on a second author (Brandon Sanderson, 167 books / 30 series):

| Book | Shows | Cosmere pos | Stormlight pos |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Way of Kings | `The Cosmere Universe #1` | 6 | **1** ← the number is Stormlight's |
| Words of Radiance | `The Cosmere Universe #2` | 8 | **2** ← the number is Stormlight's |
| Oathbringer | `The Cosmere Universe #12` | 12 ✓ | 3 |
| Rhythm of War | `The Cosmere Universe #15` | 15 ✓ | 4 |
| Wind and Truth | `The Cosmere Universe #20` | 20 ✓ | 5 |

Also Warbreaker `The Cosmere Universe #1` (Cosmere says 5), White Sand `#1` (says 11), The Lost Metal `Mistborn, Era 2: Wax & Wayne #16` (Era 2 says 4 — 16 is its Cosmere position).

Because the number is inconsistent within one label, the same string is emitted for different works: `The Cosmere Universe #1` covers The Way of Kings, Warbreaker **and** White Sand. Same collision on `Skyward #1`, `The Reckoners #1`, `Mistborn, Era 1: Original Trilogy #1`, `The Stormlight Archive #1`.

**Why:** `BookResource.cs` (~155) reads the series from denormalized Book fields instead of the links:

```csharp
// Use SeriesName and SeriesPosition from Book model until SeriesBookLink is properly populated
var seriesTitle = !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(model.SeriesName) ? ... : null;
```

They're stamped once at add time and never re-derived. Upstream Readarr builds the same field purely from `SeriesLinks` (`Readarr.Api.V1/Books/BookResource.cs:61`), so the two never disagree there. The `SeriesLinks` fallback below the quoted block is dead in practice — across 234 books not one contained the `"; "` separator it would produce.

The correct data is already present — Erikson has `Malazan Book of the Fallen` (id 3447, 18 links), and `SeriesBookLink.IsPrimary` exists but nothing reads it.

**Can't reconcile by name either:** `gr:135117` is stored under two different titles in the same instance — the scalar says `The Cosmere Universe` (which is Goodreads' actual title for that id: goodreads.com/series/135117, Elantris #1 / Warbreaker #5 / Way of Kings #6), while `/api/v1/series?authorId=` returns the same `gr:135117` titled `The Cosmere`. So a client can't match the scalar back to the links by string as a fallback.

**No workaround:** `PUT /series/{id}` → 405 · `PUT /book` ignores `seriesTitle` · `RefreshAuthor` changed 0 of 3 · `/variants` is narrator-only. Only fix today is editing the DB by hand.

**The fields for a proper fix exist but are dead:**

| Field | Populated? | Exposed? |
|---|---|---|
| `SeriesBookLink.IsPrimary` | never set in `BookInfoProxy` | not in `SeriesBookLinkResource` |
| `Series.ParentSeriesId` | never referenced in `BookInfoProxy` | not in `SeriesResource` |
| `Series.SeriesType` (`main/spin-off/companion`) | **yes** — in `V5AuthorResponse`, written by `BookInfoProxy` | **not** in `SeriesResource` |

`SeriesType` looks like the cheapest win: the metadata server already sends it and Chaptarr already stores it, it just never leaves the database. Without those fields a client can't tell an umbrella from a real parent — Sanderson's Mistborn books each sit in three series at three different numbers (The Alloy of Law is Saga #4, Era 2 #1, Cosmere #7, all correct), and the only way to recover the hierarchy today is inferring it from set containment.

**Suggestion:** use the `SeriesBookLink` path (honour `IsPrimary`), or re-derive `SeriesName`/`SeriesPosition` on refresh so `RefreshAuthor` can repair existing rows. Exposing `SeriesType` — and populating `ParentSeriesId` / `IsPrimary` — would additionally let clients render overlapping series correctly instead of guessing.

Happy to test a patch — 368-book library, 30 reproducible cases, plus the Sanderson author above.

items.title: [BUG] Deleting an author with files unlinks BookFile rows and allows the author to be recreated
items.body:
## Summary

Deleting an author with **Delete author folder / delete files** removes the author and physical folder, but the author's book-file row can survive as an unmapped file. A background discovery/import task can then recreate the deleted author.

Observed with Chaptarr **v0.9.925.0** and author **P.N. Elrod**.

## System Information

- Host OS: Unraid 7.3.2

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have a monitored author with at least one imported ebook.
2. Delete the author and select the option to delete the author folder/files.
3. Allow the root scan / unmapped refresh / discovery process to continue.
4. Observe that the author disappears initially but is recreated later.

## Expected behavior

- The author, books, book-file database rows, ingest rows, and selected physical folder are deleted.
- No active or queued discovery task can recreate the explicitly deleted author.

## Actual behavior

- The author count decreased from 345 to 344, confirming that the author row was deleted.
- The folder was permanently deleted.
- The corresponding book-file row was unlinked and became unmapped instead of being deleted.
- Missing-file cleanup preserved the unmapped row because the folder was no longer visible.
- Roughly 24 minutes later, background discovery called `AuthorLibraryService` for P.N. Elrod and recreated the author with six books.

Relevant log sequence:

```text
2026-08-15 15:00:41.0|Info|MediaFileService|Purged 1 stale ingest queue rows under deleted author path: /ebooks/Lifeblood/P. N. Elrod - Vampire Files 02 (12841)
2026-08-15 15:00:43.7|Info|RecycleBinProvider|Recycling Bin has not been configured, deleting permanently. /ebooks/Lifeblood/P. N. Elrod - Vampire Files 02 (12841)
2026-08-15 15:01:07.7|Warn|RefreshUnmappedFilesCommandHandler|[UNMAPPED-REFRESH][FILE-NOT-VISIBLE] Leaving unmapped row unchanged for '/ebooks/Lifeblood/P. N. Elrod - Vampire Files 02 (12841)/P. N. Elrod - Vampire Files 02 - Lifeblood.epub'. A trustworthy root scan owns missing-file cleanup.
2026-08-15 15:01:14.3|Warn|DiskScanService|Skipping scan cleanup for /ebooks/Lifeblood/P. N. Elrod - Vampire Files 02 (12841) because the folder is not visible. This may be a missing mount or unavailable root folder.
2026-08-15 15:01:14.9|Info|RefreshAuthorService|Checking 344 authors for metadata changes...
2026-08-15 15:25:12.6|Info|AuthorLibraryService|[METADATA-PROFILE] No Audiobook metadata profile configured for author 'P.N. Elrod'...
2026-08-15 15:25:16.2|Info|AuthorLibraryService|ProcessBooksForAuthor: Returning 6 books...
```

The import list was not responsible; it logged `No list items to process`.

## Root cause in current `develop`

`AuthorController` correctly passes `deleteFiles` to `AuthorService.DeleteAuthor`, and `AuthorService` correctly publishes `AuthorDeletedEvent` with that value.

However, `BookService.Handle(AuthorDeletedEvent)` drops both flags:

https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d/src/NzbDrone.Core/Books/Services/BookService.cs#L1971-L1975

```csharp
public void Handle(AuthorDeletedEvent message)
{
    var books = GetBooksByAuthorId(message.Author.Id);
    DeleteMany(books);
}
```

`DeleteMany` then always publishes `BookDeletedEvent` with `deleteFiles=false` and `addImportListExclusion=false`:

https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d/src/NzbDrone.Core/Books/Services/BookService.cs#L1696-L1714

```csharp
_eventAggregator.PublishEvent(new BookDeletedEvent(book, false, false));
```

As a result, `MediaFileService` takes the unlink branch:

https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d/src/NzbDrone.Core/MediaFiles/MediaFileService.cs#L484-L491

```csharp
if (message.DeleteFiles)
{
    _mediaFileRepository.DeleteFilesByBook(message.Book.Id);
}
else
{
    _mediaFileRepository.UnlinkFilesByBook(message.Book.Id);
}
```

This produces the surviving unmapped row seen in the logs.

There also appears to be a secondary race: discovery author imports are started using background `Task.Run` work. Purging ingest queue rows does not necessarily cancel an author import already in flight, so it may still reach `AddAuthorAsync` after deletion and recreate the author.

## Suggested fix

1. Propagate `message.DeleteFiles` and `message.AddImportListExclusion` from `BookService.Handle(AuthorDeletedEvent)` into every generated `BookDeletedEvent`.
2. Add a regression test proving that deleting an author with `deleteFiles=true` deletes its `BookFile` rows rather than setting `EditionId=0`.
3. Add a test for propagation of `AddImportListExclusion`.
4. Cancel/invalidate in-flight discovery work for paths/provider IDs belonging to an explicitly deleted author, or check an author-deletion tombstone immediately before `AddAuthorAsync`.
5. Optionally purge unmapped `BookFile` rows under the deleted author paths as defense in depth.

## Source revision inspected

`develop` at `093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d`.

comments.body: #261 fixes the `deleteFiles` part: author deletes always passed `deleteFiles: false` down to the books, so the file rows were unlinked instead of deleted. It doesn't cover the second cause you raised, where discovery work that's already running can re-add the author.

items.title: [BUG] Author and book filters reuse stale memoized collection results
items.body:
## Describe the bug

Selecting **Monitored Only** in the author index filter does not update the visible author list. Unmonitored author cards remain visible and the page appears unchanged.

The built-in filter definition is correct, but the memoized author collection selector uses an inverted equality predicate.

## System Information

- Host OS: Unraid 7.3.2

## To reproduce

1. Open the author index with a mixture of monitored and unmonitored authors.
2. Open **Filter**.
3. Select **Monitored Only**.
4. Observe that unmonitored authors remain visible.

## Expected behavior

Only authors with `monitored === true` should remain visible.

## Actual behavior

The previously rendered, unfiltered collection is reused, so the visible list does not change.

## Root cause

In `createAuthorClientSideCollectionItemsSelector.js`, `hasDifferentItemsOrOrder` is passed to Reselect as an equality function:

https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d/frontend/src/Store/Selectors/createAuthorClientSideCollectionItemsSelector.js#L16-L28

```js
function authorListEqual(a, b) {
  return hasDifferentItemsOrOrder(a, b);
}

const createAuthorEqualSelector = createSelectorCreator(
  defaultMemoize,
  authorListEqual
);
```

`hasDifferentItemsOrOrder` returns `true` when the collections differ:

https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d/frontend/src/Utilities/Object/hasDifferentItemsOrOrder.js#L1-L19

Reselect interprets `true` as “the arguments are equal; reuse the cached result”. When filtering creates a different list, the selector therefore returns the stale unfiltered result.

The same inverted comparator is present in `createBookClientSideCollectionItemsSelector.js`, so book list filtering/sorting may also return stale results:

https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d/frontend/src/Store/Selectors/createBookClientSideCollectionItemsSelector.js#L22-L34

## Suggested fix

Invert the result in both selectors:

```js
function authorListEqual(a, b) {
  return !hasDifferentItemsOrOrder(a, b);
}
```

Alternatively, remove the custom memoization layer if it is not needed.

## Regression tests

- `all` → `monitored` removes unmonitored authors.
- `monitored` → `all` restores all authors.
- Sorting changes return the new item order.
- Equivalent lists reuse the cached result.
- The same scenarios for the book collection selector.

## Additional UI typo

The built-in author filter for `monitored: false` is labelled **All Only**. It likely should be **Unmonitored Only**:

https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d/frontend/src/Store/Actions/authorActions.js#L42-L51

## Source revision inspected

`develop` at `093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d`.

items.title: [BUG] Duplicate author merge repeatedly fails on unique AudnexusAuthorId
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

Automatic duplicate-author merging repeatedly fails when the source author owns an Audnexus ID that is copied to the survivor before the source row is deleted.

Observed with two Lee Child author records:

- Source: `[416][Lee Child]`
- Survivor: `[1577][Lee Child]`
- Audnexus ID: `az:B000APO0PQ`

**To Reproduce**

1. Have two local author rows resolve to the same canonical author.
2. Let the source row own an Audnexus ID that the survivor does not yet have.
3. Run bulk author sync so automatic consolidation is attempted.
4. Observe the unique-constraint exception.
5. Run later refreshes and observe the same blocked merge being attempted again.

**Actual behavior**

```text
[BULK-SYNC] Failed to merge author [416][Lee Child] into [1577][Lee Child]
Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteException: SQLite Error 19:
'UNIQUE constraint failed: Authors.AudnexusAuthorId'.

[BULK-SYNC] Failed auto-merge hc:1221318 -> hc:71527:
SQLite Error 19: 'UNIQUE constraint failed: Authors.AudnexusAuthorId'.

[BULK-SYNC] Skipping refresh for hc:1221318 -> hc:71527;
merge resolution was blocked to avoid data loss
```

The failure was recorded repeatedly on 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-15, including multiple attempts on August 15.

**Expected behavior**

The duplicate author should be merged without violating unique provider-ID constraints:

1. Reassign dependent rows to the survivor.
2. Remove or clear the provider ID from the source author.
3. Delete the duplicate source row.
4. Apply the merged provider IDs and metadata to the survivor.

The operation should complete once, and subsequent refreshes should not retry the same merge.

**Impact**

- Duplicate author rows remain in the database.
- Books and existing book files can remain associated with different local author identities.
- Library scans and searches may treat an existing book as missing.
- Every bulk refresh retries the same blocked merge and logs another exception.

**Technical analysis**

In `RefreshAuthorService.TryMergeAuthorsWithoutDataLoss`, the current sequence calls:

```csharp
MergeIntoSurvivor(target, source, canonicalId);
_authorService.UpdateAuthor(target);
```

before the transaction deletes `source`.

`MergeIntoSurvivor` copies `source.AudnexusAuthorId` to `target`. At that point the source row still owns the same value, so the unique index on `Authors.AudnexusAuthorId` rejects the target update.

The merge should transfer relationships and delete or clear the source author before saving the copied unique provider IDs on the survivor, while preserving the existing data-loss protections.

**System Information**

- Chaptarr Version: `v0.9.925.0`
- Host OS: Unraid
- Installation Method: Docker container on Unraid
- Browser: Not applicable

**Additional context**

This issue is intentionally limited to the repeated duplicate-author merge failure. The downstream import collision is tracked separately.

items.title: [BUG] Completed download remains ImportBlocked when destination file already exists
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

A completed download cannot be imported when Chaptarr's calculated destination file already exists. The transfer throws `DestinationAlreadyExistsException`, and the queue remains at **Downloaded - Manual Import Required** / `ImportBlocked`.

This can happen when the EPUB is physically present in the library but is not registered against the book in Chaptarr's database, for example after an incomplete or overlapping library scan or an author/edition identity mismatch.

**To Reproduce**

1. Have a valid, non-empty book file at Chaptarr's calculated library destination, but no registered `BookFile` for the selected book/edition.
2. Download the same book through Chaptarr.
3. Allow the download client to complete it.
4. Let completed-download handling attempt the automatic import.
5. Observe that the import tries to transfer the download onto the existing destination and fails.

Example:

```text
Downloaded - Manual Import Required

Lee Child - [Jack Reacher 06] - Without Fail (retail) (epub).epub

Import failed: Destination
/ebooks/Lee Child/Without Fail/Lee Child - Without Fail.epub
already exists.
```

Relevant log entry:

```text
2026-08-15 16:48:57.1|Error|ImportApprovedBooks|[CLEAN-IMPORT] Failed to import file:
Lee Child - [Jack Reacher 06] - Without Fail (retail) (epub).epub

NzbDrone.Common.Disk.DestinationAlreadyExistsException:
Destination /ebooks/Lee Child/Without Fail/Lee Child - Without Fail.epub already exists.
```

The completed download is subsequently tracked as:

```text
ClientState=Completed ChaptarrStage=ImportBlocked
```

The same behavior was observed for five existing Lee Child titles in the same import run: *No Middle Name*, *The Enemy*, *In Too Deep*, *Without Fail*, and *Better Off Dead*.

**Actual behavior**

- The existing library file is preserved, which is safe.
- The completed download remains blocked indefinitely.
- The existing file is not registered against the matched book/edition.
- The book may continue to appear missing and may be downloaded again.
- The user must manually resolve the queue item.

**Expected behavior**

There should be an opt-in Media Management setting for this collision case, for example **Keep existing library file on import conflict**.

When enabled, and only when all safety checks pass, Chaptarr should:

1. Keep the existing destination file without moving, copying, replacing, or deleting it.
2. Register that destination as the book's file and associate it with the matched edition.
3. Record the completed download as successfully imported so completed-download handling can finish normally.
4. Leave cleanup of the duplicate download to the configured download-client cleanup behavior.

The adoption path should refuse the operation when:

- the existing destination is empty or cannot be inspected;
- it is already tracked to another edition;
- the import is a normal upgrade/replacement with an existing registered file;
- the source is a generated conversion;
- the calculated destination is the same as the source.

The setting should default to disabled.

**Related prevention**

A search should not run concurrently with an initial library scan when doing so can make already-present files appear missing. Search commands that depend on current library state should wait for disk/library work to finish before release selection.

**System Information**

- Chaptarr Version: `v0.9.925.0`
- Host OS: Unraid
- Installation Method: Docker container on Unraid
- Download client: SABnzbd

**Related issue**

- #49 tracks the separate duplicate-author merge failure involving `Authors.AudnexusAuthorId`. That identity problem can contribute to files being unregistered or associated with a different local author record, but import collision handling should be robust independently.

comments.body: #238 tracks keeping and registering an identical existing file, which is what this asks for. #216 only changes the failure from an exception into a rejection with a clear reason.

items.title: [BUG] Author progress bar counts monitored future releases as missing
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

The author poster/overview progress bar stays red when every currently released, monitored book has a file and the only monitored book without a file is a future release.

Example from the eBook view for J.B. Turner on 2026-08-16:

- *Hard Road* — released 2013 — EPUB present
- *Hard Kill* — released 2016 — EPUB present
- *Hard Blood (A Jon Reznick Thriller Book 17)* — releases 2027-02-23 — no file, correctly shown as **Future Release**

The author card nevertheless renders a red progress bar at approximately 66.7%, effectively treating the future title as missing.

**To Reproduce**

1. Monitor an author and three books for one media type.
2. Ensure two already-released books have files.
3. Leave the third without a file and give it a release date in the future.
4. Open the author's book list and confirm that the third book is shown as **Future Release**.
5. Return to the author index/poster view.
6. Observe that the progress bar is red rather than complete.

**Expected behavior**

If all currently available/released monitored books have files, the author progress bar should show 100% completion. A monitored future release without a file should not make the bar red.

For this example, progress should be calculated as `2 / 2 = 100%`, not `2 / 3 = 66.7%`.

**Actual behavior**

The future release is included in the progress denominator. Because the author is monitored and progress is below 100%, the progress bar is rendered with the danger/red style.

**Root cause**

The backend and book-list UI use different availability definitions.

In `AuthorStatisticsRepository.Builder`, both `BookCount` and `TotalBookCount` are set to 1 for every monitored book based only on media type and monitoring flags. There is no `ReleaseDate` condition:

https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d/src/NzbDrone.Core/AuthorStats/AuthorStatisticsRepository.cs#L134-L156

```csharp
CASE
    WHEN "Books"."MediaType" = 0 AND "Books"."AudiobookMonitored" = true THEN 1
    WHEN "Books"."MediaType" = 1 AND "Books"."EbookMonitored" = true THEN 1
    ELSE 0
END AS "BookCount"
```

`AvailableBookCount` counts only monitored books that have files. The poster/overview progress component then calculates:

https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d/frontend/src/Author/Index/ProgressBar/AuthorIndexProgressBar.js#L22-L31

```js
const progress = bookCount > 0
  ? (availableBookCount / bookCount) * 100
  : 100;
```

For a monitored author, `getProgressBarKind` makes every value below 100% red.

The author book list uses a different rule and correctly identifies the same title as future:

https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d/frontend/src/Author/Details/BookRow.js#L95

```js
const isAvailable = !releaseDate || Date.parse(releaseDate) < new Date();
```

This semantic mismatch produces the contradictory UI: **Future Release** in the list but **missing/incomplete** on the author card.

**Suggested behavior/fix**

Calculate progress over the same eligible set for both numerator and denominator:

- monitored for the selected media type; and
- effective release date is null or not later than the current time.

Both `availableBookCount` and the corresponding denominator should use that same eligibility rule so a future book with an early file cannot produce inconsistent totals or progress above 100%.

The effective date should match the date displayed by the book resource (selected/monitored edition release date when present, otherwise the book release date). UTC handling should be consistent between SQLite, PostgreSQL, the API, and the frontend.

The table, poster, and overview author-index layouts should also use the same shared progress fields/formula. The table row currently calculates a different ratio, `bookCount / totalBookCount`, which can hide the same statistics inconsistency.

**Regression tests**

- Two released monitored books with files plus one monitored future book without a file => 100%.
- One released monitored book missing a file => below 100% and red.
- Future unmonitored books do not affect progress.
- A null release date follows the existing book-list rule and is treated as available.
- Audiobook and eBook media filters produce the same semantics.
- SQLite and PostgreSQL statistics SQL remain equivalent.
- Poster, overview, and table layouts report the same progress.

**System Information**

- Chaptarr Version: `v0.9.925.0`
- Host OS: Unraid
- Installation Method: Docker container on Unraid
- Source revision inspected: `develop` at `093b74892117c48944e1552c6dbc607ac34df88d`
