items.title: [BUG] Indexer save rejected when query-less browse can't filter by category, and forceSave doesn't override
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

Chaptarr refuses to save any Torznab indexer whose *browse* endpoint (a query with no `q=`) does not support category filtering, even when the indexer returns plenty of results for real book searches.

Adding the indexer fails with:

```
Query successful, but no results in the configured categories were returned from your indexer.
This may be an issue with the indexer or your indexer category settings.
```

The validation appears to issue a query-less browse and then require at least one returned item to fall inside the configured categories. Many public Torznab indexers (via Prowlarr) either ignore the `cat` parameter on a query-less browse, or return only the most recent N uploads site-wide — which for a busy general tracker will frequently contain zero books. The result is that a perfectly functional book indexer can never be saved.

Critically, `?forceSave=true` does **not** bypass this, so there is no way to override it from the UI or the API.

**To Reproduce**

1. Add a general-purpose public indexer to Prowlarr that advertises `<book-search available="yes" supportedParams="q" />` and category 7000.
2. In Chaptarr, Settings → Indexers → add it as Torznab with category `7000` (or sync it from Prowlarr as a Readarr application).
3. Save.
4. The save is rejected with the message above. Prowlarr logs the app-sync side as `HTTP request failed: [400:BadRequest] [POST] at [http://chaptarr:8789/api/v1/indexer?forceSave=true]`.

**Expected behavior**

A *successful* query that returns zero rows should not be treated as a configuration error. Suggestions, in rough order of preference:

1. Validate using a **keyword** book search rather than a query-less browse — that is the query shape Chaptarr actually uses in normal operation.
2. Downgrade this from a blocking error to a **warning**, so the indexer saves and the user can test it with a real search.
3. At minimum, honour `?forceSave=true` for this particular validator, as the other *arr apps do for failed indexer tests.

**Evidence**

Same indexer, same Prowlarr instance, three query shapes. Item counts are `grep -c "<item>"` on the raw Torznab XML:

| Query | Items |
|---|---|
| `t=search` (bare browse, no `cat`) | 50 |
| `t=search&cat=7000` (bare browse, filtered) | **0** |
| `t=search&q=dune&cat=7000` | **57** |
| `t=book&q=dune&cat=7000` | 57 |

The indexer's own caps advertise book search:

```xml
<search available="yes" supportedParams="q" />
<book-search available="yes" supportedParams="q" />
<category id="7000" name="Books" />
```

So the indexer is genuinely capable and genuinely returns books — it just cannot do a *category-filtered browse*, which is the only thing the validator tests. I tried every category shape available on this indexer (7000, plus its tracker-native ebook and audiobook category IDs); all return 0 on a bare browse while returning results for keyword searches.

**System Information:**
 - OS: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0), Docker Desktop
 - Chaptarr Version: 0.9.958 (also reproduced on 0.9.911)
 - Installation Method: Docker
 - Browser: n/a — reproduced via the REST API directly and via Prowlarr app sync

**Additional context**

Reproduced both ways:
- Prowlarr → Settings → Apps → Chaptarr added as a **Readarr** application (`fullSync`). Prowlarr's `ReadarrV1Proxy` gets a 400 back and no indexers sync.
- Direct `POST /api/v1/indexer?forceSave=true` with a hand-built Torznab payload. Identical 400.

Net effect: on this setup Chaptarr ends up with zero indexers and cannot grab anything, despite the underlying search pipeline working end to end.

comments.body:
Still reproduces on 0.9.911 via Prowlarr fullSync, and the same code is on `develop` as of e67374f.

I think I found why forceSave can't get past it. The category check in `HttpIndexerBase.cs:375` returns a plain `ValidationFailure`, which counts as an error. On create, `ProviderControllerBase.CreateProvider` calls `Test(definition, !forceSave)`, so forceSave only turns off `includeWarnings`. `VerifyValidationResult` then throws on `!result.IsValid` anyway.

Workaround until it's fixed, in case it helps anyone:

1. `POST /api/v1/indexer` with the Torznab payload but `enableRss`, `enableAutomaticSearch` and `enableInteractiveSearch` all `false`. Disabled indexers skip the test.
2. `PUT /api/v1/indexer/{id}?forceSave=true` with them set to `true`. `UpdateProvider` skips `Test()` entirely when forceSave is set.

If you use Prowlarr's exact name (`<Name> (Prowlarr)`) and base URL (`http://<prowlarr>/<indexerId>/`), Prowlarr adopts the indexer on its next sync. It still logs one 400 per sync, but the indexer stays enabled. That's how I got EBookBay (a book-only tracker) into Chaptarr.

+1 to the reporter's first suggestion.

items.title: [BUG] Audiobook conversion scheduler crashes reading ConversionJobs.Progress as Int64 instead of Double
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

Audiobook conversion jobs cause the detached conversion scheduler to fail in Chaptarr 0.9.958.

The `ConversionJobs.Progress` column is defined as `NUMERIC` in SQLite. Whole-number progress values such as `0` and `100` are being stored as SQLite INTEGER values.

When `ConversionJobService.RecoverExpiredLeases()` reads a queued conversion job with `Progress=0`, Dapper attempts to deserialize the value into the Chaptarr model and throws:

`System.InvalidCastException: Unable to cast object of type 'System.Int64' to type 'System.Double'.`

This causes the detached audiobook conversion scheduler to fail.

The actual `m4b-tool` / ffmpeg conversion process can still launch, so this appears to specifically affect conversion job scheduling/tracking rather than ffmpeg itself.


**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Enable audiobook MP3 → M4B conversion.
2. Import/download an audiobook containing MP3 files.
3. Allow Chaptarr to create an audiobook conversion job.
4. The conversion job is inserted into the `ConversionJobs` table with `Progress = 0`.
5. Chaptarr's detached conversion scheduler attempts to read non-completed conversion jobs.
6. The scheduler throws a `DataException` / `InvalidCastException`.
7. In the UI, conversion jobs may remain queued/running with incomplete progress information such as `Time Left: -`.
8. Restarting Chaptarr clears/restarts the visible conversion state, but the affected books are detected again and the problem recurs.


**Expected behavior**

Queued audiobook conversion jobs should be read successfully regardless of whether SQLite represents a whole-number progress value as INTEGER or REAL.

The conversion scheduler should remain running and correctly track conversion progress/completion.


**Screenshots**

I can provide screenshots of the affected audiobook conversion queue if useful.

The queue shows MP3 → M4B jobs with progress bars but `Time Left: -` while the scheduler error occurs.


**System Information:**

- OS: TrueNAS SCALE
- Chaptarr Version: 0.9.958
- TrueNAS Chaptarr App Version: 1.0.3
- Installation Method: Docker via TrueNAS SCALE Apps
- Docker Image: `chaptarr/chaptarr:0.9.958`
- Browser: Chromium-based browser


**Docker Information (if applicable):**

- Container name: `ix-chaptarr-chaptarr-1`
- Container user/group: `568:568`
- Docker version: Managed by TrueNAS SCALE
- Docker Compose version: Managed by TrueNAS SCALE Apps / not manually deployed with Docker Compose

Relevant mounts:

```text
/downloads   -> TrueNAS app download storage
/config      -> /mnt/plexssd/chaptarr/config
/Audiobooks  -> /mnt/pool/audiobooks
/Ebooks      -> /mnt/pool/ebooks

Write access was tested successfully from inside the Chaptarr container for:

/Audiobooks   SUCCESS
/Ebooks       SUCCESS
/downloads    SUCCESS

The actual conversion process also starts successfully. While the issue was occurring, the container showed both:

php /usr/local/bin/m4b-tool merge ...

and:

ffmpeg ... -threads 1 ...

running.

Additional context

I inspected the SQLite ConversionJobs table.

Schema:

cid  name               type
---  -----------------  -------
0    Id                 INTEGER
1    DownloadId         TEXT
2    Status             INTEGER
3    RequestJson        TEXT
4    WorkRoot           TEXT
5    WorkFolder         TEXT

16   HeartbeatAt        DATETIME
17   CompletedAt        DATETIME

I then queried the SQLite storage type of the Progress column:

SELECT
    Id,
    Status,
    Progress,
    typeof(Progress) AS ProgressType,
    AttemptCount
FROM ConversionJobs
ORDER BY Id;

Result:

Id  Status  Progress  ProgressType  AttemptCount
--  ------  --------  ------------  ------------
2   3       100       integer       1
3   3       100       integer       1

8   0       0         integer       0

So SQLite is returning whole-number Progress values as Int64.

This does not appear to be a CPU, RAM, ffmpeg, or filesystem permissions problem.

Logs

Relevant Chaptarr log:

2026-09-12 19:58:32.8|Error|ConversionJobService|Detached audiobook conversion scheduler failed

items.title: [BUG] Failed Usenet releases can be repeatedly re-grabbed when the indexer varies publish dates
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a Usenet release fails, Chaptarr blocklists it and automatically searches for a replacement. If the indexer returns the same release title with a different published timestamp, the blocklist considers it a different release and it can be grabbed repeatedly.

**To Reproduce**

1. Enable automatic re-download of failed downloads.
2. Grab a Usenet release.
3. Let the download fail so Chaptarr blocklists it.
4. Have the indexer return the same release title with a different `PublishDate`.
5. Observe that the same named release is accepted and grabbed again.

**Expected behavior**

A failed Usenet release with the same title for the same author should be rejected even when the indexer changes its published timestamp. Differently named releases should remain eligible as replacements.

**Actual behavior**

The same named release is accepted and can be downloaded repeatedly, creating duplicate failed-download and blocklist history entries.

**System Information:**
- OS: Unraid
- Chaptarr Version: 24.04
- Installation Method: Docker

**Additional context**

The failed-release blocklist already narrows entries by author and release title. The Usenet comparison then requires matching publication metadata; this does not hold when an indexer republishes the same title with a different date.

items.title: Add a recurring "Search for Missing Books" scheduled task
items.body:
Sonarr and Radarr both ship with a built-in recurring task that automatically searches for anything currently missing/wanted (Sonarr: "Missing Episode Search"; Radarr: "Missing Movie Search"). Chaptarr doesn't seem to have an equivalent — checking `/api/v1/system/task` shows only these scheduled tasks:

- Application Update Check
- Backup
- Check Health
- Hardcover Library Sync
- Housekeeping
- Import List Sync
- Messaging Cleanup
- Process Pending Imports
- Refresh Author
- Refresh Monitored Downloads
- Refresh My Anona Mouse Account Status
- Repair Author Media Covers
- Rescan Folders
- Rss Sync

There's no "Missing Book Search" (or similar) among them. The only automatic discovery mechanism is `Rss Sync`, which is passive — it only catches a release if it happens to already be in an indexer's recent RSS feed at the moment of the sync. It doesn't actively query indexers for books that are still wanted.

The underlying capability already exists — `POST /api/v1/command` with `{"name": "MissingBookSearch"}` works fine when triggered manually via the API, and does exactly what's needed. It just isn't wired into the scheduler.

**Impact:** without this, a book that isn't found on the first search attempt (e.g. added right as it becomes available, but no indexer has it yet) just sits in "wanted" indefinitely with nothing ever retrying it, unless a user notices and manually triggers a search again. This is surprising behavior coming from Sonarr/Radarr, where retrying missing items is automatic.

**Suggested fix:** add a `MissingBookSearch`-backed scheduled task (configurable interval, matching the pattern of Sonarr's `RssSyncCommand`/`MissingEpisodeSearchCommand` pairing) to the default task list, likely with a sensible default interval (e.g. every few hours) and maybe a toggle in Settings to disable it for users on indexers with tight search-rate limits.

**Environment:** Chaptarr 0.9.911.0, Docker (`chaptarr/chaptarr:latest`), confirmed via direct API inspection on 2026-09-14.

items.title: [BUG] Import Mixed Content checkbox doesn't reflect that root folders with assigned authors can't change type
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

The "Import Mixed Content?" checkbox in the Edit Root Folder modal is always
enabled, even for a root folder that already has authors assigned. Unchecking
it and saving fails with a 500 (`BadRequest`) that never reaches the user in a
useful way, since it comes back as an unhandled API error rather than a form
validation message:

```
API Error: BadRequest: You can't split a mixed-content root folder or switch
an assigned single-type root folder. Remove it and re-add it as
audiobook-only or eBook-only.
```

This is `RootFolderController.UpdateRootFolder`'s fail-closed guard working
exactly as designed/tested (`RootFolderControllerTypeChangeFixture
.should_reject_narrowing_mixed_root_when_authors_are_assigned` and siblings) —
I don't think the guard itself is wrong given the history of author-path bugs
in this area (#106, #112, #115, #88, #63, #28). The bug is that the **UI never
tells the user this is a one-way ratchet** until after they've already filled
out the form and clicked Save. For a root folder with hundreds of assigned
authors (a real library import, not a fresh/empty folder), the checkbox
*looks* editable but every attempted narrow/flip is guaranteed to be rejected
server-side.

**To Reproduce**

1. Add a root folder as Mixed (or end up with one from an import that treated
   it as mixed even though only one media type is actually present on disk).
2. Let it accumulate assigned authors (any author whose `EbookRootFolderPath`
   or `AudiobookRootFolderPath` matches the folder's path).
3. Settings → Media Management → edit that root folder → uncheck "Import
   Mixed Content?" → Save.
4. Get a generic "An error occurred while saving the root folder" banner, with
   the real reason only visible in the browser's network tab.

**Expected behavior**

The checkbox should be disabled (with explanatory help text, e.g. "This root
folder already has authors assigned — remove it and re-add it as
audiobook-only or eBook-only to change its type") whenever the folder has any
assigned authors, so the constraint is visible before the user does the work
of filling out the form.

**Suggested fix**

`RootFolderResource` doesn't currently expose whether the folder has any
assigned authors, so the frontend has no way to know. Two-part fix:

- Backend: add a `HasAssignedAuthors` bool to `RootFolderResource`, computed
  in `RootFolderController.GetResourceById` / `GetRootFolders` the same way
  `UpdateRootFolder`'s own guard does (`author.AudiobookRootFolderPath
  .PathEquals(path) || author.EbookRootFolderPath.PathEquals(path)` across
  `_authorService.GetAllAuthors(bypassCache: true)`), threaded through the
  existing `ToResource(...)` overloads in `RootFolderResourceMapper`.
- Frontend: in `EditRootFolderModalContent.js`, disable the "Import Mixed
  Content?" `FormInputGroup` (and swap in a new help text key) when
  `item.hasAssignedAuthors.value` is true, mirroring how `isFolderTypeFixed()`
  already hides the control entirely for the fixed-type-on-create case.

I don't have a working `dotnet`/frontend build environment to hand right now
to turn this into a tested PR, so filing with the exact root cause and
proposed approach instead — happy to have someone else pick it up, or I can
take a pass at the PR later if it's still open.

**System Information:**
- Chaptarr Version: 0.9.958 (also present in 0.9.911.0)
- Installation Method: Docker Compose (`mirror.gcr.io/chaptarr/chaptarr:develop`)

items.title: Notifications: OnUpgrade never enables a provider on its own; Discord posts empty username and gets rejected
items.body:
## Summary

Found two related bugs while setting up a Discord notification on v0.9.958.0 (develop branch): a notification configured for upgrade-only alerts silently never enables, and the Discord provider posts an empty `username` field that Discord's API rejects outright.

## Bug 1: `NotificationDefinition.Enable` never triggers on `OnUpgrade` alone

`src/NzbDrone.Core/Notifications/NotificationDefinition.cs`:

```csharp
public override bool Enable =>
    (Implementation == "AudioBookShelf") ||
    (OnGrab || OnReleaseImport || (OnReleaseImport && OnUpgrade) || OnRename || OnAuthorAdded || OnBookAdded || OnAuthorDelete || OnBookDelete || OnBookFileDelete || OnBookFileDeleteForUpgrade || OnHealthIssue || OnHealthRestored || OnDownloadFailure || OnImportFailure || OnBookRetag || OnApplicationUpdate);
```

`(OnReleaseImport && OnUpgrade)` is dead code — it can only be true when `OnReleaseImport` is already true, at which point the preceding `OnReleaseImport` clause has already short-circuited the expression to `true`. `OnUpgrade` never appears on its own anywhere in the condition, so a notification configured with only `OnUpgrade = true` (a normal pattern carried over from Sonarr/Radarr/Readarr, e.g. "only tell me about upgrades, not every import") computes `Enable = false` and is saved as disabled with no error or warning.

Repro:
1. `POST /api/v1/notification` with a Discord definition, `onUpgrade: true`, everything else `false`.
2. Response comes back with `"enable": false`.
3. `PUT` the same definition (even re-asserting `onUpgrade: true`) — still `"enable": false`.
4. The notification never fires on an upgrade despite the UI/API showing the intended trigger checked.

Expected: `OnUpgrade` alone should set `Enable = true`, matching upstream Readarr's behavior and the other independent event flags in the same expression.

## Bug 2: Discord notification always sends `username`, even when blank, and Discord rejects it

Field help text says: "The username to post as, **defaults to Discord webhook default**" — implying an empty value should omit the field. Instead the payload always includes `username`, and when it's empty Discord's webhook API returns a 400:

```
[Warn] HttpClient: HTTP Error - Res: HTTP/2.0 [POST] https://discord.com/api/webhooks/.../...: 400.BadRequest (80 bytes)
{"username": ["Must be between 1 and 80 in length.", "Username cannot be \"\""]}

[Error] DiscordProxy: Unable to post payload NzbDrone.Core.Notifications.Discord.Payloads.DiscordPayload
NzbDrone.Common.Http.HttpException: HTTP request failed: [400:BadRequest] [POST] at [https://discord.com/api/webhooks/.../...]
   at NzbDrone.Core.Notifications.Discord.DiscordProxy.SendPayload(DiscordPayload payload, DiscordSettings settings) in ./Chaptarr.Core/Notifications/Discord/DiscordProxy.cs:line 37
```

This surfaces to the API caller (and presumably the UI's test-notification button) as a generic `Unable to post payload` / `Invalid request Validation failed` error with no indication that leaving the documented-as-optional username field blank is the cause.

Repro:
1. Configure a Discord notification with a valid webhook URL and leave `username` blank (as the help text says is fine).
2. Test/save the notification.
3. Get a 400 from Discord and a confusing "Unable to post payload" validation error instead of a message actually being sent.

Expected: omit `username` from the outgoing payload entirely when the field is blank, same as upstream Readarr, so the webhook's own configured default name is used.

## Environment

- Chaptarr 0.9.958.0, `develop` branch, Docker (`mirror.gcr.io/chaptarr/chaptarr:develop`)

items.title: Rename/refresh commands can hang indefinitely: unthrottled retries of 403-blocked cover URLs exhaust the shared HTTP connection pool
items.body:
## Summary

A user-triggered "Rename Files" job covering ~1600 authors (`RenameAuthorCommand`) hung indefinitely on v0.9.958.0 (develop), stuck reporting `Organizing all files in author: <name>` with zero progress for 15+ minutes. The app itself stayed responsive (API calls returned in ~30ms, CPU/memory normal, no threads in an uninterruptible/D state), but the command made no forward progress until manually cancelled via `DELETE /api/v1/command/{id}`.

## Root cause

`MediaCoverService` has no negative-caching/backoff for cover URLs that a CDN has already rejected with `403 Forbidden`. Every call path that touches a book or author's cover (rename/organize, refresh, import, RSS sync touching the same book) re-attempts the exact same already-known-bad URL from scratch:

```csharp
// EnsureBookCovers -> EnsureMonitoredBookCover -> DownloadBookCover -> GetImageResponse
catch (HttpException e) when (e.Response?.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.Forbidden)
{
    _logger.Warn("Book cover download blocked (403 Forbidden) for {0} from URL: {1}", book, candidate.Cover.Url);
}
```

(same pattern exists for author covers a few hundred lines earlier in the same file)

In this instance, a batch of Amazon/Goodreads-hosted cover images were being rejected with 403 (likely bot/rate-limit detection on the CDN side, independent of Chaptarr). With no backoff, the retry storm across many books sharing overlapping/duplicate cover URLs (several distinct book IDs `150360`/`52096`/etc. pointed at the identical blocked `compressed.photo.goodreads.com` URL) produced dozens of near-simultaneous outbound requests to the same blocked host. `ManagedHttpDispatcher` caps outbound connections at `maxConnectionsPerServer: 12`, so once the retry rate for a single blocked host exceeded that cap, later requests queued behind it. Live diagnostics on the affected host (`/proc/<pid>/net/tcp`) confirmed multiple leaked `CLOSE_WAIT` sockets to another local *arr service on the same box at the moment of the hang, consistent with connection-pool starvation rather than a genuine deadlock — cancelling the command via the API immediately cleared the `CLOSE_WAIT` sockets and let every other queued command (`RssSync`, `ProcessMonitoredDownloads`, etc.) resume instantly.

Because none of this produces an exception the command-execution loop treats as fatal (each 403 is caught, logged, and the loop moves to the next book), the command's `status` stays `started` with no forward progress and no error surfaced to the user — it just looks hung.

## Repro

1. Have a library where multiple books/editions reference the same (or several) Amazon/Goodreads cover URLs that the CDN currently rejects with 403 (easy to hit at scale — cover URLs get reused across editions/omnibuses, and Amazon's image CDN does rate-limit non-browser clients).
2. Run "Rename Files" (`RenameAuthorCommand`) or any bulk refresh across enough authors to include several of these.
3. Watch the command's `message` field via `GET /api/v1/command/{id}` stop advancing while the logs show repeated `MediaCoverService: Book/Author cover download blocked (403 Forbidden)` for the same handful of URLs.

## Fix

Opened #<PR_NUMBER_PLACEHOLDER> — adds a simple in-memory negative cache (`ConcurrentDictionary<string, DateTime>`, 6h backoff) in `MediaCoverService.GetImageResponse`, the single chokepoint both the author-cover and book-cover download paths already funnel through. A URL that returned 403 is skipped (fast-fail, no network call) for the backoff window instead of being retried by every subsequent book/author that references it.

This doesn't fix the underlying CDN blocking (out of Chaptarr's control), but it stops one blocked URL from being able to stall unrelated bulk operations for the whole library.

## Environment

- Chaptarr 0.9.958.0, `develop` branch, Docker (`mirror.gcr.io/chaptarr/chaptarr:develop`)
- ~1600 authors, mixed ebook/audiobook library

items.title: [FEATURE] Paginate GET /api/v1/book
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

`GET /api/v1/book` always returns the entire library in one response, and `page`/`pageSize` query parameters are ignored. Scale therefore falls entirely on the client: on my library that is **~164,000 records in a ~247 MB JSON response** (~1.5 KB per record), which any client must hold in memory to parse. A straightforward `json.loads` of it peaks around 1.2 GB. Anyone with a larger library pays proportionally more, and clients that only need a few fields per book still pay for the whole payload on every call.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Honor paging on `GET /api/v1/book`: a `page`/`pageSize` (or `offset`/`limit`) pair, plus the total record count in the response so a client can tell a complete result from a truncated one. A server-side cap on page size would also be reasonable.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Incremental (streaming) JSON parsing. This is the current client-side workaround, but every client has to implement it, and it does not reduce transfer size or serialization cost.
- `authorId` filtering. Requires one request per author (~1,300 here) and does not help a client that wants the full set.
- A field selector. Would cut the payload and compose well with paging, but is a separate request.

**Additional context**

Measured against 0.9.958. `/ajax`-style paging already exists elsewhere in the ecosystem, so this is consistency rather than a new concept.

**Media Type**

Does this feature apply to:
- [ ] Audiobooks
- [ ] eBooks
- [x] Both

**Use Case**

A maintenance script that reads every book record once per run, to reconcile monitoring state against an external ownership source. It needs one full pass over the library and does not need the full record shape.

items.title: Cached<T> leaks a Task.Delay/timer per Set()/rolling-expiry touch on the same key
items.body:
## Describe the bug

`Cached<T>.ScheduleTryRemove()` (`src/NzbDrone.Common/Cache/Cached.cs`) schedules a new `Task.Delay(lifeTime).ContinueWith(...)` on every `Set()` call, and on every rolling-expiry `Find()`/`Get()`, without ever cancelling a delay already pending for that same key. On a long-lived cache that's touched more often than its lifetime, these orphaned delays are never cancelled and pile up - each is harmless in isolation, but they're real live `Timer`/`Task` objects sitting in memory and the ThreadPool queue until they individually fire.

`MediaCoverProxy.RegisterUrl()` hits this hard: it calls `_cache.Set(hash, url, TimeSpan.FromHours(24))` unconditionally on every call, and it's invoked for every cover URL in every API response that includes book/author cover art (author lists, book lists, the queue view, etc). On a library with enough authors/books that cover URLs get re-touched well within their 24h lifetime, this accumulates continuously.

## To Reproduce

Not easily reproducible in isolation without a large library - this was found on a live instance (~1,600 authors, large tracked-download queue) where the process was pegged at 200-300% CPU even with no user activity.

## Diagnosis

`dotnet-counters` showed `dotnet.timer.count` steady at ~15,180+ (should be dozens for an idle instance), with a matching `dotnet.gc.heap.total_allocated` rate of 75-250MB/s - i.e. continuous GC churn with nothing visibly happening.

A `dotnet-dump` heap snapshot (`dumpheap -stat`) showed near-identical live counts across several types, all tracing to one code path:

```
15,207  System.Threading.TimerQueueTimer
15,179  System.Threading.Tasks.Task+DelayPromise
15,179  System.Threading.Tasks.ContinueWithTaskContinuation
15,180  System.Action<System.Threading.Tasks.Task>
15,181  System.Threading.Tasks.Task+ContingentProperties
15,176  NzbDrone.Common.Cache.Cached<System.String>+<>c__DisplayClass16_0
```

`<>c__DisplayClass16_0` is the compiler-generated closure for `ScheduleTryRemove`'s lambda, confirming these are all orphaned expiry delays against the same `Cached<string>` instance (`MediaCoverProxy`'s 24h cover-url cache), none of them ever cancelled.

## Expected behavior

Re-touching an already-cached key (via `Set()` or rolling-expiry `Find()`/`Get()`) should not add another concurrent expiry timer on top of whatever's already scheduled for that key.

## Fix

Opened #156 - tracks one pending removal per key and cancels/disposes the previous one before scheduling a new one. Includes a regression test (`CachedFixture`).

## Environment

- Chaptarr `:develop`, `v0.9.958.0`
- ~1,600 authors, download-client queue in the low thousands of tracked items

comments.body: Fix in #156.

items.title: Import list "specific book" add ends up monitoring (and grabbing) the author's entire catalog within hours
items.body:
Chaptarr version 0.9.936+ (confirmed on latest `develop`, commit `7a06004`).

**Bug:** A `GoodreadsBookshelf` import list configured with `shouldMonitor:"specificBook"` correctly scopes the *initial* add to just the one book on the shelf — but roughly 60–90 minutes later, once the author's periodic metadata refresh (`RefreshAuthorService`) runs, other books by that same newly-added author silently flip to monitored and get grabbed too, even though the author's own `AudiobookMonitorNewItems`/`EbookMonitorNewItems` is correctly stored as `None`.

**Two real-world reproductions, both via `GoodreadsBookshelf` lists with `shouldMonitor:"specificBook"`, `monitorNewItems:"none"`:**

1. **2026-09-17** — a shelf added one book, "The Good Girl Effect" by Sara Cate. Within the day, 47 file-editions across 30 distinct Sara Cate titles were grabbed (her entire back-catalog). Same pattern, smaller scale, hit "I Will Break You" by Gigi Styx (1 listed → 7 titles/13 editions grabbed) from the same shelf sync.
2. **2026-09-19** — a shelf added three books: "The Halls of the Dead" (S. M. Hallow), "The Other Moctezuma Girls" (Sofia Robleda), "Muñeca" (Cynthia Gómez). Chaptarr's own Info-level log shows the initial add was correctly scoped:

```
2026-09-19 02:03:53.6|Info|ImportListSyncService|Queued author from import list for background import (author pass): Cynthia Gómez
2026-09-19 02:03:53.6|Info|ImportListSyncService|Queued author from import list for background import (author pass): S. M. Hallow
2026-09-19 02:03:53.6|Info|ImportListSyncService|Queued author from import list for background import (author pass): Sofia Robleda
2026-09-19 02:04:14.8|Info|ReleaseSearchService|Searching indexers for [Cynthia Gómez - Muñeca]. 1 active indexers
2026-09-19 02:04:19.4|Info|ReleaseSearchService|Searching indexers for [Sofia Robleda - The Other Moctezuma Girls]. 1 active indexers
2026-09-19 02:05:29.5|Info|ReleaseSearchService|Searching indexers for [S. M. Hallow - The Halls of the Dead]. 1 active indexers
```

Only the three requested titles searched — correct. Then, ~76 minutes later, the routine per-author refresh ran:

```
2026-09-19 03:20:06.3|Info|RefreshAuthorService|Author Cynthia Gómez was updated from API (...)
2026-09-19 03:20:12.0|Info|RefreshAuthorService|Author Sofia Robleda was updated from API (...)
2026-09-19 03:20:12.7|Info|RefreshAuthorService|Author S. M. Hallow was updated from API (...)
```

Ten minutes after that, searches began for four titles that were **not** on anyone's shelf:

```
2026-09-19 03:30:23.6|Info|ReleaseSearchService|Searching indexers for [Cynthia Gómez - The Nightmare Box and Other Stories]. 1 active indexers
2026-09-19 03:30:25.9|Info|ReleaseSearchService|Searching indexers for [Sofia Robleda - Daughter of Fire]. 1 active indexers
2026-09-19 03:30:51.6|Info|ReleaseSearchService|Searching indexers for [Cynthia Gómez - Split Scream Volume Two]. 1 active indexers
2026-09-19 03:30:55.0|Info|ReleaseSearchService|Searching indexers for [S. M. Hallow - How To Survive This Fairytale]. 1 active indexers
```

`GET /api/v1/book?authorId=...` afterward showed every book row for these three authors — including ones never grabbed yet — at `monitored:true`, despite `GET /api/v1/author/{id}` showing `audiobookMonitorNewItems:"none"` / `ebookMonitorNewItems:"none"` on all three (the value the import list explicitly set at add time, per `ImportListSyncService.BuildMonitoringConfigForGoodreadsImportList`, `AudiobookMonitorNewItems = importList.MonitorNewItems`).

**Suspected code path (not yet confirmed with DEBUG-level logs — this is the strongest lead from reading the source, not a certainty):**

`RefreshAuthorService.cs`, `ShouldMonitorNewBook(Book addedBook, Author entity, bool isAudiobook)` (~line 1865):

```csharp
private bool ShouldMonitorNewBook(Book addedBook, Author entity, bool isAudiobook)
{
    if (addedBook == null || entity == null || addedBook.MediaType != (isAudiobook ? BookMediaType.Audiobook : BookMediaType.Ebook))
    {
        return false;
    }

    // AddOptions remains present until the initial disk scan completes...
    if (entity.AddOptions != null)
    {
        return false;
    }

    var monitorNewItems = entity.GetMonitorNewItemsForMediaType(isAudiobook);
    return monitorNewItems.HasValue &&
           _monitorNewBookService.ShouldMonitorNewBook(addedBook, entity, monitorNewItems.Value);
}
```

used by `AddChildren` (~line 1840) when the refresh discovers book rows not yet present locally. `MonitorNewBookService.ShouldMonitorNewBook` itself correctly returns `false` for `NewItemMonitorTypes.None` — so on paper this should have kept the four extra books unmonitored. Since the observed behavior contradicts that, either:

- `entity.GetMonitorNewItemsForMediaType(isAudiobook)` isn't returning the value actually stored on the author row at the moment the refresh runs (timing/caching issue?), or
- these particular books didn't go through this `AddChildren` gate at all (e.g. a different insert path for "book exists in bibliography snapshot from initial add but wasn't grabbed yet" vs. "genuinely new to the local catalog"), or
- something between the original `MonitoringConfig` (`SpecificBook` + explicit `AudiobookBooksToMonitor`/`EbookBooksToMonitor` list, built correctly in `ImportListSyncService.BuildMonitoringConfigForGoodreadsImportList`) and the author row that actually gets persisted loses the "only these specific books" intent, and the refresh's "new item" classification for these four titles is being computed against a mode other than the author's own `MonitorNewItems`.

I don't have a DEBUG-level capture from either incident (both discovered after the fact) — flipping `logLevel` to `debug` in advance and reproducing on the next scheduled refresh would nail the exact branch. Flagging what I found in case it saves someone the initial trace.

**Impact:** For any household/shared-library use of `GoodreadsBookshelf` with `shouldMonitor:"specificBook"` (the documented way to track one person's list without inheriting their author's whole back-catalog), one person adding a single book to their shelf silently triggers dozens of unwanted grabs about an hour later — real bandwidth/storage cost, and easy to miss since the initial add looked correctly scoped.

**Workaround used:** manually unmonitor the affected authors and the individually-created stray book rows (`PUT /api/v1/book/monitor {bookIds, monitored:false}` — reliable; `PUT /api/v1/author/{id} monitored:false` is not, see #17), then delete the wrongly-grabbed torrents/files once past the tracker's Hit & Run grace period.

comments.body:
Correcting my own earlier hypothesis in this issue — spent several hours today with DEBUG-level logging and two clean, controlled live reproductions, and the `RefreshAuthorService.ShouldMonitorNewBook` theory I originally proposed is **wrong**. Documenting what's actually confirmed vs. still open, in case it saves someone time.

**Ruled out: `RefreshAuthorService` / the later author-refresh cascade.** Checked the `added` timestamp on the extra (wrongly-monitored) book rows from the real 2026-09-19 incident directly via the API — they were created at the exact same second as the correctly-monitored book, during the original import-list add, not later during any refresh:
```
46757 The Nightmare Box and Other Stories | added= 2026-09-19T06:04:05Z
46810 The Halls of the Dead (correct)      | added≈ 2026-09-19T06:04:0xZ
46811 How To Survive This Fairytale        | added= 2026-09-19T06:04:07Z
```
So whatever's wrong happens during the initial `AuthorLibraryService.ProcessBooksForAuthor` call, not the periodic refresh I originally pointed at.

**Also ruled out (live repro, twice):** a fresh `specificBook`-scoped `GoodreadsBookshelf` add, reproduced with debug logging on, both with ebook-only and with both audiobook+ebook enabled simultaneously (matching the real list's config), against two different new-to-catalog authors (one with 3 works, one with 7 and one with 2). Both times, only the requested title ended up monitored — `ProcessBooksForAuthor`'s `hasSpecificBookMode`/`shouldMonitorThisBook`/`BookMatchesProviderId` logic worked exactly as intended.

**Also checked and ruled out:** a shared/colliding Hardcover or Goodreads provider ID between the wanted and unwanted book in the real incident (this repo has known data-quality issues in that space, e.g. #111, #142) — the two book rows have completely disjoint `hardcoverBookId`/`goodreadsWorkId` values, no overlap at all, so that's not it either.

**Still unconfirmed / open:** something about the *real* incidents' specific data or timing causes `ProcessBooksForAuthor` (or something upstream of it, e.g. how `AudiobookBooksToMonitor`/`EbookBooksToMonitor` gets populated per-author in `ImportListSyncService`'s Goodreads shelf pagination, `review/list.xml` fetch) to include or match more than the single requested book — but I could not reproduce it on demand against two fresh test authors under conditions that otherwise matched the real incidents closely. It may be specific to particular Hardcover/Goodreads catalog data shapes for the affected authors, multi-page shelf pagination timing, or something else I haven't isolated.

Not going to guess further or open a PR against an unconfirmed mechanism. If anyone hits this again, the highest-value next step is DEBUG-level logging *already on* before the next real occurrence, specifically capturing `[SPECIFIC-BOOK-TRACE]`/`[SPECIFIC-BOOK-MATCH]` lines from `AuthorLibraryService.ProcessBooksForAuthor` during the actual add — I only had that instrumentation for after-the-fact reproductions, which didn't reproduce.

Two more reproductions this week (v0.9.958, grabs landed on v0.9.965). These have a clean enough timeline to narrow things down, and they partly overturn my 9/19 correction above.

**Short version:** the extra book rows are created at add time, but they are **not** monitored at add time. They flip to monitored hours later, right after the scheduled import list sync refreshes the (now existing) author.

**Repro A, one book on a `GoodreadsBookshelf` list (`specificBook`, `monitorNewItems: none`), author with 87 books.** Times are from Chaptarr's log file:

| Time (09-25) | Event |
|---|---|
| 03:42 | List sync queues the new author. All 87 book rows are created in the same second. Only the listed book is searched. Correct. |
| 06:30 | A missing-book search runs across the library (47 searches, including full-catalog searches for another affected author). For this author it searches **only the listed book**, so the other 86 rows were not monitored yet. |
| 15:46 | Scheduled import list sync of the same shelf: `Existing authors: 47, Authors queued: 1, Books monitored: 62`. It then runs `RefreshAuthorService` on each existing author in turn. |
| 15:50 | `RefreshAuthorService: Author <author> was updated from API` |
| 16:00 | Searches start for the author's **entire catalog**. All 87 rows are now monitored, while `audiobookMonitorNewItems`/`ebookMonitorNewItems` are still `none`. |

**Repro B, a different list, author with 46 books.** Same shape: added 09-24 02:54 with only the listed book searched, only that book searched again at 06:30, author refreshed 15:06, then a container restart. At the next missing search (09-25 02:44), the whole catalog was searched.

**What this means for the earlier analysis:**
- My 9/19 comment ruled out the refresh because the extra rows' `added` timestamps matched the original add. That is true here too, but a row existing is not the same as a row being monitored. In both cases the monitored flag changed later, not at insert.
- So the flip happens on the second, recurring pass: the import list sync's existing-author handling (the `Books monitored: N` step), or the `RefreshAuthorService` run it triggers for existing rows. It does not happen in `AddChildren`/`ShouldMonitorNewBook`, since no new rows are created.
- It would also explain why my controlled repros on 9/19 came back clean: I checked right after the add, before the next scheduled list sync.

**Impact:** once the [indexer] grab guard (#193) was fixed in v0.9.965, 37 unwanted titles were grabbed within about 10 minutes. I cleared 74 more pending grabs by hand before the next RSS sync. On a ratio tracker, every one of those is a seeding obligation before it can be deleted. With one household shelf sync every 12h, any user of `specificBook` lists will eventually pull in whole catalogs without noticing.

**Workaround:** `PUT /api/v1/book/monitor {bookIds, monitored:false}` after each new author appears (reliable). Checking again after the next list sync is required, since the flip happens there.

I'll turn on DEBUG before the next list sync that adds a new author and post the exact trace of which step sets `monitored=true`.

Same bug reported with a Hardcover list in #270 (0.9.965, by @foinse), with an on-demand repro:

1. Hardcover "Want to Read" list with Initial Book Monitoring = Specific Book and **Search for New Items = on**.
2. Add a book by an author not yet in Chaptarr and run the list. Only that book is monitored and searched (correct).
3. Run "Refresh & Scan" on the author. Every book flips to monitored and gets searched.

"Search for New Items" may be the condition here. @jbob06, was it turned on for the Goodreads lists in your reproductions?

Turn off Automatic Search while testing, or it will grab the whole catalog.

items.title: [BUG] Bulk-enabling Sync Monitored Audio/eBooks silently skips authors missing one root folder, with no way to see which or fix it
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

The bulk Author Editor's "Sync Monitored Audio/eBooks" action (`SyncMonitoredAcrossFormats`)
silently skips any author who doesn't already have *both* an audiobook root
folder and an ebook root folder set (`AuthorEditorController.SaveAll` ->
`HasSyncMonitoredAcrossFormatsEligibility` / `HasCompatibleRootFolder`).

On a library that grew by importing audiobooks and ebooks separately (e.g.
two separate root-folder scans, or a bulk import that only matched one
media type per author), a large fraction of authors end up with only one of
the two root folder paths populated - not because the user did anything
wrong, just because that's how they were first added to the library.

When you bulk-enable sync across a large author selection, the only
feedback is an aggregate count in a response header, shown verbatim as a
banner in the UI:

> Sync was enabled for 782 author(s). 1036 author(s) were skipped because
> both audiobook and ebook root folders are required.

There's no way to see *which* authors were skipped, and no guidance on how
to fix it. The actual fix (bulk-setting both root folder paths via the same
`/api/v1/author/editor` endpoint with `moveFiles: false`, which is metadata
-only and doesn't touch any files) works, but it's not exposed anywhere in
the UI - the only way to find it is to read the controller source or call
the API directly.

**To Reproduce**

1. Have a library where a meaningful number of authors only have one of
   `AudiobookRootFolderPath` / `EbookRootFolderPath` set (common after
   importing audiobooks and ebooks as separate scans/passes).
2. Go to Authors -> select many/all authors -> Author Editor -> set "Sync
   Monitored Audio/eBooks" to Enabled -> Save.
3. Observe the warning banner reports only an aggregate skipped count, with
   no indication of which authors or what to do next.

**Expected behavior**

At minimum, the warning message should say *what to do* (set both root
folders for the skipped authors), not just report a count. Ideally the
response would include the skipped author IDs so the UI could offer a
direct fix (e.g. "N authors are missing a root folder for one format -
assign the default root folder for that format?") when there's exactly one
registered root folder of the missing `FolderType`, since that's the common
case and requires no per-author decision.

Repro numbers from a real instance: 1819 authors total, 1036 skipped (321
missing only the audiobook root folder, 716 missing only the ebook root
folder, 0 missing both).

**System Information**
- Installation Method: Docker (`mirror.gcr.io/chaptarr/chaptarr:develop`)
- Relevant source: `src/Chaptarr.Api.V1/Author/AuthorEditorController.cs`
  (`HasSyncMonitoredAcrossFormatsEligibility`, `HasCompatibleRootFolder`),
  warning surfaced via `X-Chaptarr-Warning` header and rendered in
  `frontend/src/Author/Index/AuthorIndex.js` / read in
  `frontend/src/Store/Actions/authorIndexActions.js`.

**Additional context**

Happy to submit a small PR that improves the warning message to at least
name the fix (set both root folders, then retry). The bigger UX
improvement - auto-offering to assign the single registered root folder of
the missing type - changes author data as a side effect of a checkbox and
probably deserves discussion before landing.

items.title: [PERF] RefreshAuthor runs per-book Authors/Editions queries (N+1); ~1.3M statements in 204 s on a large library
items.body:
## Summary

The scheduled `RefreshAuthor` command issues several queries **per book** where a single query per author would do. On a large library the refresh is bound by chaptarr-side CPU and round-trips, not by the database: Postgres spent ~20 s executing queries in a 204 s window (~10% of wall time) while three .NET threads sat at 30-40% CPU.

## Environment
- Chaptarr 0.9.958.0 (`chaptarr/chaptarr:develop`), Docker
- PostgreSQL backend (PG 18), ~850 authors, a very large library (tens of thousands of books; largest authors have 3,000-10,000 book rows each)
- Measured with `pg_stat_statements` (reset, then sampled for 204 s while the scheduled `RefreshAuthor` command was running)

## Observed (204 s window, refresh at authors 41-53 of 850)

| Calls | Avg | Rows | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|
| 254,056 | 0.01 ms | 254,056 | `SELECT "Authors".* FROM "Authors" JOIN "Books" ON ... WHERE "Books"."Id" = $1` |
| 233,131 | 0.01 ms | 428,252 | `SELECT "Editions".* FROM "Editions" WHERE "BookId" = $1` |
| 2,328 | 0.50 ms | 498,518 | `SELECT "Books".* FROM "Books" WHERE "AuthorId" = $1` (~214 books per call) |

Total 1.3M statements in the window (~6,400/s). Each is trivial in the database; the cost is the per-book round-trip and entity materialization on the app side. Per-author time scales with catalogue size: small authors take 10-20 s, authors with large catalogues 1-2 minutes.

The author is already known inside the refresh loop, so looking it up again once per book (254k calls) looks unnecessary.

## Suggested changes

1. Load editions for all of an author's books in one query (`WHERE "BookId" = ANY(@ids)`) instead of one per book.
2. Reuse the author already in hand rather than re-fetching it via the book.
3. If the metadata provider returns an unchanged ETag, skip the reconcile entirely (the log already reports "was updated from API (ETag: ...)" but the full pass appears to run regardless; I have not verified this).

## Not caused by

Postgres tuning: `random_page_cost` and `jit` were already adjusted, and the statements above are index lookups at ~0.01 ms.

items.title: [PERF] Postgres receives DISCARD ALL after nearly every query (646k of 1.3M statements)
items.body:
## Summary

During a normal workload Postgres receives a `DISCARD ALL` after essentially every query. In a 204 s sample it was the most frequently executed statement by a wide margin: **645,831** `DISCARD ALL` calls against 1.3M statements total.

## Environment
- Chaptarr 0.9.958.0 (`chaptarr/chaptarr:develop`), Docker
- PostgreSQL backend (PG 18), ~850 authors, a very large library (tens of thousands of books; largest authors have 3,000-10,000 book rows each)
- Measured with `pg_stat_statements` (reset, then sampled for 204 s while the scheduled `RefreshAuthor` command was running)

## Why it matters

`DISCARD ALL` is what Npgsql sends to reset a connection when it is returned to the pool. It adds a round-trip per pooled-connection return, which multiplies the cost of chatty code paths such as the per-book queries during author refresh.

## Suggested change

Check the Npgsql connection string chaptarr builds. If the reset on return is not needed (no session state is changed by the app), `No Reset On Close=true` avoids it. If it is needed, it may be worth confirming the connection is not being opened and closed per statement in hot loops.

I have not tested whether `No Reset On Close` changes behavior or timing here; this is based on the statement counts alone. I could not find whether chaptarr exposes a way to pass extra connection-string options.

comments.body:
Correction to the description above after measuring further (longer window, 1,133 s):

- `DISCARD ALL` ran 3.39M times but cost only ~15.9 s of server time in total (~0.005 ms each), about 14% of database execution time and ~1.4% of wall time. It is very frequent but cheap, so it is not a meaningful contributor to the slow author refresh. The N+1 pattern in #163 is.
- I said it adds "a round-trip per pooled-connection return". As I understand Npgsql, the reset is sent together with the next command rather than as a separate round trip, so that claim was probably wrong.
- Chaptarr does not expose a way to pass extra connection-string options (only host/port/user/password/database names), so I could not test `No Reset On Close` on my setup. Any effect is unmeasured.
- It is a PostgreSQL-only Npgsql keyword. If it were ever added it would need to be applied only in the Postgres connection-string builder, since SQLite providers reject unknown keywords. It would also stop session state (SET, temp tables, advisory locks, etc.) being cleared on return to the pool.

Leaving this open as low priority in case maintainers want it; it may be reasonable to close.

items.title: [PERF] ConversionJobs looked up once per download per pass (100k queries in 204 s)
items.body:
## Summary

`SELECT "ConversionJobs".* FROM "ConversionJobs" WHERE "DownloadId" = $1` ran **100,844** times in a 204 s window while `ProcessMonitoredDownloads` was running against a large queue (hundreds of items in the download queue and a large set of monitored torrents).

## Environment
- Chaptarr 0.9.958.0 (`chaptarr/chaptarr:develop`), Docker
- PostgreSQL backend (PG 18), ~850 authors, a very large library (tens of thousands of books; largest authors have 3,000-10,000 book rows each)
- Measured with `pg_stat_statements` (reset, then sampled for 204 s while the scheduled `RefreshAuthor` command was running)

## Detail

Avg 0.00 ms per call, 2,163 rows returned in total, so the lookup is nearly always empty. The cost is the volume: one query per download per pass. With thousands of monitored torrents this is a large share of the round-trips.

I cannot say for certain which command issued them (`ProcessMonitoredDownloads` and `RefreshAuthor` were both running); the timing correlates with the monitored-downloads pass.

## Suggested change

Load conversion jobs for all download IDs in the current pass with one query (`WHERE "DownloadId" = ANY(@ids)`), or cache them for the duration of the pass.

comments.body: #203 replaces the per-item `ConversionJobs` lookup in `QueueService.ApplyConversionStatuses` with one query.

items.title: [BUG] Slow pages, and an out-of-memory crash, on a large library: per-row lazy loading in a few API endpoints
items.body:
While profiling the database for the SQLite index PR (#169), I found that most of the slowness on my library isn't slow SQL. It comes from a few endpoints that lazy-load related rows one book at a time. Indexes can't fix these; they need code changes. I've listed each one with what I measured and where it comes from, so they can be picked off separately.

**Library:** 925 authors, 75,493 books (75,041 audiobook), 130k editions, 12k book files, 650 MB database. The measurements come from a copy of my database, a local build of `develop` with an SQLite profiling hook (not committed), and headless Chromium driving the UI. The call stacks behind the repeated queries came from that hook.

### 1. Every full page load waits 2–4 s for `/api/v1/author`

The app shell fetches the author list on every page, and on this library it takes 1.9–4.4 s. Nearly all of that is about 5,000 small queries per request:

- `AuthorController.LinkNextPreviousBooks` → `ToAuthorIndexBookResource` → `book.ToResource()` runs for each author's next and last book (about 1,200 books). Each call lazy-loads that book's `Editions`, `Author`, `BookFiles` (for `HasFiles`) and `SeriesLinks`, one query each.
- `LinkRootFolderPath` → `FileNameBuilder.GetAuthorFolder` → `NamingConfigService.GetConfig()` runs once per author, which is 925 identical `SELECT * FROM NamingConfig` queries per request.

### 2. Book page: 20–30 s here, and an out-of-memory crash on a book with 498 files

- **`GET /api/v1/history/author?authorId=…&bookId=…&includeBook=true` takes 8.7–9.6 s on its own** (10–18 s during a page load) and returns 2.8 MB. That book has 274 history rows, one per imported file, and 273 files. `HistoryController.MapToResource` maps the same book once per history row, and each mapping lazy-loads all of that book's files (`Book.HasFiles` → `BookFiles`). That comes to 274 × 273 ≈ 75k BookFile rows materialized, each carrying its `MatchProvenance`/`AllTags` JSON.
  For a book with 500 history rows and 498 files it's about 250k rows. That ran Chaptarr out of memory (8 GB box) and it exited with `System.OutOfMemoryException` inside Dapper, logged as "Out of memory.".
  **Possible fix:** map each distinct book once per request, or don't load files when mapping a book for history.
- **`GET /api/v1/book?bookId=<titleSlug>` takes 5.6 s.** `BookController.ResolveBookRouteToken` calls `BookService.GetAllBooks()` to find the slug, which loads all 75k books (3.1 s of SQL) plus the series links for all of them.

### 3. Bookshelf (`/shelf`) takes about 2 minutes

`GET /api/v1/book?mediaType=audiobook` took 113 s. On a cold start it hadn't finished after 120 s. It maps all 75k audiobook books, with the same per-book lazy loads as in #1.

### 4. Author page: 4–6 s for big authors

`GET /api/v1/book?authorId=…` takes 4.3–6.4 s for authors with 2–5k books, and about 1 s of that is SQL. The rest is mapping, and loading whole `Editions` rows, including `Chapters` (see #6).

### 5. Smaller repeated queries

- **Root folder health check:** `RootFolderCheck` calls `RootFolderService.GetBestRootFolderPath(path)` for each author path, and each call reads the RootFolders table again. That's 925 queries per health check. The `GetBestRootFolderPath(path, allRootFolders)` overload already exists, so reading the folders once and passing them in would fix it.
- **Every startup:** `UpdateFtsCommandHandler` handles `ApplicationStartedEvent` by running `FtsMaintenanceService.RebuildAllFts()`. That loads each author and issues a no-op `UPDATE` on every Authors row to fire the FTS trigger, so it's 925 × (select + update + FTS rewrite). `INSERT INTO author_fts(author_fts) VALUES('rebuild')` would do the same in one statement.

### 6. Wide JSON columns are read by every `SELECT *`

| Table | Size | Largest columns |
|---|---:|---|
| Editions | 219 MB | `Chapters` 129 MB, `Images` 18 MB, `Links` 16 MB |
| BookFiles | 88 MB | `MatchProvenance` 55 MB, `AllTags` 29 MB |
| Books | 64 MB | `Overview` 17 MB, `Images` 11 MB |

Every lazy load and repository `Query` selects these columns, even when the caller only needs ids, titles or sizes. That is what makes #2 run out of memory. Loading `Chapters`, `MatchProvenance` and `AllTags` on demand would cut the memory and I/O of most of the paths above.

---

*Found with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) (Claude Opus 5, `claude-opus-5`, `xhigh` effort) while profiling for the index PR. I reviewed the findings before posting.*

items.title: [PERF] SaveEntity/GetSyncUpdatesForMutations re-fetches an author's whole catalogue once per book saved when SyncMonitoredAcrossFormats is on (#163)
items.body:
## Summary

Fourth contributor to #163, distinct in kind from the others (#166/#167/#168):
this one scales with **book count of a single author**, not with total
authors processed, and is gated behind `Author.SyncMonitoredAcrossFormats`.

`BookService.SaveEntity` is called once per book during a refresh
(`RefreshBookService.SaveEntity` -> `_bookService.UpdateMany(new List<Book> {
local })`, one book per call by design). Inside `UpdateMany`,
`GetSyncUpdatesForMutations` groups the (single) changed book by author, and
if `author.SyncMonitoredAcrossFormats == true`, calls
`_bookRepository.GetBooksByAuthorId(authorId)` to re-fetch **every** book
belonging to that author, in order to re-evaluate the cross-format
monitoring policy.

Because this runs once per saved book, an author with N books and this flag
enabled triggers roughly N full re-fetches of their own N-book catalogue
during a single refresh - O(N) query volume scaling with N callers, each
O(N) sized, i.e. O(N^2) row reads in the worst case where most books need
saving (e.g. the first refresh after a schema/ETag change, or `forceRefresh`).

## Observed

On a live instance (chaptarr-main, real traffic, `pg_stat_statements`
filtered to that database): while processing 3 authors -
Jeffery Deaver (377 books), Brian W. Aldiss (423 books), Nora Roberts
(1,155 books) - all three with `SyncMonitoredAcrossFormats = true`:

```
2,500 calls | 4,284.8ms total | 1.71ms avg | SELECT "Books".* FROM "Books" WHERE ("Books"."AuthorId" = $1)
```

in an 8-minute window, and the refresh was still on Nora Roberts (the
largest of the three) after 15 minutes.

Charles Dickens (10,107 books) also has `SyncMonitoredAcrossFormats = true`.
1,821 authors in this library have the flag enabled in total. Each
individual query here is cheap (~1.7ms, an indexed lookup) - the cost is
purely the repetition count, not per-query expense.

## Why I'm not attaching a fix yet

The straightforward fix (thread the author's already-known book list from
`RefreshBookService.RefreshBookInfo(List<Book> books, ...)` - which already
has the author's full local catalogue in memory - down through `SaveEntity`
so `GetSyncUpdatesForMutations` can reuse it instead of re-querying) is
correctness-sensitive: `GetSyncUpdatesForMutations` decides which sibling
book gets un/monitored to keep exactly one format monitored per work, and
there's an existing dedicated test fixture for this logic
(`RefreshAuthorServiceMonitoringFixture` and friends in
`Chaptarr.Core.Test`). A caching mistake here risks silently monitoring/
unmonitoring the wrong book rather than just being slow, which is a worse
failure mode than the current inefficiency. I'd rather this get proper
review/testing than land a hasty change on top of #166/#167/#168.

Related note: #166 and #167 already reduce the *cost* of each of these
repeated re-fetches somewhat (the books they return are cheaper to clone
now, per #167), so this is a real but partial mitigation already in place
independent of a fix for this specific issue.

comments.body: Tracked under #173 (author-refresh N+1/O(N^2) query cluster).

items.title: [PERF] Author-refresh N+1/O(N^2) query cluster (tracking issue for #166, #167, #168, #172)
items.body:
## What this is

Tracking issue for a cluster of N+1/O(N^2) query problems found in the
author-refresh path, all discovered while investigating why `RefreshAuthor`
could take hours (or never finish) on authors with very large catalogues on
a real library (~40k books, largest single author 10k+ books). Started from
#163.

## The child issues, roughly in the order they were found and fixed

- #163 - original report: blocked-download re-analysis + N+1 queue queries
  (the umbrella this cluster grew out of)
- #166 (merged/open) - `RefreshBookService.PublishEntityUpdatedEvent` did a
  full `Book+Author+Editions+BookFiles` re-fetch per changed book
- #167 (merged/open) - `BookService.CloneStoredBook` eagerly loaded `Author`
  and resolved an unused edition-level ASIN on every book save, both via
  lazy-loaded properties that fire a query on first read
- #168 (merged/open) - `RootFolders` re-fetched once per work group during
  cross-format monitoring sync instead of once per author
- #172 (merged/open) - the big one: `GetSyncUpdatesForMutations` re-fetches
  and re-clones an author's **entire** catalogue once per book saved when
  `SyncMonitoredAcrossFormats` is on, i.e. O(N^2) for an N-book author.
  Confirmed live: after #166/#167/#168 alone, Mark Twain (5,695 books, flag
  on) still pinned chaptarr at 100% CPU for 25+ minutes with Postgres
  essentially idle - the query volume had moved from the database to pure
  in-process repetition of this pattern.

## Method

Each was found by profiling a live instance with `pg_stat_statements`
(filtered to the chaptarr database specifically - the instance also hosts
other apps' databases, and an unfiltered aggregate is misleading), reading
the exact query text back to its call site in source, and verifying the
fix against an isolated copy of the production database plus, for #172,
the full existing `Chaptarr.Core.Test` suite (3,008 tests, all passing -
this one touches correctness-sensitive cross-format monitoring logic with
its own dedicated fixtures).

## Status

All four (#166-168, #172) are open as separate, independently reviewable
PRs rather than one bundle, and have been running combined on a real
instance's `RefreshAuthor` pass (10k+ book authors included) without
errors or regressions observed. Still watching that run and will report
back here if anything else turns up in the same vein.

comments.body:
Follow-up finding while watching a live 10k+ book author refresh (Charles Dickens) with #166/#167/#168 + the (not-yet-PR'd) #172 fix all applied: `BuildWorkGroups` itself accounted for ~99% of sampled CPU time in a 30s `dotnet-trace` capture, on top of everything the merged fixes already address. It's called once per book saved via `GetSyncUpdatesForMutations`, and is internally O(N^2) (pairwise `WorkIdMatcher.CrossFormatSafeMatches` over the remaining book list). Caching it per-author (same pattern as #172's DB-fetch cache) turned a 10,107-book author's refresh from "still running after 30+ minutes" into single-digit minutes for the whole 700+ author library, Dickens included.

Related, smaller finding: `ApplyInsertSyncDefaults` (the insert-time counterpart, used when many NEW books get created for an author in one pass) has the same uncached `BuildWorkGroups`/`GetBooksByAuthorId` pattern, but since it's only called once per author (not once per book), it's a single O(N^2) cost rather than the O(N^3)-ish repetition the update path had. Noticeable but far less severe - observed on Lewis Carroll (1,871 books, an unusually large number of new omnibus/collection entries created in one pass): ~6.5 minutes for that one author vs. single-digit seconds for typical authors. Not fixed yet; lower priority than the others in this cluster.
Fix for the BuildWorkGroups O(N^2) finding from the earlier comment: #174.

Follow-up measurement on a live instance (346k books): after #166/#167/#168/#174/#218 the remaining per-book full-catalogue read during author refresh was `EnsureUniqueTitleSlugs` (one `SELECT Books.* WHERE AuthorId` of ~12,000 rows per book, 3.7M rows/min), fixed in #221. Author refresh also runs on the shared 3-thread command executor (#222 makes it configurable).

items.title: [FEATURE] Metadata profile can't filter by genre (e.g. exclude comics/graphic novels) even though Genres data is already fetched and stored
items.body:
## Summary

The metadata source (Hardcover, via `BookInfoProxy`) already returns genre tags for every book, and `Book.Genres` already stores them - but nothing in the metadata profile filtering pipeline (`MetadataProfileService.FilterBooks`) ever reads that field. There's no way to exclude books by genre/format (e.g. comics, graphic novels) short of manually deleting each author one at a time after the fact.

## Evidence this is real, not speculative

Checked our own library's stored `Genres` values directly:

```
"Superman – Action Comics (2011-2016) #49" -> ["Comics", "Superman"]
"Dungeons & Dragons"                        -> ["Comics", "Dungeons and dragons", "Fantasy",
                                                 "Forgotten Realms", "Gaming", "Graphic novels",
                                                 "Graphic Novels Comics"]
"Proof, Volume 4: Julia"                    -> ["Comics", "Cryptids", "Fantasy", "Fiction",
                                                 "Graphic novels", "Horror", "Monsters"]
"Action 50th Anniversary Special"           -> ["COMIC BOOK."]
```

The data is there on every book row, from authors we ended up having to delete manually one at a time (Stan Lee, Brian Michael Bendis, Grant Morrison, Charles M. Schulz, Peter David) because there was no way to filter them out proactively at the metadata-profile level.

I read through `FilterBooks` line by line to confirm: it checks rating, release date, parts/sets, secondary series, omnibus, the free-text `Ignored` title-term list, min pages, and language - never `Genres`.

## Suggested fix (have a working patch, opening as a PR alongside this issue)

Add `IgnoredGenres` (`List<string>`) to `MetadataProfile`, matching the existing `Ignored` title-term list's shape for API/UI consistency. Filter: a book is excluded if any of its `Genres` case-insensitively matches any entry in `IgnoredGenres`. Kept as a separate list from `Ignored` rather than overloading it, since genre tags are discrete values to match exactly, not free text to pattern-match.

items.title: [BUG] Converting a book in place with an outside tool (e.g. Audiobookshelf MP3→M4B) creates a duplicate copy and leaves the original book monitored with no files
items.body:
**Title:** Converting a book in place with an outside tool (e.g. Audiobookshelf MP3→M4B) creates a duplicate copy and leaves the original book monitored with no files

### What happens

When something other than Chaptarr replaces a book's files in place — Audiobookshelf's M4B encoder is the obvious case, but any tool that swaps MP3s for a single `.m4b` in the same folder does it — a single **Rescan Folders** leaves the library in this state:

- the original book keeps its monitoring and ends up with **zero files**, so it reappears in **Wanted → Missing** and is eligible to be downloaded again;
- a **duplicate copy of the book, with its own edition**, is created and the new `.m4b` is attached to that copy.

So you end up with the book twice: one copy holding the real file, and the original still asking for a download.

### Reproduction (clean instance, 0.9.964.0 `develop`)

1. A monitored book with 4 MP3 files in `/audiobooks/H.G. Wells/The Island of Dr. Moreau - Flo Gibson/`, tracked on the monitored edition (224).
2. Outside Chaptarr, write `The Island of Dr. Moreau.m4b` into that same folder and remove the four MP3s. (This is what Audiobookshelf's encoder does: the M4B lands next to the originals and the originals are moved into ABS's metadata folder.)
3. Run **Rescan Folders** once.

Result:

```
ORIGINAL book 5 'The Island of Dr Moreau'  AudiobookMonitored=1  files: []
NEW      book 6436 slug 'the-island-of-doctor-moreau_copy_81990751'
         edition 13129 (monitored)  file 60 → .../The Island of Dr. Moreau - Flo Gibson/The Island of Dr. Moreau.m4b
Wanted → Missing: 1 record  (book 5, The Island of Dr. Moreau)
```

The copy also shows up as its own entry in the author's book list.

### Cause

Two things combine:

1. **A rescan imports before it cleans up.** `DiskScanService.Scan` runs the import orchestrator at `DiskScanService.cs:163` and only calls `CleanMediaFiles` at `:192`. So while the new `.m4b` is being placed, the `BookFile` rows for the MP3s that no longer exist are still in the database.

2. **The destination "unit key" includes the file extension.** `BookUnitDestinationService.BuildRootUnitKeyWithExtension` (`:48-59`) builds `<book root folder>|<media type>|<extension>`, deliberately, so that an MP3 copy and an M4B copy of the same book in the same folder stay separate ("ensuring different media containers (m4b vs mp3) never collapse into the same book"). `ResolveDestinationForUnit` then compares the incoming key against the keys of the book's **existing file rows** (`:144-170`) — and those stale MP3 rows produce `…|.mp3`, which doesn't match the incoming `…|.m4b`, so it clones the book and the edition:

```
[UNIT-CLONE] Created duplicate BookId=6437 EditionId=13130
  for unitKey='/audiobooks/h.g. wells/the war of the worlds - flo gibson|audiobook|.m4b'
  from canonical BookId=9 EditionId=348
```

Seconds later the MP3 rows are deleted by the cleanup pass, so the comparison that caused the clone was against files that were already gone.

Note the path that would have been correct is right there: when the canonical book has **no** files, `ResolveDestinationForUnit` reuses the canonical book and edition (`:144-151`). Confirmed by hand: once the stale MP3 rows were gone, the same `.m4b` was applied to the **original** book (edition 238, which became the monitored edition) and the book left Wanted.

### Suggested fix

In `ResolveDestinationForUnit`, ignore file rows whose path no longer exists on disk when deciding whether this is a new "copy":

```csharp
var existingFiles = (_mediaFileService.GetFilesByBook(canonicalBook.Id) ?? new List<BookFile>())
    .Where(f => _diskProvider.FileExists(f.Path))   // rows for files already gone are not another copy
    .ToList();
```

(`BookUnitDestinationService` would need `IDiskProvider` injected; it doesn't take one today.) That is one `stat` per file of that one book, and it leaves the intended behaviour (a real second copy sitting next to the first) untouched. Cleaning up missing files before the import pass instead would also work, but the cleanup deliberately waits for a complete scan list, so filtering at the decision looks like the smaller change.

### Second, related issue: "Ignore Deleted Books" never unmonitors anything

Media Management → **Ignore Deleted Books** says "Books deleted from disk are automatically unmonitored in Chaptarr". Nothing implements that. The setting's only reader is `DeletedBookFileSpecification` (`DecisionEngine/Specifications/RssSync/DeletedBookFileSpecification.cs:35`), which rejects RSS releases *while* the database still has rows pointing at files that are missing from disk — and its own comment says the book "will be unmonitored on next diskscan", which no code does. After a rescan those rows are deleted, so the guard stops applying too, and the book is simply missing and grabbable. (Upstream Readarr has the same gap, so this is inherited rather than new.)

Either implementing it (unmonitor on `DeleteMediaFileReason.MissingFromDisk` when the setting is on) or changing the help text would avoid the surprise.

### Workaround for anyone hitting this now

1. Delete the duplicate copy in Chaptarr, choosing **keep files**.
2. Restart Chaptarr  — the destination cache still points at the deleted copy, and without a restart the retry in step 3 fails with `APPLY_EXCEPTION`.
3. Unmapped Files → select the `.m4b` → retry the match. It then attaches to the original book, which leaves Wanted.

A plain rescan in step 3 is not enough: the file already has a (now unmapped) row, so the scan skips it.

---

*Created and tested in the wild then recreated using Claud Code to find the deeper problem and possible solution  also to give a clean write up of the problem. (Claude Opus 5, `claude-opus-5`, `xhigh` effort), reproduced six times from a clean library in Docker.  Four times in my test lab and 2 times in claude code

items.title: Goodreads eBook import skips books for existing audiobook-only authors
items.body:
### Reproduction

1. Start with a fresh database.
2. Import an audiobook for an author, leaving that author with only audiobook profiles and a root folder configured.
3. Add one of the author books to a Goodreads eBook shelf.
4. Refresh a Goodreads eBook import list configured to monitor and search specific books.

### Actual

The list fetch succeeds, but Chaptarr does not initialize the eBook side of the existing author. The requested book is skipped:

> Import list Goodreads eBooks: book Red Rising by Pierce Brown was not found locally after ensuring author exists; it may have been filtered out or the media type is disabled

Pierce Brown remains audiobook-only: EbookQualityProfileId, EbookMetadataProfileId, and EbookRootFolderPath are null, even though the selected eBook root folder has valid defaults. No Red Rising eBook row or search is created.

### Expected

A Goodreads eBook request should initialize the missing eBook side of an existing audiobook-only author using the import-list or root-folder defaults, import the eBook catalog, then monitor and search the requested book.

Reproduced on a fresh database with 0.9.911.0. This is not caused by legacy database state, duplicate audiobook files, or a Goodreads/Hardcover provider-ID mismatch.
