A `PUT /api/v1/author` that omits the root folder fields still clears them (#88, fix in #97), which puts an author back in this state. #242 tracks fixing existing authors.

items.title: Unsatisfied-slot guard blocks all grabs from the native [indexer]: account status refresh fails with "did not include a valid unsatisfied-torrent summary"
items.body:
**Version:** v0.9.958.0 (`chaptarr/chaptarr:develop`, revision fb1a55b2)

Indexer name redacted as `[indexer]`. It's the native private book tracker indexer, the only one with the "Protect Unsatisfied Slots" setting.

**What happens**

Since 2026-09-23 around 15:53 UTC, every release from [indexer] is rejected with:

```
[indexer] safety pause: the unsatisfied-slot status is unavailable or stale; test the indexer and try again
```

Queue items sit in `delay` indefinitely and nothing is grabbed from that indexer, for both automatic and interactive searches.

**Cause (from debug logs)**

The account status refresh throws on every attempt:

```
System.InvalidOperationException: [indexer] user data response did not include a valid unsatisfied-torrent summary
   at NzbDrone.Core.Indexers.[Indexer].[Indexer].RefreshAccountStatus() in ./Chaptarr.Core/Indexers/[Indexer]/[Indexer].cs:line 263
   at NzbDrone.Core.Indexers.[Indexer].[Indexer].TestConnection() in ./Chaptarr.Core/Indexers/[Indexer]/[Indexer].cs:line 192
```

The tracker's user-data response for the `snatch_summary` request still returns `classname` (the session is valid) but the `unsat` and/or `created` fields the parser requires are no longer present or valid. The last successful refresh persisted in the indexer settings is `unsatisfiedStatusRefreshedUtc: 2026-09-23T15:53:52Z`. Once `MaximumStatusAge` (2h) passed, `HasFreshStatus` in the unsatisfied-slot guard returns false and every release from that indexer is temporarily rejected.

**Why it was hard to spot**

1. The account status service logs refresh failures at Debug only, so at the default Info level nothing indicates a problem.
2. The indexer **Test** catches the same exception and still reports success, showing the last persisted (stale) values, e.g. `VIP Member - Class: VIP; unsatisfied torrents: 8/150`. The rejection message says to test the indexer, the test passes, and grabs stay blocked.
3. Restarting the container, re-saving the indexer, and running the account status refresh command all hit the same exception.

**Suggestions**

- Update the parser for the tracker's current user-data response (possibly a tracker-side change around 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-23).
- Log refresh failures at Warn and surface them as a health check.
- Make the indexer Test fail, or at least warn, when the account status refresh fails instead of showing stale counts.

**Workaround:** disable "Protect Unsatisfied Slots" on the indexer until this is fixed.

comments.body: This should be fixed in v0.9.965 by #189 and 9b4c8dd. Can you pull the latest `chaptarr/chaptarr:develop` image and confirm?

Confirmed fixed on v0.9.965 (develop image from 2026-09-28). Account status refresh parses correctly now (`unsatisfied 19/150`), the slot guard is enabled, and grabs from the MaM indexer go through. No summary-parse errors in the last week. Closing, thanks!

items.title: Manual Import: "Will add from metadata" suggestions without an edition id can never be added for an existing author
items.body:
## Summary

For a queue item the matcher could not place, the Manual Import modal shows **"Will add from metadata: 1"** with action **"Select to Add"**. Clicking Import on such a row cannot succeed when the author already exists locally and the suggestion carries only a work id (no edition id). The import is rejected with:

> The authoritative author catalog does not currently contain suggested work 'hc:781589' for Ebook.

## Evidence

Queue item `Jonathan Strahan (ed) - Eclipse 01 - New Science Fiction and Fantasy [retail]` (`.epub`):

- `GET /api/v1/manualimport?downloadId=...` returns `suggestedForeignAuthorId: hc:162031` (already a local author), `suggestedForeignBookId: hc:781589`, **`suggestedForeignEditionId: null`**, and `rejections: []`.
- Executing exactly what the UI sends (`selectionSource: userMetadataSuggestion`, `foreignEditionId: null`) is rejected as above. I reproduced this both through the API and by clicking Import in the real UI (headless Chrome).
- Across a larger sample, about 90% of manual-import commands built from these suggestions imported nothing (816 of 920 ended as "Manually imported 0 files (1 failed/skipped)", and the command result was `successful`; see #191 for the reporting part).

## Cause (from reading `ManualImportService.Execute`)

1. `MaterializeUserSelectedEditionAsync` (which can add a missing work to an existing author) only runs when `SelectionSource == UserMetadataSuggestion` **and** `ForeignEditionId` is set.
2. Otherwise, when the work is not in the local catalog, execution "hydrates" it with `AddAuthorAsync(foreignAuthorId, config)` where `config.MonitorMode = SpecificBook`. For an author that already exists this returns the existing author unchanged, so the specific work is never added.
3. `ResolveSuggestedWorkBooks` then finds nothing and rejects.

A second, separate failure mode appears when the work *is* in the catalog: `Local grouped matching could not match '<file>' inside provider work '<work>'` (19 of the first 21 outcomes in one run). The suggestion pairs a file with a work the grouped matcher then refuses.

## Suggested directions

- Have the server pick the edition for a work-only suggestion when exactly one edition of the file's media type exists in the remote author blob, then use `MaterializeUserSelectedEditionAsync`; or make the `AddAuthorAsync` fallback actually add the specific work for an existing author.
- At minimum, make the preview honest. #197 adds a preview warning for the "work not in catalog, no edition id" case.

## Related

- #191 report why a manual import imported nothing
- #194 blank confirmation dialog with these rows (the button did nothing before it)

comments.body: #201 fixes the main case, where a work-only suggestion is never added to an existing author. It doesn't cover the second failure, where grouped matching refuses a work that's already in the catalog.

items.title: [BUG] HTTP response cache: non-unique Url index and find-then-insert race create duplicate rows
items.body:
## Problem
`HttpResponse` (cache database) has a non-unique index `IX_HttpResponse_Url`, and `CachedHttpResponseService.Get` does find-then-`Upsert` per URL. Two concurrent lookups of the same URL can both miss and both insert, so duplicate rows accumulate. Measured on a live cache: 7,846 rows for 6,261 distinct URLs, 782 URLs with duplicates (one with 47 rows).

## Impact
Before #206 every later lookup of an affected URL threw `Sequence contains more than one element` ("Invalid response received from Goodreads"). #206 makes reads tolerate duplicates and removes stale rows lazily, but new duplicates are still created.

## Suggested fix
A migration that dedupes existing rows (keep the newest per URL) and adds a unique index on `Url`, plus an upsert keyed on `Url` (or handling the unique-violation by re-reading). Found while reviewing #206.

items.title: [BUG] QueueService keeps a static _queue list that a concurrent refresh can overwrite with an older snapshot
items.body:
## Problem
`QueueService` holds the queue in a static list. `Handle(TrackedDownloadUpdatedEvent)` computes the new queue from the current list and then overwrites it, so a slower concurrent refresh can replace a newer result with an older snapshot. It self-heals on the next refresh, but until then the queue view can show stale state (items already removed still listed, or new ones missing).

## Evidence
Observed on a live instance: items removed via `DELETE /api/v1/queue/{id}` kept appearing in `GET /api/v1/queue` until the next sweep or a restart.

## Suggested fix
Not just a lock: publish immutable snapshots with a version/timestamp and only replace when the incoming snapshot is newer, or rebuild the list under a single writer. Found while reviewing #207.

items.title: [BUG] Manual import execution aborts the whole batch when one selected file has vanished
items.body:
## Problem
`ManualImportService.ExecuteManualImport` reads `fileInfo.Length` (around the `Size = fileInfo.Length` assignment for each requested file) with no `Exists` guard or per-file try/catch. If one selected file disappears between the preview and the execute, `FileNotFoundException` aborts the command and none of the other files are imported.

## Expected
Reject that one file (as the suggested-match path already does) and continue with the rest.

## Related
The preview side of the same problem is fixed in #208. Found while reviewing it.

items.title: [LOG] Manual import decision maker logs an Error with a stack trace for every file that vanished or fails to read
items.body:
## Problem
`SimpleImportDecisionMaker` catches per-file failures and turns them into rejected decisions, but logs each one at Error level with a full stack. A folder with many unreadable or vanished files floods the log at Error. A rejection that the user sees in the UI is not an application error; Warn (or Debug for the stack) is enough.

Found while reviewing #208.

items.title: [BUG] BasicRepository.InsertMany binds parameters by runtime type, so polymorphic handler-typed columns fail on Postgres
items.body:
## Problem
The Postgres batch path of `BasicRepository.InsertMany` adds each value with `parameters.Add(name, prop.GetValue(model))`, so Dapper resolves the type handler from the value's runtime type. A column whose handler is registered for a base type (for example `CommandModel.Body` with the `Command` handler) fails for every derived type: `The member p0_Body of type ...RefreshAuthorCommand cannot be used as a parameter value`. Single `Insert` binds the model and uses the declared property type, so it works.

## Impact
Any `InsertMany` caller with such a column. The only one found is `CommandModel.Body` via `CommandQueueManager.PushMany` (worked around in #210 by inserting per command, which broke the bulk author editor with a 500).

## Suggested fix
Bind by declared type in `InsertMany` (or apply the registered handler to the value before adding it), so batch and single inserts behave the same. Found while reviewing #210.

items.title: [BUG] CommandQueueManager.PushMany only dedupes against the queue snapshot, not within its own batch
items.body:
## Problem
`PushMany` checks each command against `_commandQueue.QueuedOrStarted()` captured before the loop, so passing the same command twice in one batch inserts and queues it twice.

## Suggested fix
Also compare each command against the ones already accepted in the current batch. Found while reviewing #210.

items.title: [PERF] Blocked completed downloads are re-matched from scratch on every retry, with no backoff
items.body:
## Problem
A completed download that cannot be imported (for example a multi-hundred-file audiobook whose files do not match) is re-matched file by file on every retry pass. With the retry that reuses the manual preview's matching context (#211) each retry does roughly two matching passes instead of one, and nothing caps or backs off the retries for a download whose result has not changed.

## Suggested direction
Remember the last result per download (path set plus mtime/size signature) and skip re-matching until the folder contents or the library's relevant metadata change, or apply exponential backoff. This is a design decision for the maintainers, so filing as an issue only. Found while reviewing #211; not measured.

items.title: [LOG] Auto-import retry logs an Error with a stack trace every time local matching throws
items.body:
## Problem
When the local matching pass used by the completed-download retry throws, it is logged at Error with the exception for every retry of every affected download, which floods the log for a persistently failing download. Warn (message only) with the stack at Debug would do. Found while reviewing #211.

items.title: [BUG] EBook tag readers catch Exception and turn cancellation and out-of-memory into TagExtractionException
items.body:
## Problem
The EPUB, AZW3/MOBI and PDF tag readers wrap their work in `catch (Exception)` and rethrow as `TagExtractionException`, which also swallows cancellation and out-of-memory conditions and reports them as an unreadable file (the import is then rejected). Cancellation and `OutOfMemoryException` should propagate. Found while reviewing #212.

items.title: [BUG] EBookTagService.Truncate mis-sizes a lone surrogate character
items.body:
## Problem
`Truncate` decides how many chars to keep from the character at the cut point; a lone (unpaired) surrogate followed by a non-surrogate makes it use the wrong char size. It does not crash, but the result can cut a valid character or keep one char too many. Low priority. Found while reviewing #212.

items.title: [BUG] Import into a same-work pocket fails with an exception when the author has no root folder for that media type
items.body:
## Problem
When a completed download is accepted into a same-work pocket of the other media type (#213), the target author may have no root folder for that media type (on one live library 302 authors had only an ebook root and 509 only an audiobook root). The import then throws `No root folder configured for quality type: ...` from the path builder instead of being rejected with a clear reason.

## Suggested fix
Check for a root folder for the target media type when deciding the pocket match and reject with an actionable message (or fall back to the default root for that media type; #219 fills the missing root for newly added authors). Found while reviewing #213.

items.title: [PERF] After three yields the sweep runs the whole backlog while holding the disk slot, so manual imports can wait for a full sweep
items.body:
## Problem
With the bounded yield (#214), after `MaxConsecutiveYields` yields the next `ProcessMonitoredDownloads` run processes the entire backlog to completion while holding the disk-access slot. On a very large backlog this recreates the original starvation in the other direction: manual imports and other disk commands wait for a full sweep.

## Suggested direction
Bound the unbounded run by time or by a chunk of downloads (then yield regardless), so neither side can wait for a whole backlog. This is a design decision for the maintainers. Found while reviewing #214.

items.title: [BUG] On a profile with UpgradeAllowed false, an equal-or-worse automatic re-download creates an additional-copy Book instance instead of being rejected as already imported
items.body:
## Problem
For a quality profile that does not allow upgrades, an automatic re-download of an edition that already has files of equal or better quality is routed to an additional-copy path (a new Book instance) before the duplicate guard from #215 runs, so it does not get the 'Already imported' rejection. This is the same import churn as the equal-quality replace bug in another form, and it multiplies Book rows per edition.

## Open question
When an additional copy is genuinely wanted (a second narrator or format) versus a duplicate needs a design decision, so this is filed as an issue only. Found while reviewing #215.

items.title: [UX] Downloads rejected as 'Already imported' stay importBlocked in the queue forever
items.body:
## Problem
A completed download rejected because the edition already has files of equal or better quality stays in the queue as importBlocked and needs manual removal. On a library-scale import this leaves thousands of items that can never resolve.

## Suggested direction
Complete or remove the queue item automatically when the rejection is a duplicate (with the download client keeping the torrent), or make it a configurable behaviour like completed-download handling. This is a maintainer's design call. Found while reviewing #215.

items.title: [FEATURE] Adopt an identical untracked file at the managed destination instead of rejecting the import
items.body:
## Problem
With #216 an automatic import onto a destination that is occupied by an untracked file (for example an orphan left by an earlier failed import) is rejected, which leaves the download blocked until someone removes the file by hand.

## Suggested direction
If the untracked file at the destination is byte-identical (size and hash) to the incoming file, adopt it (create the BookFile row) instead of rejecting, so an interrupted import can complete. Found while reviewing #216.

comments.body: Related: #50, which asks for the same adoption behavior as an opt-in setting, extended to non-identical files with safety checks.

items.title: [BUG] A forced import onto an occupied destination still throws DestinationAlreadyExistsException
items.body:
## Problem
The up-front destination check (#216, #217) excludes forced downloads (`downloadForced`), but the transfer never overwrites an existing file, so a forced import onto an occupied destination still throws `DestinationAlreadyExistsException` instead of being rejected with a reason (or replacing when that was intended).

## Suggested fix
Apply the same classification to forced imports, or define what a forced import should do to an occupied destination. Found while reviewing #217.

items.title: [UX] Manual import occupied-destination rejection does not say how to proceed
items.body:
## Problem
The rejection shown for a manual import onto an occupied destination (#217) says what is in the way but not what to do (remove or track the existing file, or choose replace). A short hint would make it actionable. Found while reviewing #217.

items.title: [PERF] SaveEntity still clones every book of the author on each single-book save (authorStoredById)
items.body:
## Problem
Even with the author book list reused (#166, #218), `authorStoredById` clones all N books of the author for every single-book save during an author refresh, so the CPU cost per refresh is still O(N^2) in clones (no database round trip, but 5,000 clones per save for a 5,000-book author).

## Suggested direction
Clone only the books whose stored state is actually compared (the changed book and its work-group siblings), or compare against the loaded instances without cloning. Found while reviewing #218.

items.title: [FEATURE] Backfill missing root folders for existing authors, or a bulk 'set default roots' editor action
items.body:
## Problem
#219 fills the missing format's root folder for newly added authors only. Existing authors created before it keep a single root (on one live instance 509 were audiobook-only and 303 ebook-only, all created by import paths), which blocks 'sync monitored across formats' for them. They had to be fixed through the bulk author editor API, in batches, because each change queues a metadata refresh.

## Suggested direction
A one-shot 'set default roots for authors missing one' action in the bulk editor (or a startup/maintenance task) that applies the effective defaults. Found while reviewing #219.

items.title: [FEATURE] Let an import list or author be explicitly single-format so default root filling and profile inheritance are skipped
items.body:
## Problem
With #219 every newly added author gets both formats' default roots, and with them the other format's profiles and monitoring copied from the root defaults. There is no way to say an import list or an author is intentionally single-format. Found while reviewing #219.

items.title: [PERF] Manual import preview matches every file of a multi-file group independently; memoize the match by identical tag evidence
items.body:
## Problem
The manual import preview context sets `PerFileMatching = true`. For a multi-file group `FileMatchingService.MatchPerFile` runs a full independent staged match for every file (FTS recall and ranking, scoped and unrestricted evaluation, `EvaluateHolyGrailMatchFileInternal` per file). The only cache is by path, so chapters of one audiobook that carry identical tag evidence each pay the whole cost again. Measured: a 655-file audiobook preview took ~577 s on a repeat run (~0.9 s per file), so it is not tag reading (tags are cached by path/mtime/size).

## Suggested direction
Memoize the match result by the tag evidence (author, album/title, series, year, ...) within one preview, keeping the 'avoid flat-folder collapse' behaviour for genuinely different files. Found while reviewing #220.

items.title: [PERF] The tag cache clears itself completely at 1,000 entries instead of evicting
items.body:
## Problem
The in-memory tag cache used by the import decision maker is capped at 1,000 entries and clears entirely when it overflows, so any folder larger than the cap thrashes it and re-reads tags. It should evict (LRU or oldest-first) instead. Low priority. Found while reviewing #220.

items.title: [BUG] Per-refresh state on singleton services is shared between concurrent RefreshAuthor commands (plain Dictionary/HashSet fields)
items.body:
## Problem
RefreshAuthorCommand neither requires disk access nor is type exclusive, so per-author refreshes run concurrently (3 command threads by default, more with #222), but several singleton services keep per-refresh state in plain instance fields that are cleared at the end of each refresh:
- `RefreshBookService._bookMetadataCache` (Dictionary, cleared at the end of RefreshBookInfo while other refreshes read and write it) and `_editionRefreshMatchingIndex`
- `RefreshAuthorService._bookRefreshMatchingIndex` and `_authorRefreshRehomeBlueprint`
- `AuthorStatisticsService._deferredFileAuthorIds` (HashSet updated and cleared from several threads)
Concurrent access can corrupt a Dictionary/HashSet (exceptions, infinite loops) or make one refresh see or clear another's state. The same class of bug was fixed for the author books hint (#218) and the matched-remote hint (#181) by holding the state in an AsyncLocal.

## Suggested fix
Hold each in an AsyncLocal (or pass it explicitly) for the duration of one refresh. Found while reviewing #222.

items.title: [PERF] Long per-author refreshes can occupy every command thread and starve short commands
items.body:
## Problem
Command priority ordering exists, but N long RefreshAuthor commands (an author with ~5,000 books takes minutes) can still occupy all N command threads while RSS sync, download processing and imports wait. Raising the thread count (#222) reduces but does not remove this.

## Suggested direction
Reserve one or two threads for non-long-running or high-priority commands, or cap concurrent commands of the same name. Found while reviewing #222.

items.title: [BUG] A multi-part audiobook with one vanished part can still be marked Imported when previewFiles is absent
items.body:
## Problem
In the manual import completion logic, when `previewFiles` is absent and the expected books already exist, a multi-part audiobook with one vanished part can still be marked Imported: the count of expected files is not compared with the files that were actually imported. Pre-existing; the per-file rejection added in #249 makes the vanished part visible but the download-level decision does not use it in this path. Found while reviewing #249.

items.title: [BUG] A failed cache-database migration blocks startup instead of recreating the cache
items.body:
## Problem
The HTTP response cache database is disposable, but if a migration fails on it (for example a unique-index migration such as #252 hitting unexpected data) chaptarr stops at startup with 'Error creating main database'. Since the cache holds only re-fetchable responses, a failed cache migration could recreate the cache database (or drop the table) and continue. Found while reviewing #252.

items.title: [PERF] Manual import preview loads up to 20 full Book entities per file (GetBooks in EvaluateHolyGrailMatchFileInternal); cache per preview call by book id
items.body:
## Problem
A 655-file audiobook manual import preview takes ~512 s (~0.75 s per file) even with recall and ranking memoized (#253: 577 s -> 512 s). The remaining cost is inside `FileMatchingService.EvaluateHolyGrailMatchFileInternal`, per file: `_bookService.GetBooks(uniqueBookIds)` (~line 6024) hydrates up to 20 books with editions and authors per file, plus `GetBook` (~4670, ~9384) and `GetAuthor` (~4402) per candidate. Tags and durations are cached per path; `GetAllAuthors` is cached.

## Suggested direction
Cache hydrated books/authors by id for the duration of one preview call (like the memo in #253), so 655 chapters of one audiobook load the same candidate books once. Cheapest measurement first: diff `pg_stat_statements` calls/rows for the `Editions.*, Books.*, Authors.*` join and take thread snapshots during one preview. Found while reviewing #253.

items.title: [BUG] Chaptarr drops still valid mam_id

But the second i press "update" in mousetrap, i can do a successful "test"-button press and the indexer is once again ok in chaptarr. Mind you, mousetrap is never reporting anything as failed or not working and i dont have to visit MaM to update/refresh the mam_id.

items.title: Release search only uses the localized/current edition title, no fallback to other-language editions
items.body:
## Description

When an author's book has its primary `title` set to a non-English (translated) edition — because the Metadata Profile's Allowed Languages was scoped to that language when the author was first added/refreshed — `ReleaseSearchService` searches indexers using only that single, localized title. There is no fallback to the book's other known editions/titles (e.g. the original English title, or other translated editions that do have releases indexed).

This means an automatic/manual search can process hundreds of raw indexer results and still return "0 reports downloaded", even though releases for the same book exist in abundance under a different title/language — with no warning to the user about why.

## Repro steps

1. Create a Metadata Profile with `Allowed Languages` restricted to a non-English language (e.g. `Dutch`).
2. Add an author using that profile (audiobook or ebook).
3. Note the book's `title` gets set from the localized edition, e.g. `Mooie Meisjes` for Karin Slaughter's *Pretty Girls*.
4. Run a search (interactive `GET /api/v1/release?bookId=X` or `AuthorSearch`/`BookSearch` command).
5. Log shows the query sent to indexers uses the localized title, e.g.:
   ```
   ReleaseSearchService|Searching indexers for [Karin Slaughter - Mooie Meisjes]. 5 active indexers
   ```
   Meanwhile a direct Prowlarr/indexer search for `Karin Slaughter` alone returns 200+ results, none titled "Mooie Meisjes" (they're in English/German/Danish/Swedish, e.g. "Pretty Girls", "Blutige Fesseln").
6. Result: `0 reports downloaded`, despite the book being genuinely available.

## Workaround found

Widening the Metadata Profile's `Allowed Languages` afterward is **not enough** — the book/edition data already in the local DB doesn't change. Only after manually triggering a full `RefreshAuthor` command (metadata refresh) does chaptarr pull in the other-language editions from the metadata source (Hardcover in our case), at which point it auto-picked a different primary `title` for the book (`Pretty Girls`) and search started working.

This workaround isn't discoverable — there's no UI hint that the book's title/search-term is effectively "stuck" on a language with no available releases, and manually editing the `title` field via the API is silently ignored/overwritten (presumably re-derived from the edition data on save).

## Suggested fixes (any of)

- Include a book's known alternate-language edition titles as additional/OR'd search terms, not just the current primary title.
- Surface a warning/badge on the book/author page when 0 releases are found for repeated searches, especially when other-language editions are known to exist for the same book.
- After changing a Metadata Profile's Allowed Languages on an author with existing books, prompt to refresh metadata (or do it automatically) so search terms stay in sync with the new language scope.

## Environment

- Chaptarr version: 0.9.911.0 (develop branch), Docker (`chaptarr/chaptarr:latest`)
- Metadata source: Hardcover
- Reproduced with author Karin Slaughter / book "Pretty Girls" (Dutch edition title "Mooie Meisjes")

items.title: [BUG] Import matches a sibling book when the file title carries a subtitle the edition title lacks
items.body:
**Version:** 0.9.965.0 (Docker, `chaptarr/chaptarr:develop`, buildTime 2026-09-27T18:51:06Z), PostgreSQL backend

## What happens

A book file whose embedded title carries a subtitle that its own edition title does not have fails the strict edition-eligibility pass with `CONTAINMENT_FAILED`. The fallback that runs next re-scores with `!stagedPreferredBookIds.Contains(...)`, so the book Stage 2 already identified is excluded by construction — and the only candidate that passes containment is the edition titled exactly the bare series name. That edition wins.

Concretely: **"The Primal Hunter 6" imports as "The Primal Hunter, Vol. 1".** Book 6, edition 16318 (ASIN `B0BW17HMDZ`), resolves to book 6589 — the series' volume 1.

## To reproduce

The trigger is the subtitle, not the series number. Take the same file and change **only** `dc:title` in its OPF:

| `dc:title` in the epub | Matched book |
|---|---|
| `The Primal Hunter 6` | The Primal Hunter 6 — **correct** |
| `The Primal Hunter 6: A LitRPG Adventure` | The Primal Hunter, Vol. 1 — **wrong** |
| `The Primal Hunter` | The Primal Hunter, Vol. 1 |

Same file, same ASIN, same tags otherwise. Nothing but the title string differs between rows 1 and 2.

Steps:

1. `GET /api/v1/manualimport?folder=<folder>&filterExistingFiles=false` on the file titled `The Primal Hunter 6: A LitRPG Adventure`.
2. Response suggests "The Primal Hunter, Vol. 1" with `rejections: []`.
3. Edit `dc:title` to `The Primal Hunter 6`, re-zip, repeat. Response suggests "The Primal Hunter 6".

For the A/B I built `NzbDrone.MatchBench` and ran `/libraryaudit /live=true /source=disk` against a directory holding the variants, then compared `match_selected` per file.

## What the trace shows

```
[STAGED-FTS-FALLBACK] Stage 2 selected provider Book 'Ebook|base:hc:1093426',
but none of its Editions passed eligibility; running deep analysis on the
remaining author-gated Books.
MATCH ACCEPTED (book-occurrence-edition-selection-leftover): EditionId=16309, Title='The Primal Hunter'
```

Stage 2 gets it right — `hc:1093426` is the correct book (local id 6598), with `fts_stage2_book_selected` reporting `localBookIds: 6598`, `titleFields: title[0]`, `yearExact: true`, and the edition's provider keys `az:B0BW17HMDZ,hc:edition:31229956`. The exact ASIN is right there in the file.

The strict pass then rejects that very edition:

```
candidate_rejected  ed=16318 book=6598  reason=CONTAINMENT_FAILED
```

**21 of the 22 candidates were rejected with `CONTAINMENT_FAILED`.** The sole survivor was edition 16309, titled exactly `The Primal Hunter`. So the fallback picks it, and the winning provenance records the series digit as neutral:

```
[ 0,17] 'The Primal Hunter'   supporting   title      edition
[18,19] '6'                   neutral      tolerated_metadata
```

## Expected behavior

A file whose title contains its own edition title as a prefix should match that edition. At minimum, this shouldn't come back as a clean success with no rejections — see #105.

## Diagnostics gap (may be worth fixing on its own)

The rejection reason is invisible in production. `IFileMatchingService.TraceSink` is assigned only in `HolyGrailSmokeTestFixture` and `NzbDrone.MatchBench`, so every `RecordCandidateRejection` call — gate name, leftovers, reason — writes to a sink that doesn't exist at runtime. No log level exposes it; two Trace-level captures of this exact match produced zero rejection lines. I only got `CONTAINMENT_FAILED` by building MatchBench.

## Additional context

- Related but distinct from #111: that's duplicate book rows hijacking the monitored row via intersecting work IDs. This author's rows are a different mechanism, and the wrong match here happens inside `FileMatchingService` containment, not the retarget path.
- #105 is the reporting side of this: the wrong match is returned with `rejections: []` and no confidence, so it's indistinguishable from a correct one. This is one concrete mechanism behind it.
- The leftover symptom is the `importBlocked` queue record (#50, #236): grabbed for book 6598, import matched 6589, and it stays there.
- Across this library, 65 `DownloadImportIncomplete` events over 31 books with repeated grabs of the same book are consistent with this path.

**Uncertainty:** I haven't pinned the exact predicate inside containment that yields no evidence when the field value has extra trailing tokens. The interior-gap check in `TitleTokenAlignment.TryAlignStructural` (lines 88–98) looks like it should pass for `[the, primal, hunter, 6]` against `[the, primal, hunter, 6, a, litrpg, adventure]`, so something upstream of it is dropping the evidence. The A/B above should locate it quickly.

## Logs

Matcher trace from the repro (MatchBench `/libraryaudit`):

```
[FILE-GROUP] Embedded tags used (14 keys): all_authors, author, authors, calibre:timestamp, calibre:title_sort, contributor_bkp, cover, creator_aut, date, identifier_unknown
Staged FTS retained 20/20 recalled Books after 1 unique author evaluations and ranked 22 Editions from 6 residual fields
Got 22 FTS results, validating evidence and leftovers...
[STAGED-FTS-FALLBACK] Stage 2 selected provider Book 'Ebook|base:hc:1093426', but none of its Editions passed eligibility; running deep analysis on the remaining author-gated Books.
MATCH ACCEPTED (book-occurrence-edition-selection-leftover): EditionId=16309, Title='The Primal Hunter'
SUCCESS: bk=6589 'The Primal Hunter, Vol. 1' ed=16309 author='Zogarth'
```

The book is not truncated by the recall limit — I re-ran the stage-1 recall SQL directly against Postgres and it ranks #10 of 23 with the `6` token and #17 without it, against a limit of 20.

items.title: [BUG] Infinite pending-import retry recreates user-deleted authors as monitored and ignores ImportListExclusions
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

A `PendingAuthorImport` row whose requested works can never be resolved retries forever (`MaxAttempts = 0`, no terminal condition). Each retry calls `AuthorLibraryService.AddAuthorAsync` with the monitoring config stored on the row. If the user has since deleted the author, the retry re-inserts it **monitored** (both media sides) with `MonitorNewItems = All`.

Two things make this unrecoverable from the UI:

1. `ImportListExclusions` is never consulted on the pending-queue path, so the exclusion that the UI creates on "delete author → add import list exclusion" does not stop the retry.
2. Removing the import list that queued the row does not purge or cancel its pending rows.

Observed in production: one row at **415 attempts** over ~2 days, reinstating the author roughly every 5 minutes.

**To Reproduce**

1. Have a Hardcover import list whose request includes a *work* that the metadata server keeps out of the author's catalog (announced/upcoming work, or a work with no editions). The row never reaches the success path and is retried indefinitely with errors like:

   ```
   Requested Ebook work hc:XXXXXX, Ebook work hc:YYYYYY is not yet present in the authoritative author catalog.
   Requested work(s) hc:ZZZZZZ ... are still being prepared by the metadata server.
   ```

2. Let it retry. `AttemptCount` climbs without bound; `OverallStatus` stays `Retrying` (3); `MaxAttempts` stays `0`.

3. Delete the imported author from the library, with "add import list exclusion" checked.

4. Observe: within ~5 minutes the author is re-added **and** monitored. The exclusion does not prevent it.

**Expected behavior**

- Retries should not resurrect an author the user deliberately deleted.
- An `ImportListExclusion` for the row's provider ID should stop, cancel, or refuse the retry.
- Removing an import list should not leave permanently-retrying orphan rows behind.
- A row that cannot ever succeed should reach a terminal state instead of retrying forever.

**Root cause (source, running develop @ `e67374f`)**

`src/NzbDrone.Core/Books/Commands/ProcessPendingImportsCommandHandler.cs`

- `ProcessPendingImportAsync` (line 198) calls `AddAuthorAsync(item.ProviderId, config)` (line 226) **before** any check on whether the requested works can be resolved.
- When they can't be, it calls `_pendingImportService.ScheduleRetry(item, reason)` (lines 254/270) and returns — the success path (`MarkSucceeded` line 280 + `TryDeleteIfUnchanged`) is unreachable, so the row is immortal.
- Nothing in this handler reads `ImportListExclusions`.

`src/NzbDrone.Core/Books/Services/AuthorLibraryService.cs`

- Line 331: `ApplyMonitoringConfig(author, config)` sets the media gates from the row's stored config before any existence check.
- Line 351: if no author exists locally, the create path runs — line 389 `_authorService.AddAuthor(author, false)` inserts the recreated author with those gates applied. This is the resurrection.
- Line 354: if the author does exist, `HandleExistingAuthorAsync` → line 1068 `ApplyExistingAuthorProgressiveSettings`, which routes into `UpdateAuthorProgressiveSettings`. That method does NULL-only fills (`if (!author.AudiobookMonitored.HasValue && audiobookMonitored.HasValue)`), so an author that was merely *unmonitored* keeps its explicit `false` — the damage is specifically on the delete-then-recreate path.

`src/NzbDrone.Core/Books/Services/PendingAuthorImportService.cs`

- `Cancel(int id)` (line 677) exists and sets a terminal status, but nothing calls it automatically when an exclusion is added or a list is removed.

`src/NzbDrone.Core/Books/Repositories/PendingAuthorImportRepository.cs`

- `GetDueForProcessing` (line 45) selects rows with `OverallStatus == Pending || Retrying` and `NextAttemptAt <= cutoff` — no attempt ceiling.

**Evidence**

Pending rows at time of filing (5 rows, all `MaxAttempts = 0`):

```
Id   ProviderId     OverallStatus  AttemptCount  LastError
103  hc:NNNNNN      3 (Retrying)   415           Requested Ebook work hc:XXXXXX, hc:YYYYYY is not yet present in the authoritative author catalog.
122  hc:NNNNNN      3 (Retrying)   96            Requested Ebook work hc:XXXXXX, hc:YYYYYY is not yet present in the authoritative author catalog.
117  hc:NNNNNN      3 (Retrying)   93            Requested Audiobook work hc:XXXXXX, hc:YYYYYY, Ebook work hc:XXXXXX is not yet present in the authoritative author catalog.
118  hc:NNNNNN      3 (Retrying)   95            Requested Ebook work hc:XXXXXX is not yet present in the authoritative author catalog.
119  hc:NNNNNN      3 (Retrying)   97            Requested work(s) hc:XXXXXX, hc:XXXXXX are still being prepared by the metadata server.
```

(provider/work IDs redacted; happy to supply on request)

Log, repeating every ~5 minutes indefinitely:

```
2026-09-29 01:17:53.5|Info|ProcessPendingImportsCommandHandler|Processing pending import 103 for provider hc:NNNNNN
2026-09-29 01:17:53.5|Info|ProcessPendingImportsCommandHandler|Processing queued author import for provider hc:NNNNNN
2026-09-29 01:17:54.8|Info|AuthorLibraryService|Author 'Author A' already exists in database with 45 books (audiobook=True, ebook=True)
...
2026-09-29 09:18:16.1|Info|AuthorLibraryService|Author 'Author A' already exists in database with 45 books (audiobook=True, ebook=True)
```

`ImportListExclusions` contains the correct exclusion for that provider ID, created via the delete-author flow. `ImportLists` is empty (list removed) — the pending rows survived.

**Suggested fixes**

1. Honour `ImportListExclusions` in `ProcessPendingImportsCommandHandler` (same `MatchesExclusionId` semantics as `ImportListSyncService`) — skip and cancel the row.
2. Cancel pending rows for an author when the user deletes it with "add import list exclusion", and/or when the queueing import list is removed.
3. Do not re-apply `AudiobookMonitored`/`EbookMonitored`/`MonitorNewItems` from a stored row when the author already exists and the user has explicitly changed those settings — the manual-override flags (`AudiobookSettingsManuallyOverridden` / `EbookSettingsManuallyOverridden`) exist for exactly this and are not consulted here.
4. Give the "requested work not present in catalog" branch a terminal or long-backoff state (it can never resolve on its own). Related: #119 covers the unbounded-retry family.

**Workaround**

The supported cancel endpoint stops it, and the row then leaves the retry set (`GetDueForProcessing` only selects `Pending`/`Retrying`):

```bash
curl -X DELETE -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" http://HOST:8789/api/v1/pendingauthorimport/103
# -> {"message": "Pending import cancelled"}
```

Finding the stuck rows requires `GET /api/v1/pendingauthorimport`. The API was the only path I found to list or cancel these rows once the author is absent from the library, which is why this is easy to hit and hard to diagnose.

**System Information:**
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (Docker container, Unraid host)
- Chaptarr Version: 0.9.965.0 (develop), migrationVersion 107
- Installation Method: Docker (`chaptarr/chaptarr:develop`)
- Database: PostgreSQL 18 (not SQLite — this is not the #119 lock cascade)

comments.body:
Same issue here, with a **Goodreads** import list (not Hardcover), still present on **0.9.965.0**.

I had started a Goodreads list import, stopped it because it was grabbing too many books, then deleted the list. Two `PendingAuthorImport` rows created by that list kept retrying for **40 days**:

| Id | Provider | OverallStatus | AttemptCount | MaxAttempts | LastError |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 57 | gr:19597346 | 3 | 9262 | 0 | Requested Audiobook work gr:171328772 is not yet present in the authoritative author catalog. |
| 16 | gr:21646097 | 3 | 9246 | 0 | Requested work(s) gr:288355600 are still being prepared by the metadata server. |

Both rows: `CreatedAt = 2026-08-31`, `RequestedBy = ImportList:<list name>`, and the `ImportLists` table is empty (list already deleted).

**Performance impact:** every retry (~every 3–5 min) runs a full author + book refresh even though the author already exists, so Chaptarr kept re-reading its 144 MB `chaptarr.db`. On a Synology DS720+ (HDD, 6 GB RAM) Chaptarr alone was ~90% of the NAS disk I/O (~30 MB/s of reads), system iowait was ~70%, and the Chaptarr UI took a long time to load.

```
2026-10-10 18:07:56.0|Info|ProcessPendingImportsCommandHandler|Processing pending import 57 for provider gr:19597346
2026-10-10 18:07:56.0|Info|ProcessPendingImportsCommandHandler|Processing queued author import for provider gr:19597346
2026-10-10 18:08:26.3|Info|RefreshAuthorService|Checking Info for Alex Sol
2026-10-10 18:09:57.2|Info|AuthorLibraryService|Author 'Alex Sol' already exists in database with 9 books (audiobook=True, ebook=False)
2026-10-10 18:10:52.0|Info|RefreshAuthorService|Checking Info for Alex Sol
2026-10-10 18:11:21.3|Info|AuthorLibraryService|Author 'Alex Sol' already exists in database with 9 books (audiobook=True, ebook=False)
```

**Workaround (no container stop, no manual DB edit):** the API cancels the rows cleanly:

```
DELETE /api/v1/pendingauthorimport/57   -> {"message": "Pending import cancelled"}
DELETE /api/v1/pendingauthorimport/16   -> {"message": "Pending import cancelled"}
```

```
2026-10-10 18:13:36.6|Info|PendingAuthorImportService|Cancelled pending import 57
2026-10-10 18:13:36.6|Info|PendingAuthorImportService|Cancelled pending import 16
```

Rows move to `OverallStatus = 6` and the retries stop. System iowait went from ~71% to ~3% right after. `GET /api/v1/pendingauthorimport` lists the rows, but there's no UI for it as far as I can tell, so a page under Activity to list and cancel pending author imports would help users find this.

**Environment:** Synology DSM 7 (DS720+), Docker, `chaptarr/chaptarr:develop` (0.9.965.0), installed with Docker Compose.
