items.title: perf: post-scan metadata-file cleanup probes every MetadataFiles row across up to 3 base paths, with directory-enumeration fallback on misses
items.body:
## Summary
After every author scan, `CleanExtraFileService.Clean` checks **every** `MetadataFiles` row of that author against the disk, one `FileExists` per row per base path, and deletes rows one at a time. On a large library on network storage this is a lot of disk round trips per scan, and the misses are the expensive ones because `FileExists` falls back to directory enumeration when the exact path is not found.

I have not measured the wall time of a single `Clean` call, so this is a code-reading plus profiling observation, not a benchmark.

## Where
- `MetadataService.CreateAfterAuthorScan` calls `_cleanMetadataService.Clean(author)` first thing (`Extras/Metadata/MetadataService.cs`), reached from `ExtraService` after an author scan (`Extras/ExtraService.cs`, two call sites).
- `CleanExtraFileService.Clean` (`Extras/Metadata/Files/CleanMetadataFileService.cs`):
  ```csharp
  foreach (var metadataFile in metadataFiles)   // every row for the author
  {
      var exists = ExtraFilePathHelper.GetAuthorBasePaths(author)      // audiobook, ebook, legacy path
          .Select(p => Path.Combine(p, metadataFile.RelativePath))
          .Any(_diskProvider.FileExists);
      if (!exists) _metadataFileService.Delete(metadataFile.Id);        // one DELETE per missing row
  }
  ```
- `DiskProviderBase.FileExists(path, comparison)` does the stat, and if it misses it returns `ResolveExistingFilePath(path).IsNotNullOrWhiteSpace()`, which walks the path segment by segment and enumerates directory entries (`ResolvePathSegment`).

## Why it is costly
1. **Rows x base paths.** `GetAuthorBasePaths` returns up to three distinct paths in the order audiobook, ebook, legacy `Path`. `.Any(...)` stops at the first hit, so a sidecar that lives under the ebook folder is first probed under the audiobook folder. That first probe is a miss, so it takes the directory-enumeration fallback before the ebook probe hits. Every sidecar in the "second" folder pays for a miss.
2. **Misses enumerate directories.** For a missing file the fallback lists entries in each directory on the path. With hundreds of books per author folder that is a large listing per probe.
3. **Per-row deletes.** Each missing row is deleted individually instead of in one batch.
4. **It runs on every scan**, even if nothing on disk changed since the last one.

## What I saw
On a library of about 2,770 authors with about 70,800 `MetadataFiles` rows on network-mounted storage (authors with 500 to 700 rows each are common, e.g. 716, 609, 532, 526):
- During a large refresh, a stack sample showed one busy thread in `DiskProviderBase.FileExists` under `CleanExtraFileService.Clean` (`CreateAfterAuthorScan` <- `ExtraService.Handle`). That was 1 of 14 busy stacks, so it was present but not the dominant cost in that window. The larger costs at the time were elsewhere.
- Not measured: time per `Clean` call, or how many probes are misses.

## Possible improvements
- Probe only the base path that matches the row's media type (or remember which base path each row belongs to), instead of trying paths in a fixed order.
- List each base folder once per scan and test rows against that in-memory set, instead of one `FileExists` per row.
- Delete missing rows in a single batched statement.
- Skip the cleanup when the author's folders have not changed since the last scan.

## Related
`FileExists` falling back to directory enumeration on a miss is also the cause of the quadratic behaviour in the cover-metadata case addressed by the open PR #237, so this is the same underlying cost showing up in a second place.

items.title: [BUG] Unmapped files are re-matched with no backoff on every author-import completion, sustaining pegged CPU indefinitely
items.body:
## Summary

Any library containing files that cannot be matched (unmapped, `EditionId == 0`) enters a
sustained re-match cycle: each completed pending-author import queues a *targeted folder
rescan* of any author folder that contains an unmapped file; the rescan re-runs the staged
FTS matcher (including the "deep analysis" fallback) on those files, produces the identical
failure, and leaves them unmapped — ready to be re-triggered by the next completion.

With `ProcessPendingImportsCommand` at a 1-minute interval and `ImportListSyncCommand` at
5 minutes (both hard-coded in `TaskManager`), a library with 1,762 unmapped files sustained
pegged CPU around the clock. Over a 32-hour window on one instance: constant 75–180% CPU,
**2.97 TB of block I/O**, and a **2.3 GB SQLite WAL** on a 781 MB database — while the
unmapped count did not move, because the failures are deterministic (same files, same
catalog, same rules every time).

## Reproduction (observed on a live library)

1. Have at least one unmapped file under an author folder (e.g. a work whose book was
   dropped by metadata-profile filtering — see #68 — or an edition the matcher rejects).
2. Leave import lists enabled (auto-add) or let any pending author import complete.
3. `IngestQueueOnAuthorReadyHandler.QueueRescanForPendingImportSuccess` pushes a
   `RescanFoldersCommand` for the author's folders whenever they contain any
   `EditionId == 0` file; the rescan re-runs `FileMatchingService` on those files and
   fails identically. The same handler's `[INGEST-AUTHOR-READY-FLUSH]` sweep
   terminal-completes the residual staging items, so every cycle is a clean slate for
   the next trigger.

Log signature (repeats every few minutes, indefinitely):

```
[Info] StagingResidualQueueSweeper: [INGEST-AUTHOR-READY-FLUSH] Swept N residual staging items under '/audiobooks/<author>'
[Warn] FileMatchingService: [HOLY-GRAIL][main-tags][STAGED-FTS-FALLBACK] Stage 2 selected provider Book ... but none of its Editions passed eligibility; running deep analysis on the remaining author-gated Books.
```

## Measurements (one instance, ~49k files / 1,762 unmapped at peak)

- 8,909 futile match attempts against 662 distinct suggested works over ~2 days with
  lists enabled; a single file attempted 17 times in one day
- Disabling auto-add on the lists dropped CPU to idle; re-enabling them resumed the
  cycle immediately (842 wasted attempts in the first hour back)
- The trigger chain: list sync (5 min) → pending import completion (1-min processor) →
  author-ready rescan → deep analysis → identical failure

## Code path

- `IngestQueueOnAuthorReadyHandler.QueueRescanForPendingImportSuccess` — queues the
  targeted `RescanFoldersCommand` whenever the author's folders contain an
  `EditionId == 0` file
- The rescan's discovery/match path re-runs `FileMatchingService` with no memory of
  prior identical attempts — no attempt counter, no backoff, no terminal state that
  distinguishes "temporarily unmatched" from "deterministically unmatched"

Related but distinct: #119 / #264 cover the *author import* retrying forever (not this
file re-match loop); #152 is the same no-backoff shape in the cover-download subsystem;
the perf items (#234 sweep backlog, #244 manual-import preview, #247 command-thread
starvation) address throughput, not the futility of the work.

## Suggested directions

- Persist a per-path attempt count / failure signature; skip re-analysis when the inputs
  (tags, catalog, rules) are unchanged, or back off exponentially per file
- Re-queue unmapped items only on configuration-relevant events (profile change, catalog
  refresh for that author) rather than every import completion
- Surface a terminal state ("unmatchable — needs upstream metadata" vs. "retry later")
  so the /unmapped page can distinguish them

## Environment

Chaptarr `0.9.911.0` (deployed from `chaptarr/chaptarr:latest`, develop branch), Docker,
Linux host, SQLite, ~49k files across two root folders (audiobook + ebook).

comments.body:
**Update — appears fixed on current develop (0.9.965).**

Re-verified after upgrading the reporting instance from 0.9.911 to `0.9.965` (docker `0.9.965` tag, 2026-09-27):

- Same library, same 210 unmapped files, import lists still enabled with auto-add
- Over a 30-minute window: list syncs running (47 items per pass, authors queued for background import) and pending author imports actively completing (78 import-activity log lines) — i.e. the trigger conditions from the original report were live
- **Zero** unmapped-file re-match attempts and **zero** `[INGEST-AUTHOR-READY-FLUSH]` / `STAGED-FTS-FALLBACK` log signatures in the window
- For comparison, on 0.9.911 under equivalent conditions the same instance measured 842 futile match attempts in the first hour after re-enabling the lists

Whatever landed between 0.9.911 and 0.9.965 (possibly the #234/#244/#247 perf family) addressed this on the client side. Closing as resolved on current develop — the server-side hydration gaps that keep the files *unmatched* in the first place are tracked in #276.

items.title: [BUG] POST /api/v1/book/import can crash with `SQLite Error 19: 'NOT NULL constraint failed: Books.CleanTitle'` while saving the "Pending Import" stub
items.body:
## Summary

`POST /api/v1/book/import` intermittently fails with a 400 whose body is a raw
persistence crash rather than a validation message:

```json
[
  {
    "propertyName": "Import",
    "errorMessage": "Failed to import book: SQLite Error 19: 'NOT NULL constraint failed: Books.CleanTitle'."
  }
]
```

The import endpoint first creates a "Pending Import" stub book/author row; on the
affected titles that stub save dies in `BookService.AddBook` → `UpdateFields` with the
NOT NULL violation above, and the whole add fails deterministically. The book cannot be
imported at all — not on the first attempt, not on retries, even though the search
(`GET /api/v1/book/lookup`) resolves the title/author cleanly and the metadata server
clearly knows the work.

Observed live today with *De Stille Patiënt* (Alex Michaelides, Dutch edition of
*The Silent Patient*): search returns the work; the add fails with exactly this body
every time.

## Stack trace (from logs, verbatim)

```
[v0.9.911.0] Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteException (0x80004005): SQLite Error 19: 'NOT NULL constraint failed: Books.CleanTitle'.
   at Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteDataReader.NextResult()
   at Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteCommand.ExecuteReader(CommandBehavior behavior)
   at Dapper.SqlMapper.ExecuteImpl(IDbConnection cnn, CommandDefinition& command) in /_/Dapper/SqlMapper.cs:line 632
   at NzbDrone.Core.Datastore.BasicRepository`1.UpdateFields(...) in ./Chaptarr.Core/Datastore/BasicRepository.cs:line 842
   at NzbDrone.Core.Books.BookService.AddBook(Book newBook, Boolean doRefresh) in ./Chaptarr.Core/Books/Services/BookService.cs:line 344
   at NzbDrone.Core.Books.AddBookService.AddBook(Book book, Boolean doRefresh)
   ...
2026-09-27 20:10:00.8|Error|BookController|[V1-BOOK-IMPORT] Unexpected error during import
```

(4 occurrences with full stacks in one retained log rotation window; reproduced on
demand today.)

## Impact

On one instance (migrating from Readarr, ~49k files), a batch of search-and-adds across
~350 works produced ~134 persistently failed adds; those hitting this crash fail
immediately and can never be re-added by the user (the retry documented in the sibling
hydration message — "Retry the add" — cannot converge when the save itself throws).
Affected titles skew toward foreign-language editions and less-mainstream works.

## Reproduction

1. `GET /api/v1/book/lookup?term=De Stille Patiënt Alex Michaelides` (or another affected
   title; foreign-language editions are the most reliable reproducers)
2. `POST /api/v1/book/import` with the returned `foreignBookId` / `foreignAuthorId`,
   `mediaType: "ebook"`, a root folder, quality/metadata profile IDs
3. Observe the 400 body above, and the `[V1-BOOK-IMPORT] Unexpected error during import`
   Error with the SQLite stack in the logs

## Suggested directions

- The stub book appears to be saved with a NULL `CleanTitle` — guard the stub creation so
  `CleanTitle` (and any other NOT NULL columns) are defaulted before insert, or salvage
  the title slug from the search payload
- Distinguish the crash from validation: an unexpected exception during import should
  return a 500-class response rather than being folded into the 400 "Import" property,
  so automation can tell "retry later" from "will never work"

## Environment

Chaptarr `0.9.911.0` (deployed from `chaptarr/chaptarr:latest`, develop branch), Docker,
Linux host, SQLite. (Line numbers above are from the deployed 0.9.911 build; current
develop may have shifted.)

comments.body:
**Still reproducing on 0.9.965 (2026-09-27 build).**

Re-ran the same repro after upgrading from 0.9.911:

- `De Stille Patiënt` (Alex Michaelides, ebook): identical 400 — `Failed to import book: SQLite Error 19: 'NOT NULL constraint failed: Books.CleanTitle'.`
- `End of Watch` (Stephen King, audiobook): now hits the same crash too — notable because this title imported **cleanly** on 0.9.911 via the same endpoint, so the crashing sub-path is at minimum unchanged and possibly easier to reach in 0.9.965.

The related UX is also worth noting: 0.9.965 replaces the hydration-retry 400 with a queued-request flow (#276), so several adds that used to fail with this crash class now take different paths — but the stub-save NOT NULL violation itself is still live on current develop.

items.title: [BUG] "Cannot add book: one or more editions are missing Title — retry the add so Chaptarr can hydrate edition metadata from the metadata server" never converges for many works the server knows
items.body:
## Summary

`POST /api/v1/book/import` frequently rejects a correctly-searched, correctly-matched
book with:

```
Cannot add book: one or more editions are missing Title. Retry the add so Chaptarr can
hydrate edition metadata from the metadata server.
```

On one instance, **132 of 134** attempted adds that produced this message stayed blocked
across **several days** of re-attempts (initial failed add plus periodic re-tries) —
including mainstream, unambiguous works the metadata server unquestionably serves in
search results moments earlier:

- *Someone Like You* — Roald Dahl
- *End of Watch* — Stephen King
- *METAtropolis* — John Scalzi
- *Sir Gawain and the Green Knight* — J.R.R. Tolkien (translation)
- *A Glory of Unicorns* — Bruce Coville

The blocked population skews heavily toward foreign-language editions and less-famous
works (e.g. the Italian *Goldfinch*, Spanish *Jade City*, Catalan translations), which
is consistent with an on-demand hydration queue whose least-requested entries never
actually hydrate.

Author-level variant (the infinite-retry behavior itself is #119 / #264 — the new datum
here is that the server never hydrates it at all): the Goodreads author record
`gr:3137322` (Fyodor Dostoevsky) returned "Author not yet available on metadata server"
for 300+ attempts spanning two days.

Downstream effect: files whose works exist only as these un-hydrated entries sit
permanently unmapped, feeding the no-backoff re-match loop in the sibling issue.

## Reproduction

1. `GET /api/v1/book/lookup?term=<title> <author>` (note: without `mediaType` — with
   `mediaType=ebook` the search returns empty results, #67)
2. `POST /api/v1/book/import` with the returned IDs — observe the message above
3. Re-attempt hours later, then daily, for several days: same rejection for the titles
   above (verbatim body captured today)

## Related observation (the matcher side of the same missing-catalog problem)

While diagnosing, the staged matcher was observed receiving the correct work identity
from the metadata service and discarding it because the work is absent from the local
catalog:

```
"reason": "No local match; V5 suggested 'Judy Blume - Superfudge'"
```

That file (clean tags, correct author) was re-attempted 17 times in a single day (see
the sibling re-match-loop issue). If the add path could consume a high-confidence
suggestion — e.g. create the suggested work as a manual addition, which is already
exempt from metadata-profile filtering — a large class of permanently-unmapped files
would resolve without the user manually searching and adding each work.

## Suggested directions

- Investigate why the hydration queue never completes for long-tail entries — or whether
  the retry actually re-requests hydration upstream vs. only re-reading the same stale
  stub
- Persist a per-work hydration status so the UI can distinguish "hydrating" from
  "un-hydratable" and retries can escalate rather than repeat
- Consider having the proxy hydrate all editions of a work whenever any edition of it
  is requested, since the add currently fails if *any* edition lacks a title

## Environment

Chaptarr `0.9.911.0` (deployed from `chaptarr/chaptarr:latest`, develop branch), Docker,
Linux host, SQLite; ~49k files; the sample list of 132 still-blocked works was captured
across the retry window and is available on request.

comments.body:
**Update — the client-side flow changed on 0.9.965 (2026-09-27 build).**

The `Cannot add book: one or more editions are missing Title. Retry the add...` 400 no longer occurs on 0.9.965. The same adds now return:

> `Failed to import book: The author and requested book are being prepared by the metadata server. Chaptarr saved your request and will add it automatically...`

i.e. the add is accepted as a queued request instead of being rejected for a manual retry — this addresses the client-side half of the report (and is visible working: the saved requests show up as pending imports that the processor picks up).

Still open, and worth tracking from the server side: whether the "being prepared" requests ever *converge* for the long-tail works in the original list (Dahl / King / Scalzi titles, foreign-language editions). On the reporting instance those works had failed to hydrate across several days of retries on 0.9.911; I'll report back on whether the new queued flow completes them.

items.title: [BUG] Root folder dialog sends null quality/metadata profile when picked from the dropdown
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
In Settings → Media Management → Add Root Folder, an eBook root folder can't be saved if you pick its quality profile from the dropdown yourself. The dropdown shows the chosen profile, but `POST /api/v1/rootFolder` sends `"ebookQualityProfileId": null`, and the server rejects it:

```
[Warn] ChaptarrErrorPipeline: Invalid request Validation failed:
 -- ebookQualityProfileId: A ebook quality profile is required
```

The value the dialog auto-selects on load is saved correctly. Only a value the user picks gets lost. Picking the eBook metadata profile by hand fails the same way (`ebookMetadataProfileId: An ebook metadata profile is required`).

**Cause**
`QualityProfileSelectInputConnector` and `MetadataProfileSelectInputConnector` pass `onChange={this.onChange}` (which does `parseInt`) to `SelectInput`, then spread `{...otherProps}` after it. `onChange` isn't destructured out of `otherProps`, so the parent's raw handler replaces the connector's. A manual pick then stores the `<select>`'s string (`"3"`) in Redux. The root folder save in `Store/Actions/Settings/rootFolders.js` runs the id through `normalizeOptionalId`, which accepts only numbers, so the string becomes `null`.

The auto-select path calls the connector's own `onChange`, so it stores a number. That is why:
- a freshly opened dialog that's saved untouched works;
- an audiobook root folder with only one audiobook profile (auto-selected) works.

**To Reproduce**
1. Have at least two eBook quality profiles (e.g. the built-in "E-Book" and a user-made "EPUB").
2. Go to Settings → Media Management → Add Root Folder.
3. Enter a name and path, then switch the media toggle to eBooks.
4. Pick "EPUB" in eBook Quality Profile. Switching to another profile and back fails the same way.
5. Click Save Ebook Folder.
6. The save fails with "A ebook quality profile is required". In devtools, the request body has `"ebookQualityProfileId":null`.

Request body captured with "EPUB" selected. "EPUB" is a user-made profile with id 3; on a fresh install the built-in "E-Book" and "Audiobook" profiles take ids 1 and 2, so the first custom profile gets id 3.

```json
{"name":"Ebooks","path":"/ebooks/","folderType":2,"defaultTags":[],"isCalibreLibrary":false,"placeEbooksWithAudiobooks":false,"ebookMonitored":true,"ebookMonitorExistingMode":"none","ebookMonitorNewItems":"new","ebookQualityProfileId":null,"ebookMetadataProfileId":2,"ebookWriteAudioBookShelfMetadataJson":false,"ebookWriteAudioBookShelfCover":false,"ebookTags":[],"audiobookMonitored":null,"audiobookMonitorExistingMode":null,"audiobookMonitorNewItems":null,"audiobookQualityProfileId":null,"audiobookMetadataProfileId":null,"audiobookWriteAudioBookShelfMetadataJson":null,"audiobookWriteAudioBookShelfCover":null,"audiobookTags":null}
```

Redux `settings.rootFolders.pendingChanges` after a manual pick: `"ebookQualityProfileId":"3"` (string). After an auto-select: `"ebookQualityProfileId":1` (number).

**Expected behavior**
The selected profile ids are sent as numbers and the root folder is created.

**Workaround**
In the browser devtools Network tab, copy the failed request with "Copy as fetch", paste it into the JS console, change `"ebookQualityProfileId":null` to the id of the profile you want (here `3`), and run it. It returns `201 Created`, so the backend validation is fine.

**System Information:**
 - OS: TrueNAS 25.10.7. Also reproduced on macOS, built from source.
 - Chaptarr Version: 0.9.965 (commit e67374f)
 - Installation Method: Docker (Docker Compose via Komodo). Also reproduced built from source.
 - Browser: Zen 1.22.3b (Firefox 156.0.1). Also reproduced in Chromium.

**Additional context**
The same code path also affects audiobook root folders where the quality or metadata profile is picked by hand (not separately tested). Both connectors are shared with other forms (Edit Author, Add Author, import lists), which also receive string ids on manual picks today.

**Logs**
See the server log line above.

items.title: [BUG] Multi-file M4B conversion runs before the destination conflict is detected
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
When a multi-file download is converted to M4B, the destination conflict check before conversion looks at the wrong path. The conversion runs in full, and only then is the import rejected because the real destination is occupied.

`GetConvertedImportDestinationPath` (`ImportApprovedBooks.cs:2415`) builds the preview from the first source file's `Part`/`PartCount` (1 of N), so naming adds a part suffix: `Author - Title - 01.m4b`. `GetConversionDestinationConflictReason` checks that path, finds nothing, and conversion starts. The converted file from `CreateGeneratedConversionLocalBook` (`:2375`) has no `Part`/`PartCount`, so its destination is `Author - Title.m4b`. If that file already exists, `GetAdditionalCopyPathCollisionReason` rejects the import after conversion.

**To Reproduce**
1. Audiobook quality profile with Convert to Quality = M4B.
2. Import a multi-file release for a book so it is converted to a single M4B.
3. Re-import the same release (or another multi-file release of that book).
4. The full conversion runs, then the import fails: `Additional physical copy cannot be imported because the managed destination is already occupied: .../Author - Title.m4b`. The converted file is retained under `.chaptarr-conversions`.

The work-folder output is named `Author - Title - 01.m4b` (taken from the checked path), while the import targets `Author - Title.m4b`.

**Expected behavior**
The conflict is detected before conversion, and nothing is converted.

**Suggested fix**
Build the preview destination the way the converted file is named: no part number when several files are merged, and the source's part number for a single file.

**System Information:**
 - OS: Ubuntu
 - Chaptarr Version: develop (0.9.965)
 - Installation Method: built from source

**Additional context**
Seen while testing #120 (multi-part M4B merge), whose merges go through the same path. The code involved is unchanged on develop, where it also affects multi-file MP3 → M4B conversions (a full re-encode before the rejection). #160 changes `GetConvertedImportDestinationPath` but keeps the part fields, so a fix here will conflict with it.

comments.body: I dont know if this really matters, I'll keep digging

Thanks for flagging the overlap with #160. #160 already rewrites GetConvertedImportDestinationPath, so I've put the fix there to keep the two from colliding. It's the commit "Check the converted file's real destination before converting" on #160.

What changed: the destination preview no longer copies the first source file's Part/PartCount. CreateGeneratedConversionLocalBook gives the converted file neither, so the preview now carries the values the import gives that file: Part 1 and no PartCount. As a result:

  • The check before conversion looks at Title.m4b.
  • The output in .chaptarr-conversions gets its final name too. With the default { (PartNumber:smart)} naming it used to be Title (1).m4b.

One difference from your suggestion: I dropped the part fields for single-file conversions as well. The converted file never has them, whatever the input count. Keeping them for a single file that was one part of a set would bring back the same mismatch.

Tests. There are two new tests in ImportApprovedBooksAdditionalCopyFixture, and both fail without the change:

  • should_find_a_taken_destination_before_converting_a_multi_part_download: 3 MP3s (parts 1–3 of 3), with Black Sheep.m4b already on disk. Nothing is converted, and the import is skipped with the conflict reason. Without the fix, the converter runs.
  • should_name_a_merged_multi_part_conversion_without_a_part_suffix: the work-folder output is Black Sheep.m4b. Without the fix, it is Black Sheep - 01.m4b.

The full Chaptarr.Core.Test suite passes.

End to end. I built #160 with and without the change and ran each in Docker. I imported two 3-file MP3 folders for the same book through DownloadedBooksScan, with the default naming format and Rename on.

  | Second release of a book that already has The Diamond Maker.m4b -- | -- Without the fix | The release is fully converted to .chaptarr-conversions/…/The Diamond Maker (1).m4b, then rejected: "Additional physical copy cannot be imported because the managed destination is already occupied: …/The Diamond Maker.m4b". The M4B is kept in the work folder. With the fix | "Conversion skipped because the destination is already occupied: …/The Diamond Maker.m4b". Nothing is converted, and the MP3s are left where they were.

Library conversions from #160 go through the same method and get the same fix. In practice they weren't hitting this: BookFile doesn't store PartCount, so their preview never had a suffix.

On #120: this change merges cleanly with #120 in this method. #120 and #160 already overlap in one other spot, the job-failure return in ConvertBookGroupIfNeeded, which is unrelated to this fix.

If you'd rather land the fix on develop before #160, let me know. I'll send it as its own PR and rebase #160 onto it.

items.title: [BUG] ManualImport: explicitly-specified bookId/editionId silently remapped onto editions of refresh-created duplicate book records
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a `ManualImport` command specifies `authorId`, `bookId`, and `editionId` explicitly, and the library contains a duplicate book record for the same title under the same author (e.g. created by author refresh activity), the import completes and reports success — but the `BookFile` row is attached to an edition of the *duplicate* book, not the requested one. No warning is logged; the explicit IDs in the payload are silently ignored.

This is a sibling of #111 (duplicate book row hijacking import matching), but on a different surface: #111 describes the tracked-download import path rejecting a completed download because title-text matching picks the duplicate. Here the failure is in the `ManualImport` API path — even the explicit `bookId`/`editionId` workaround recommended in #111 does not reliably target the intended record. The explicit identifiers are overridden, and the import lands on the newest duplicate instead.

**To Reproduce**

Observed twice in one session on Chaptarr v0.9.965.0 (Docker, Postgres). The library had multiple book rows for the same title under one author: three `Dark Age` rows under Pierce Brown (6929, 9865, and a fresh 12939), and a duplicate `Golden Son` 12938 next to 10317. The duplicates had been created during author refresh activity the same evening.

1. `POST /api/v1/command` with a `ManualImport` command whose `files[0]` specified `bookId=10317`, `editionId=25858`:

   ```json
   {"name":"ManualImport","importMode":"move","replaceExistingFiles":true,
    "files":[{"path":"...","authorId":8,"bookId":10317,"editionId":25858,"quality":{...}}]}
   ```

2. The command completed reporting `Manually imported 1 files`, but the debug log shows:

   ```
   [EDITION-IMPORT] IMPORT COMPLETE: File 'REDRISING0202.m4b' imported to edition 32214
   [BATCH-DEBUG] File 0: EditionId=32214, Path=Golden Son (Part 2 of 2) (Dramatized Adaptation) - Red Rising Saga, Book 2 - GraphicAudio.m4b
   ```

   Edition 32214 belongs to book 12938, not 10317. The requested edition 25858 stayed fileless.

3. Same pattern with `bookId=9865`, `editionId=23583`: the file landed on edition 32215 of book 12939.

In both cases the import attached to the *newest* refresh-created duplicate rather than the record the client explicitly specified.

**Expected behavior**

An explicitly-specified `editionId` should win. If the import pipeline re-parses and re-matches the filename regardless of the client-specified target, it should at least log a warning when the requested book/edition is overridden. Silently re-parenting a manual import is data corruption from the API consumer's perspective — especially since duplicate records tend to get cleaned up later, which orphans the mis-attached `BookFile` rows entirely (we had to re-point two rows via SQL and delete the duplicates manually to restore a consistent library).

**System Information:**

 - OS: Docker on Unraid
 - Chaptarr Version: 0.9.965.0
 - Installation Method: Docker
 - Download clients: NZBGet, qBittorrent

**Logs**

Relevant debug lines included above. Happy to provide fuller logs on request.

**Additional context**

Workaround: re-point `BookFile.EditionId` to the intended edition and delete the duplicate book record. Suspected area: `ManualImportService` / `ImportApprovedBooks` — the file appears to be re-parsed and matched against parsed titles rather than honoring the client-specified book/edition.

---

*This report was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed by the reporter before filing.*

comments.body:
Checked against `develop` (e67374f). The duplicates were most likely created by the import, not by a refresh. When a book has a pinned edition (`AnyEditionOk=false`) or a `ManualAdd` edition that differs from the one you select, `ImportApprovedBooks` ([L384-427](https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/e67374f4b3fed01bbf08f18672add944062fcb49/src/NzbDrone.Core/MediaFiles/BookImport/ImportApprovedBooks.cs#L384-L427)) copies the book and the selected edition into a new row and imports there. 12938/12939 and 32214/32215 being consecutive fits that. Could you grep your debug log for `[MANUAL-EDITION-PROTECTION]` around those imports to confirm?

That branch is meant to keep automatic matching from overriding a pin. It shouldn't override an explicit manual selection. This has a different cause from #111.

Confirmed — and it corrects a premise in the report. The clones were created by the import itself, not by an author refresh. Debug log (`ImportApprovedBooks`):

```
2026-10-03 23:43:53.7|Debug|ImportApprovedBooks|[MANUAL-EDITION-PROTECTION] User pinned edition 25115 ('Golden Son (Part 1 of 2) (Dramatized Adaptation): Red Rising Saga, Book 2') but file(s) matched to different edition(s). Creating clone to preserve user's selection.
2026-10-03 23:43:54.2|Debug|ImportApprovedBooks|[MANUAL-EDITION-PROTECTION] Created new book instance ID: 12937 for files not matching pinned edition
2026-10-03 23:45:06.9|Debug|ImportApprovedBooks|[MANUAL-EDITION-PROTECTION] User pinned edition 25115 ... Creating clone to preserve user's selection.
2026-10-03 23:45:07.2|Debug|ImportApprovedBooks|[MANUAL-EDITION-PROTECTION] Created new book instance ID: 12938 for files not matching pinned edition
2026-10-03 23:53:56.5|Debug|ImportApprovedBooks|[MANUAL-EDITION-PROTECTION] User pinned edition 23578 ('Dark Age') but file(s) matched to different edition(s). Creating clone to preserve user's selection.
2026-10-03 23:53:56.7|Debug|ImportApprovedBooks|[MANUAL-EDITION-PROTECTION] Created new book instance ID: 12939 for files not matching pinned edition
```

12938/12939 (and 32214/32215 as their editions) being consecutive fits exactly what you described — import-created clones.

Two follow-ups:

1. Both ManualImport commands carried explicit `bookId`/`editionId` in the payload (10317/25858, then 9865/23583). Should an explicitly-specified payload target bypass the protection branch (no re-match, no clone), or is the pinned-edition check expected to run regardless? Today the explicit IDs lose, which is what made the outcome read as silent remapping.

2. When the branch fires, the file lands on a copy of the selection under a newly created duplicate book row. From the operator's seat that outcome is indistinguishable from the #111-style duplicates — cleanup (deleting what looked like a refresh duplicate) orphaned the BookFiles and needed an SQL re-point. Would an Info-level "imported to cloned book X because file matched edition Y" be reasonable, so clone creation is visible without debug logging?

Library is currently consistent — the two BookFile rows were re-pointed via SQL and the duplicate book rows deleted.

items.title: [BUG] Multi-narrator 'Full Cast' naming collapse + tag-dependent IsGraphicAudio detection make regular and dramatized editions path-identical, and upgrade-delete silently removes the other product
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

Two related behaviors in Chaptarr's organizer and upgrade-delete path combined to permanently destroy files from *two different products* of the same book. We lost a Golden Son GraphicAudio Part 2 file and a Dark Age GraphicAudio file (permanently — no recycle bin), caused by the sequence below. Both can coexist only if their computed destination paths differ, and in specific cases they don't.

**Behavior 1 — narrator-token collapse makes two products path-identical**

`FileNameBuilder.AddNarratorTokens` collapses any edition with more than two narrators to the literal "Full Cast" in the folder name. Books with genuinely multi-narrator regular editions (Iron Gold, Dark Age) therefore compute the same folder/file path as their dramatized (GraphicAudio) counterparts, because both collapse to "Full Cast" and the `{Book Title}` token is identical. The `graphicAudioSuffix` is appended only when the `BookFile.IsGraphicAudio` flag is true — which leads to behavior 2.

**Behavior 2 — `IsGraphicAudio` is not reliably set on import, so the suffix never applies**

The flag comes from `DetectGraphicAudioFromLocalTags` (embedded tags) and title parsing at import time. A GraphicAudio file whose tags don't advertise it (our Dark Age GA m4b, grabbed via SABnzbd) imported with `IsGraphicAudio=false`, so it computed the *same path* as the regular edition: `Dark Age - Full Cast/Dark Age.m4b`. Nothing in the ManualImport payload can set this flag — it's not exposed on the BookFile API resource — so the operator cannot force it at import time.

**Combined effect — the actual data loss**

When a regular edition was later imported onto the same book (an upgrade in Chaptarr's view), the upgrade-delete path removed the file occupying the computed destination — the GraphicAudio file — and imported the regular file over it. The GA file was permanently deleted (no recycle bin configured). The same collision later struck in reverse during a manual restore: importing the GA file with `replaceExistingFiles=true` overwrote the regular file at the same computed path. Two products of the same book cannot coexist, and in both directions the loser is silently, permanently deleted.

**To Reproduce**

1. Author a book whose regular edition has >2 narrators (e.g. Pierce Brown, Dark Age). Its computed folder is `Dark Age - Full Cast/`.
2. Obtain a dramatized/GraphicAudio edition of the same book whose embedded tags do not identify it (or whose import path doesn't detect it). Import it via ManualImport. Its computed destination is also `Dark Age - Full Cast/Dark Age.m4b` — identical.
3. Import the regular edition onto the same book with `replaceExistingFiles=true`. The GA file at the shared path is deleted; the regular file takes its place. No warning that the destination belonged to a different product.

**Expected behavior**

- Two products of the same book (regular vs dramatized adaptation) should never compute identical destination paths. Options: include `AudioProductionType`/`IsGraphicAudio` in the default naming tokens when set; or treat a destination occupied by a file flagged as a different production type as an occupied-destination conflict (reject/warn) rather than an upgrade to replace.
- Upgrade-delete should not silently remove a file that is not a prior copy of the same product.
- `IsGraphicAudio` / production type should be settable through the BookFile API resource or ManualImport payload, so operators can correct misdetections without SQL.

**System Information:**

 - OS: Docker on Unraid
 - Chaptarr Version: 0.9.965.0
 - Installation Method: Docker
 - Download clients: NZBGet, qBittorrent, SABnzbd

**Logs**

Debug-log evidence from the session is available on request (import decision lines, `[CLEAN-IMPORT]` skips, computed paths both before and after the flag was set via SQL).

**Additional context**

We recovered both files from out-of-pipeline sources (the original torrent download dir; a re-grab via SABnzbd), set `IsGraphicAudio=true` via SQL on the BookFile rows, and Chaptarr's own rename then moved them to distinct `… - GraphicAudio …` folders — confirming the suffix mechanism works and the missing flag was the trigger. The recurring collision, though, is the "Full Cast" collapse plus tag-dependent detection: any multi-narrator regular book with an undetected dramatized counterpart is one upgrade away from silent permanent deletion.

---

*This report was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed by the reporter before filing.*

comments.body:
Checked against `develop` (e67374f). The "Full Cast" collapse, the suffix depending only on `BookFile.IsGraphicAudio`, and the flag not being on the API resource all check out. Manual import is also tag-only: it never looks at the filename or folder, so `... - GraphicAudio.m4b` doesn't set the flag.

The deletion isn't path-based, though. A manual import with `replaceExistingFiles=true` replaces every existing file on the book whatever its path ([L1070-1073](https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/e67374f4b3fed01bbf08f18672add944062fcb49/src/NzbDrone.Core/MediaFiles/BookImport/ImportApprovedBooks.cs#L1070-L1073)). An automatic import replaces files on the same edition unless the new file is lower quality. With both files on one book row, distinct paths wouldn't have prevented it. Was the first deletion (regular replacing GA) a manual import or an automatic one from a download?

Automatic. The first deletion (regular replacing GA) was the automatic import of a completed download, not a manual import:

```
2026-10-03 23:04:05.0|Info|ImportApprovedBooks|[NOTIFY] Published BookImportedEvent for 'Golden Son' (BookId=9863, Files=1, NewDownload=True)
2026-10-03 23:04:07.0|Warn|ImportApprovedBooks|[IMPORT-PATH-CONFLICT] Upgrade also found destination BookFileId=1897. Including every displaced row in the atomic replacement with EditionId=23578. Source=/data/usenet/complete/audiobooks/Pierce Brown - Red Rising 05 - Dark Age (Unabr - 64k [2019])/Dark Age.m4b Dest=/data/media/audiobooks/Pierce Brown/Dark Age - Full Cast/Dark Age.m4b
2026-10-03 23:04:07.5|Info|RecycleBinProvider|Recycling Bin has not been configured, deleting permanently. .../Dark Age - Full Cast/Dark Age.m4b.chaptarr-upgrade~8ae40561...
```

Same shape for Golden Son (GA Part 2 file, BookFile 3004, permanently deleted a minute earlier) and Iron Gold (file 1570) — all three events carry `NewDownload=True` with sources under `/data/usenet/complete/`.

So I agree with your reading: distinct paths wouldn't have prevented it while both files sat on the same book row. The `[IMPORT-PATH-CONFLICT]` line shows the occupied destination was explicitly detected ("Including every displaced row in the atomic replacement") and the replace proceeded anyway — the conflict check stops one row short of noticing the displaced file is a different product.

One thing I can't place: the replacement ran with `UpgradeAllowed=False` on the quality profile (`[UPGRADE-CHECK] replaceExisting=True, existingFiles.Any()=True, filesToReplace=True, UpgradeAllowed=False`) — equal-quality replacement proceeded. Is that `replaceExistingFiles` semantics winning over the profile, or should the profile have blocked it? Flagging it because it widens the blast radius of the row-scoped replace.

Remaining asks from the report still stand: production-type-aware naming tokens (or a conflict-on-different-production-type check), and `IsGraphicAudio` settable through the API/resource.

items.title: [BUG] {MediaInfo AudioBitRate} naming token always renders "0 kbps"
items.body: **Describe the bug** `{MediaInfo AudioBitRate}` in the book/file naming format always renders `0 kbps` for imported audiobooks. Originally reported on Discord with this Standard Book Format: ``` {Book Title}{ (MediaInfo AudioBitRate) }{ {Narrator}}/{Book Title}{ (PartNumber:smart)} ``` Reproduced on a dev instance. **To Reproduce** 1. Settings → Media Management → set the audiobook file format to include `{ (MediaInfo AudioBitRate) }` 2. Import an audiobook, or rename an existing one 3. The file or folder name contains `(0 kbps)` **Expected behavior** The token renders the file's actual bitrate, or is omitted when the bitrate is unknown. **Cause (from code)** - Import paths build `BookFile.MediaInfo` from duration only: `MediaDuration.CreateMediaInfo` / `ApplyToMediaInfo` (`ImportApprovedBooks.cs:1177`, `:1194`; `BookImportService.cs:414`, `:717`), and `new MediaInfoModel()` in `DiskScanService.cs:831`, `ImportOrchestratorV2.cs`, and `BookImportUnmappedFileHelper.cs`. `AudioBitrate` stays 0. - `MediaInfoExtractor.ExtractMediaInfo` does read the bitrate, but it's only called for Matroska quality detection, MP3→M4B source-bitrate selection, and the legacy `BookDurationService` backfill. Its result never reaches the stored `BookFile.MediaInfo` on import. - `MediaInfoFormatter.FormatAudioBitrate` returns `"0 kbps"` instead of an empty string when the bitrate is 0, so the `{ (…) }` optional-token wrapper never collapses. - The naming preview uses a hard-coded sample (`AudioBitrate = 875` in `FileNameSampleService.cs:84`), so the bug doesn't show in Settings. Likely the same for the other `MediaInfo` tokens (`AudioCodec` → `Unknown`, `AudioSampleRate` → `0kHz`, `AudioChannels`/`AudioBitsPerSample` → empty). This is from reading the code; those tokens weren't tested. **System Information:** - OS: Ubuntu 25.10 - Chaptarr Version: 0.9.965 (develop) - Installation Method: built from source

items.title: [BUG] Audiobook rename preview uses unexpected edition year and omits narrator
items.body:
# [BUG] Audiobook rename preview uses unexpected edition year and omits narrator

**Describe the bug**

An existing audiobook of *The Sirens of Titan* has a rename preview that substitutes a different year and drops the narrator. This appears related to edition selection or edition metadata, but the saved preview alone does not establish the cause.

**Observed example**

On Chaptarr 0.9.965, the saved 2026-10-04 rename preview shows:

```
Existing folder:
Kurt Vonnegut/2009 - The Sirens of Titan {Jay Snyder} [B002V8L3P0]

Proposed folder:
Kurt Vonnegut/2014 - Sirens of Titan
```

A same-day edition survey reports ten editions for this book and monitored edition ID 21082. This report describes the historical preview, not a fresh import reproduction. Existing folder labels express the intended audiobook identity; they are not proof of embedded file tags or of what evidence the import matcher received.

**Expected behavior**

For an audiobook whose metadata includes the appropriate narrated edition, the preview should use that edition's year and narrator. Could edition selection prefer audiobook-format candidates when the imported file is audio, and avoid selecting an ebook/physical edition when an appropriate audiobook candidate exists? The preferred policy would need to account for incomplete metadata and language preferences.

**System Information**

- Chaptarr: 0.9.965.0 (develop), Docker image `chaptarr/chaptarr:0.9.965`.
- Observation: saved rename-preview output and edition survey; no rename performed.

**Additional context / diagnostics**

This is distinct from series-label issue #34 and PR #48. PR #142 addresses language preference in edition selection; #262 concerns matching the book itself. A format preference may be adjacent to those changes, rather than a separate matcher redesign. This report does not request using folder ASINs as matching evidence.

The saved evidence does not include a complete import trace or raw edition-format rows, so it does not prove that the selected edition was an ebook. Please indicate which diagnostic fields would distinguish a selection problem from incomplete edition metadata; a controlled reproduction can then be collected without renaming the existing library.

comments.body:
The rename preview uses whichever edition the file is linked to. It doesn't choose one, so the question is why the file was matched to 21082. Can you post:

1. `GET /api/v1/bookfile?bookId=<bookId>` for this file: `editionId`, `narrator`, `durationSeconds`, `matchProvenance` (`matchedVia`, `mode`, and the signal lists)
2. `GET /api/v1/edition?bookId=<bookId>`: for all 10 editions, `id`, `title`, `readingFormatId`, `releaseDate`, `narrator`, `durationSeconds`, `asin`/`audibleASIN`, `language`
3. The file's narrator-related tags and its duration (`ffprobe -show_format`)

If `matchedVia` is `escape_hatch` and 21082 has `readingFormatId` 1 or 3, the matcher fell back to the ebook/print edition because no audiobook edition was backed by narrator tags or duration. If 21082 has `readingFormatId` 2, the edition's metadata is incomplete. Workaround for now: manually select the Jay Snyder edition for the file, then preview the rename again.

Thanks. The stored provenance matches the escape-hatch case you described: `matchedVia=escape_hatch`, with a conflicting reading-format signal identifying the selected catalog edition as ebook.

The file was manually pinned from edition **21082** to **21068**. The current database link is therefore 21068. The provenance below still carries the original match timestamp, `2026-10-04T02:46:22Z`; it should be read as the recorded import decision, rather than evidence of a fresh match after the pin.

### 1. Bookfile and provenance

`GET /api/v1/bookfile?bookId=13501` returns file ID 30. Its response omits the top-level `editionId`, `narrator` and `durationSeconds` fields, so these values were checked with a read-only query of the corresponding `BookFiles` row:

```json
{"id":30,"bookId":13501,"editionId":21068,"narrator":null,"durationSeconds":32679}
```

The following is a projection of the API's `matchProvenance`, retaining the decision fields and all four signal lists:

```json

  "matcherVersion": "evidence-v2.7-exact-group-spans",

  "matchedVia": "escape_hatch",
  "mode": "Balanced",
  "route": "author_scoped/embedded_tags",
  "summary": "Matched from file tags",
  "supportingSignals": [
    {"type":"title","scope":"edition","source":"embedded_tag","field":"MP4:©nam","observed":"The Sirens of Titan","expected":"Sirens of Titan","detail":"This logical field supplied title containment proof."},
    {"type":"title","scope":"edition","source":"embedded_tag","field":"MP4:©alb","observed":"The Sirens of Titan","expected":"Sirens of Titan","detail":"This logical field supplied title containment proof."}
  ],
  "conflictingSignals": [
    {"type":"reading_format","scope":"edition","source":"catalog","observed":"ebook","expected":"audiobook","detail":"A representative non-native edition was selected because no better native edition was proven."}
  ],
  "neutralSignals": [
    {"type":"duration","scope":"edition","source":"media_info","observed":"32679 seconds","expected":"0 seconds","detail":"The catalog edition has no usable duration."}
  ],
  "excludedSignals": [
    {"type":"ignored_tag","scope":"metadata","source":"embedded_tag","field":"COMMENT","detail":"This field was excluded from fuzzy/content matching by the shared tag policy."},
    {"type":"ignored_tag","scope":"metadata","source":"embedded_tag","field":"GENRE","detail":"This field was excluded from fuzzy/content matching by the shared tag policy."},
    {"type":"ignored_tag","scope":"metadata","source":"embedded_tag","field":"LANGUAGE","detail":"This field was excluded from fuzzy/content matching by the shared tag policy."},
    {"type":"ignored_tag","scope":"metadata","source":"embedded_tag","field":"MP4:©too","detail":"This field was excluded from fuzzy/content matching by the shared tag policy."},
    {"type":"ignored_tag","scope":"metadata","source":"embedded_tag","field":"SERIES","detail":"This field was excluded from fuzzy/content matching by the shared tag policy."}
  ]
}
```

### 2. All ten editions

These are the current values from `GET /api/v1/edition?bookId=13501`. A dash in the ASIN columns means the field was absent from the response; empty narrator strings are shown as `""`.

| id | title | readingFormatId | releaseDate | narrator | durationSeconds | asin | audibleASIN | language |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21068 | The Sirens of Titan | 2 | 2009-08-13T00:00:00Z | Jay Snyder | 33600 | B002V8L3P0 | B002V8L3P0 | eng |
| 21069 | The Sirens of Titan | 2 | 2015-08-04T00:00:00Z | Jay Snyder | 0 | — | — | eng |
| 21070 | The Sirens of Titan | 2 | 1959-01-01T00:00:00Z | Jay Snyder | 0 | — | — | eng |
| 21071 | The Sirens of Titan | 2 | 2011-01-01T00:00:00Z | Dennis Boutsikaris | 0 | — | — | eng |

| 21082 | Sirens of Titan | 3 | 2014-05-10T00:00:00Z | "" | 0 | — | — | und |

### 3. Audio duration and narrator-related tags

`ffprobe` of the actual file reports duration **32678.994286 seconds**. A probe restricted to `artist`, `album_artist`, `composer`, `narrator`, `performer` and `title` returned `artist=Kurt Vonnegut`; none of the other requested narrator-related keys were returned. There is no Jay Snyder narrator value in that projection. The provenance separately records the embedded title/album strings shown above.

Edition 21068 has a catalog duration of 33600 seconds, about 921 seconds longer than the file. The provenance only records the comparison against the selected edition's zero duration; it does not show whether 21068 was evaluated. Does this evidence fit the intended Balanced-mode fallback, and would an audiobook-only preference for existing audio files be an appropriate separate option?

Yes, that's the intended fallback. The file has no narrator tag, and its duration is 921s off 21068's, past the 2% tolerance (672s). With no audiobook edition proven, the matcher falls back to an ebook edition with a title match. Pinning 21068 should fix the preview, since narrator, year and title all come from the linked edition. Can you confirm?

Preferring an unproven audiobook edition over an ebook in that fallback seems reasonable, but changing the default is the maintainer's call.

comments.body:
Checked against `develop` (e67374f). Your logs show the cause. `/shelf`, and `/books` in Table or Overview view, both call `GET /api/v1/book?mediaType=…` with no author or book filter. That request loads the whole library into memory before it filters anything:

- `GetBooksForDisplay` calls `GetAllBooks()` ([L2234](https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/e67374f4b3fed01bbf08f18672add944062fcb49/src/NzbDrone.Core/Books/Services/BookService.cs#L2234)). That reads all 643,135 book rows, for both media types, and only then filters to the requested type in memory.
- It then calls `GetAllMonitoredEditions()` ([L2267](https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/blob/e67374f4b3fed01bbf08f18672add944062fcb49/src/NzbDrone.Core/Books/Services/BookService.cs#L2267)). That runs `SELECT * FROM Editions WHERE Monitored = true` across the whole library, wide JSON columns included (`Chapters`, `Images`, `Links`), before narrowing to the books it needs. Your `OutOfMemoryException` is thrown there.

This fails the same way on SQLite and Postgres, so switching databases and re-importing wouldn't have changed it. The thread-pool-starvation warnings come from the same memory pressure.

Related to #170 (item 3): same endpoint, but on a library about 8× smaller it was slow rather than out of memory. The `/api/v1/author` times in your log (50 s, then 143 s) fit #170 item 1.

Updated environmental info:
Version
0.9.965.0
.NET Core
Yes (10.0.12)
Docker
Yes
Database
Postgresql 18.6
Database Migration
107
AppData Directory
/config
Startup Directory
/app
Mode
Console
Uptime
01:29:05

db log entries taht may support report 170
EDT [25406] ERROR:  canceling statement due to user request
EDT [25406] STATEMENT:  SELECT "Editions".*
	 FROM "Editions"    WHERE ("Editions"."Monitored" = $1)
	   
EDT [25406] ERROR:  canceling statement due to user request
EDT [25406] STATEMENT:  SELECT "Editions".*
	 FROM "Editions"    WHERE ("Editions"."Monitored" = $1)

Two possible fixes, from smallest to largest:

~~**1. Make the general `/api/v1/book` path load only what it needs** (backend only). This should stop the crash.~~
~~- Filter by media type in SQL instead of calling `GetAllBooks()` and filtering in memory.~~
~~- Replace `GetAllMonitoredEditions()` with a query for the monitored editions of the books being returned. Leave out `Chapters`, which list mapping never reads and which is the largest column in `Editions` (129 of 219 MB in the #170 table). Read `Overview` only when `include=overview` is passed. `FindByBook` already chunks the IDs, but it also joins Book and Author on every edition, so this path needs its own leaner query.~~
~~- Load series links once: `GetAllBooks()` loads them, and `MapToResource` loads them again.~~

~~This roughly halves the rows read and drops the largest column. It still returns about 320k books for one media type in a single JSON response, which the server buffers in full and the browser holds in Redux. So it stops the crash but leaves the page slow.~~

**2. Page `/shelf` and the Table/Overview views on the server** (frontend and API). This fixes the slowness too.
- Table and Overview views can switch to the `/book/paged` and `/book/ids` endpoints that Posters view already uses for infinite scroll. Custom filters would need server-side support as well, or they'll keep loading the full list.
- `/shelf` shows one row per author, and it fetches every book only to work out which authors to list and what goes in each row. It could build the rows from the author list and load each author's books as the row scrolls into view. The existing `?authorId=` path is the heavy one, so that load needs a lean variant.

Fix 1 is small and safe to ship first. Fix 2 is the real fix for libraries this size.

Reproduced locally on a synthetic SQLite library the same size as yours (643,599 books, half audiobook and half eBook), with the .NET heap capped at 4 GB:

| Build | Request | Result | Time | Peak memory | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `develop` | `/api/v1/book?mediaType=audiobook&include=author` (Books page) | 500, `OutOfMemoryException` in `GetAllMonitoredEditions()`, same as your logs | 54 s | 4.3 GB | — |
| Fix 1 (local) | same | 200 | 100 s | 4.0 GB | 1.6 GB |
| Fix 1 (local) | `/api/v1/book?mediaType=audiobook` (Shelf page) | 200 | 46–129 s | 3.5 GB | 583 MB |

With fix 1 the server survives, but only just. The browser then runs out of memory parsing the 583 MB response on Shelf. So fix 1 on its own moves the failure from the server to the browser, and fix 2 (server-side paging) is needed for these pages to work at this size.

Correction to my earlier comment: the server doesn't buffer the response. `BufferingMiddleware` buffers request bodies only. The memory goes into loading the rows and building the resources.

Workaround for `/books` until there's a fix, tested on the same 643k-book repro: switch to **Posters** view and pick one of the built-in filters (All, Monitored, Unmonitored, Exists, Missing, Wanted). That combination loads books a page at a time through `/api/v1/book/paged` instead of the full list, and the page loads fine.

Table and Overview views, and custom filters, still load everything. `/shelf` has no equivalent yet.

Draft PRs for this, tested together on the 643k-book repro:

- #294 keeps the general `/api/v1/book` list from running the server out of memory (filters by media type in SQL, skips edition chapters).
- #295 loads the Bookshelf a few authors at a time as rows scroll into view.
- #296 pages the Books Table and Overview views on the server, like Posters already does.

With all three, `/books` (every view, built-in filters) and `/shelf` load normally and the server stayed under 1.3 GB. Custom filters on `/books` still load the full list.
25k files and 96k titles much better after filter, app stayed stable, new scrolling  interim method is stable, but end user scroll pause is a smidge invasive feeling.

items.title: [BUG] External EPUB renames create duplicate records and leave monitored originals missing
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

An external EPUB filename change within the same library root causes Rescan Folders to attach the file to a new book/edition record. The original monitored book then appears in Wanted → Missing even though the same matched edition remains in the library. A plain filesystem rename reproduces it; no BookOrbit integration is required.

**To reproduce**

1. Import a correctly matched EPUB and enable ebook monitoring on its book.
2. Rename the file without changing its contents or root:

   ```sh
   mv "/books/Author/Book/Original.epub" "/books/Author/Book/Renamed.epub"
   ```

3. Run Rescan Folders on the library root.
4. Inspect the original book's file association and Wanted → Missing.

**Expected behavior**

The renamed file remains on the original monitored book and edition. Genuine additional copies remain separate.

**Actual behavior**

The new path is attached to another book/edition record. The original has no files and is reported missing.

**Controls**

- The filesystem-rename reproduction retained file contents and the same provider edition identity.
- English title correction and author display reordering with automatic renaming disabled preserved IDs, path and the Missing list.
- Polish metadata saves, including a work also present in English, preserved separate ownership with renaming disabled. Rename-on controls reproduced false Missing status for both languages.
- A real BookOrbit metadata save also reproduces it when it renames the file.

**System information**

Linux, local filesystem, official Docker image, Chaptarr `0.9.965.0` (`develop`), standalone EPUBs.

**Additional context**

items.title: Docker healthcheck uses curl but image doesn't ship curl — container permanently 'unhealthy'
items.body:
## Bug

The Docker image's built-in healthcheck uses `curl`, but the image doesn't ship `curl` (or `wget`/`node`). The healthcheck therefore fails on **every** interval even when the app is perfectly healthy, and the container sits permanently at `(unhealthy)`  1000+ consecutive failed checks in my case.

## Impact

- False `unhealthy` status in `docker ps`.
- Any watchdog/auto-restart tool keyed on container health (autoheal, watchtower healthcheck mode, etc.) will bounce a perfectly healthy container on a loop.

## Reproduction

```bash
docker inspect chaptarr --format '{{json .Config.Healthcheck}}'
# {"Test":["CMD-SHELL","curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:8789/ping || exit 1"],...}

docker exec chaptarr sh -c 'command -v curl wget node'
# (nothing — none installed)

# from the host, the app itself is fine:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8789/ping
# 200
```

Version: chaptarr/chaptarr:latest (0.9.911.0, branch develop, build 2026-08-08).

## Suggested fix

The image does include `bash`, so a dependency-free check works:

```yaml
healthcheck:
  test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/8789"]
```

(or install curl in the image, or use the actual healthcheck endpoint via a tool that's present).

Workaround applied on my side: compose-level healthcheck override with the bash /dev/tcp form — container reports `healthy` on the first cycle.

items.title: [BUG] Renaming audiobook folders leaves untracked sidecars behind and races AudioBookShelf's watcher
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a rename moves an audiobook to a new folder, Chaptarr moves the audio files one by one and afterwards only moves the sidecars it tracks in `MetadataFiles`. Two things go wrong with an AudioBookShelf library on the same folders:

1. **Untracked sidecars stay behind.** Books imported through Manual Import have no `MetadataFiles` rows, so AudioBookShelf's `cover.jpg` / `metadata.json` (and anything like `.opf`, `desc.txt`) are left in the old folder while the audio moves away.
2. **Race with AudioBookShelf's folder watcher.** As soon as the first audio file lands in the new folder, AudioBookShelf sees a new folder, creates a new library item, scrapes it from scratch and writes its own `cover.jpg` / `metadata.json` there. When Chaptarr then moves the tracked sidecars, they collide:

```
Warn|MetadataService|Unable to move metadata file after rename: /media/audiobooks/Robin Hobb/L'Assassin royal/0.6 - Le prince batârd/cover.jpg: File already exists
Warn|MetadataService|Unable to move metadata file after rename: /media/audiobooks/Robin Hobb/L'Assassin royal/0.6 - Le prince batârd/metadata.json: File already exists
```

In both cases the curated metadata ends up orphaned in the old folder and AudioBookShelf treats the renamed book as a new, badly matched item instead of a rename.

**To Reproduce**

1. Have an audiobook folder with AudioBookShelf sidecars (`cover.jpg`, `metadata.json`) and ABS watching the library.
2. Change the naming format so the book folder changes (e.g. `{Book SeriesPosition}` → `{Book SeriesPosition:00}`), then run Rename for the author.
3. Either the sidecars stay in the old folder (untracked book), or ABS writes new ones in the destination first and the move fails with `File already exists` (tracked book).

**Expected behavior**

The sidecars follow the book, and a watcher sees the book folder renamed rather than a new folder filling up.

**Environment**

Chaptarr 0.9.965 (Docker), library on an rclone mount, AudioBookShelf with its folder watcher enabled.

items.title: [FEATURE] Configurable Audible marketplace (audible.fr, .de, .co.uk…) instead of hardcoded audible.com
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

`AudibleCatalogProxy` hardcodes `https://api.audible.com` (plus `www.audible.com` for links, `Origin` and `Referer`, and `Accept-Language: en-US`). For a non-US library, the Audible search provider and ASIN lookups query the wrong catalog, and local-language audiobooks simply aren't found.

Example with a French library:

| ASIN | api.audible.fr | api.audible.com |
|---|---|---|
| `B0H417971Y` (Solo Leveling, French audiobook, tome 1) | ✅ found, with series "Solo Leveling (French Edition) #1" | ❌ absent |

The same catalog endpoints (`/1.0/catalog/products/{asin}`, product search) work unchanged on the other marketplaces; only the domain differs.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A setting for the Audible marketplace (us, uk, fr, de, it, es, ca, au, in, jp, br) that drives:
- the API host (`api.audible.<tld>`);
- the generated product links (`www.audible.<tld>/pd/<asin>`);
- the `Origin`/`Referer`/`Accept-Language` headers.

Ideally the setting would also reach the metadata server, so that author catalogs and `az:` editions come from the user's marketplace. Today they also come from the US catalog, which mixes in editions that don't exist locally and misses local-only audiobooks.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

As a local patch, I read the marketplace from an environment variable (`CHAPTARR_AUDIBLE_REGION=fr`) in `AudibleCatalogProxy`. It works: the Audible search provider then returns `az:B0H417971Y`. But a proper setting (per instance, or tied to the metadata profile's language) would be cleaner, and it wouldn't cover the server side.

**Additional context**

Running two instances (French and English audiobooks), so a per-instance setting is enough.

items.title: [BUG] Metadata server merges distinct Audible volumes of a series into one work (Solo Leveling FR tomes 2–4 under gr:183187350)
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

The author catalog returned by the metadata server folds several **distinct volumes** of an Audible series into a single work. Each volume is a separate product on Audible, with its own ASIN, release date and series sequence, but Chaptarr only shows one book for all of them, and the remaining volumes can't be added at all.

Example: author CHUGONG (`hc:245256`), French audiobook series **Solo Leveling (French Edition)**, Audible series `B0H474JJ3H` on audible.fr.

| Audible.fr | ASIN | Release | In Chaptarr |
|---|---|---|---|
| Solo Leveling, Tome 1 (#1) | B0H417971Y | 2026-06-25 | own work `gr:293868336` ✅ |
| Solo Leveling, Tome 2 (#2) | B0H8T336DS | 2026-07-16 | edition `az:B0H8SY91X1` of work `gr:183187350` |
| Solo Leveling, Tome 3 (#3) | B0H95GR62X | 2026-08-06 | edition `az:B0H955RL6J` of work `gr:183187350` |
| Solo Leveling, Tome 4 (#4) | B0H958PYZH | 2026-08-27 | edition `az:B0H958PYZH` of work `gr:183187350`, plus a separate duplicate work `az:B0H954CH5Z` |

So `gr:183187350` ("Solo Leveling", shown as volume 2 of the Korean novel series) carries three audiobook editions that are really volumes 2, 3 and 4.

**Consequences**
- Only one book appears for volumes 2–4, so they can't be monitored, searched or imported separately.
- Adding volume 3 explicitly (Audible search → `az:B0H95GR62X` → Add) doesn't create a book: it resolves to the existing `gr:183187350` because the ASIN is an alias of that work.
- Importing files for two of those volumes would put them on the same book, and Rename would put them in the same folder.

**Expected behavior**

Editions with different series sequences (or different Audible product ASINs in the same series) shouldn't be clustered into one work. Volumes 2, 3 and 4 should be three books in the series, with positions 2–4.

**Environment**

Chaptarr 0.9.965 (Docker). The data above comes from `GET /api/v1/edition?bookId=…` and from `api.audible.fr/1.0/catalog/products/<asin>`.

items.title: [BUG] Upgrading from 0.9.911–0.9.928 re-monitors every author that was unmonitored (migration 104)
items.body:
Versions: upgraded from 0.9.911 (Docker latest at the time) to 0.9.965 (develop). SQLite.

What happens

After the upgrade, every author I had unmonitored shows as monitored again. On my library, 69 of 925 authors were unmonitored for audiobooks before the upgrade. Afterwards, all 925 have AudiobookMonitored = 1.

Cause

On 0.9.911–0.9.928, the UI decides an author is monitored from MonitorExisting only:

js
// frontend/src/Utilities/Author/getAuthorMediaTypeMonitoringStatus.js (v0.9.914)
export function isAuthorMonitoredForMediaType(author, mediaType) {
  return getAuthorMonitorExistingValue(author, mediaType) > 0;
}

The monitor toggle on those versions only writes audiobookMonitorExisting / ebookMonitorExisting (coerceMonitorExistingValue(monitored) in TOGGLE_AUTHOR_MONITORED). It leaves MonitorFuture at true. So an author unmonitored from the author list or the author page is stored as MonitorExisting = 0, MonitorFuture = 1.

Migration 104 (migrate_author_media_monitoring) counts MonitorFuture = TRUE as monitored:

sql
"AudiobookMonitored" = CASE
    WHEN "AudiobookMonitorExisting" IN (1, 2) OR "AudiobookMonitorFuture" = TRUE THEN TRUE
    WHEN "AudiobookMonitorExisting" = 0 THEN FALSE
    ...

Monitored uses the same rule. Every author unmonitored with the toggle therefore comes out as Monitored = 1, AudiobookMonitored = 1, AudiobookMonitorNewItems = 2.

That matches the UI from 0.9.929 on, which shows an author as monitored when MonitorExisting > 0 || MonitorFuture. It doesn't match 0.9.911–0.9.928, where MonitorFuture didn't affect the monitored state.

Reproduction
Take a database from 0.9.911 (migration 101) in which some authors were unmonitored with the toggle. In my backup, 69 authors have AudiobookMonitorExisting = 0, AudiobookMonitorFuture = 1 (3 of them also have EbookMonitorExisting = 0, EbookMonitorFuture = 0). None have 0, 0.
Start 0.9.965 on a copy of it (migrations 102–107 run).
SELECT AudiobookMonitored, COUNT(*) FROM Authors GROUP BY 1 returns 1 | 925. All 69 come out Monitored = 1, AudiobookMonitored = 1, AudiobookMonitorNewItems = 2.

Examples from my library: Aesop, Albert Einstein, Alexandre Dumas, Aristotle, Arthur C. Clarke, Arthur Conan Doyle.

Book rows aren't changed. Every Books.AudiobookMonitored / EbookMonitored value was identical before and after the migrations, and after refreshing 12 of the affected authors.

Suggested fix

The two legacy shapes can't be told apart from the columns alone:

Existing = 0, Future = 1 was "unmonitored" on 0.9.911–0.9.928.
On 0.9.929–0.9.936 it means "monitored, new books only".

Options:

Treat MonitorExisting = 0 as unmonitored (AudiobookMonitored = FALSE) and keep MonitorFuture only for AudiobookMonitorNewItems. This gets the 0.9.911–0.9.928 case right. On 0.9.929–0.9.936, a "new books only" author would come out unmonitored, but it keeps monitoring new books through MonitorNewItems.
Or decide by the database's last legacy migration, if one marks 0.9.929.

For users who already upgraded, a follow-up migration can't recover the old state, because 104 dropped the legacy columns. Release notes could point affected users to re-unmonitor those authors, or to restore a pre-upgrade backup.

Found with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code); I reviewed the findings before posting.

items.title: Upstream the remaining ChaptarrNG features needed by SeerrNG
items.body:
I maintain [ChaptarrNG](https://github.com/snapetech/chaptarrng) because [SeerrNG](https://github.com/snapetech/seerrng) still depends on a small set of integration and standalone features we carry there. I would rather have SeerrNG target supported Chaptarr releases and retire the fork if these changes are a fit upstream.

I reviewed Chaptarr `develop` at [e67374f](https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/commit/e67374f4b3fed01bbf08f18672add944062fcb49). The format-aware book routes, provider IDs, paged library reads, and pending-author-import operations are already there; I am not proposing to reimplement those.

## What SeerrNG needs

1. **A discoverable integration contract.** Chaptarr keeps the `Chaptarr` app identity for Readarr-compatible clients. SeerrNG needs a way to ask which provider-ID dialect and extended book operations this instance supports instead of inferring that from the app name or version. The proposed `GET /api/v1/system/capabilities` response describes that contract, including format-scoped routes, paging, provider identity, and pending-import support.

2. **A book-scoped service key.** SeerrNG handles requests and library state; it does not need Chaptarr's global settings, delete, file-removal, or unrelated administrative commands. An optional key limited to the book workflows SeerrNG uses lets an operator avoid sharing the full admin key. The existing API key keeps its current behavior.

These two pieces let SeerrNG safely select the right API behavior for ebook and audiobook requests while keeping provider identity intact and using least-privilege access.

## Other ChaptarrNG features

ChaptarrNG also carries encrypted full-backup archives. Full backups include the database and configuration, so they can contain credentials. The implementation makes encryption optional for new full backups using a passphrase from a mounted secret, while existing `.zip` backups remain restorable.

The built-in Direct Download indexer/client is another standalone ChaptarrNG feature. It already has an upstream proposal in [PR #36](https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/pull/36), so I am linking that work rather than opening a duplicate.

## Current ChaptarrNG implementations

I consolidated the earlier review branches after comparing them with the maintained fork: the capability/key and backup behavior already exist in ChaptarrNG `main`, while those branch snapshots were based on older code. I removed the redundant branch refs. These are permanent links to the implementation we maintain today; they are references for this discussion, not pull requests against Chaptarr:

- [Capability discovery and encrypted backup implementation (`865e0b1`)](https://github.com/snapetech/chaptarrng/commit/865e0b1)
- [Restricted SeerrNG service API key (`113c5ff`)](https://github.com/snapetech/chaptarrng/commit/113c5ff)
- [Current fork feature and replacement notes](https://github.com/snapetech/chaptarrng/blob/552b1982f471a14cbe1db3521d9c5c94a204efe2/docs/FORK_FEATURES.md)
- [Direct Download Indexer upstream proposal, PR #36](https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/pull/36)

## What would let us retire ChaptarrNG

For SeerrNG, a supported Chaptarr release would need to advertise the integration contract, preserve the required format/provider behavior, expose the scoped service key, and pass SeerrNG's integration checks. If we want to keep the fork's standalone Direct Download and encrypted full-backup features, those need to be available upstream too (or have an accepted replacement). We would then move SeerrNG and the fork-owned images/packages to the supported Chaptarr release line and verify the migration before retiring ChaptarrNG.

Would these pieces fit in Chaptarr? If the API shape or key scope should be different, I am happy to adjust the proposal to match the project's conventions.

So the renames are about 12% of the reviewable diff, not half. The 10,500 line total is also inflated by 2,420 lines of yarn.lock, and 2,381 of those sit inside the lodash commit, which is most of why it looks so big.

The review time is really in the jQuery to fetch commit (2,765 lines in frontend/src) and react-virtualized to react-window (2,411). Those two are 65% of the source churn and neither is renaming. The commit boundaries also don't match the commit messages, which is what made this hard to follow: QueueRow.js (873 lines), HistoryRow.js (410), BlocklistRow.js (315), AuthorEditorRow.js (225) and IgnoredDownloadRow.js (178) are class to functional component conversions sitting inside the commit titled "replace jQuery AJAX with native fetch", and the new 123-line sw.js is inside the one titled "add React Query for server state management".

Four bugs, all in the parts I actually read:

1. dayjs is missing the isBetween plugin. dayjsSetup.js extends relativeTime, duration, weekOfYear, isoWeek and customParseFormat, and isInNextWeek.js line 8 calls dayjs(date).isBetween(...). moment had isBetween built in, dayjs needs the plugin, and nothing else registers it transitively (I checked against 1.11.21 with exactly those five plugins). The throw happens on the call, not on the range test, so getRelativeDate.js line 36 blows up for every date that isn't yesterday, today or tomorrow, past dates included. That's 9 consumers including RelativeDateCell, TimeleftCell and DayOfWeek, and ShowRelativeDates defaults to true in ConfigService.cs line 518, so it's on unless someone turned it off. The rest of the dayjs plugin surface looks fine, .from, .fromNow and .duration are all covered.

2. createAjaxRequest never populates responseJSON. It sets responseText, status, statusText and aborted, and there are about 50 reads of xhr.responseJSON left across 22 files. Five other sites build a responseJSON themselves and still work, so this only affects errors coming back from a real request. No crash, every deref is behind an optional chain or a truthiness check, but getErrorMessage always returns its fallback string, and at SpinnerErrorButton.js line 26 a 400 gives some(undefined, ...) twice, so hasWarning and hasError both come out false and the button shows no error state at all rather than the validation failures.

3. A timeout is indistinguishable from a user abort. The timeout calls abortRequest() on the same AbortController, fetch rejects with an AbortError, and line 154 sets aborted: true on it. 13 call sites then do `error: xhr.aborted ? null : xhr` and discard it. createFetchHandler.js is the clearest one: it dispatches isFetching false, isPopulated false and error null together, so the section renders an empty state with no error and no retry rather than surfacing the timeout. Only AudioBookShelfLibraryMappings.js line 241 passes a timeout today (10 seconds), so it's narrow now, but it's a trap for the next one.

4. There's a semantic change inside the lodash commit. InteractiveImportModalContent.js line 220 rewrote `_(items).filter(...).keyBy((x) => x.book.id).map((x) => x.book).value()` as `mapValues(keyBy(...), (x) => x.book)`. Lodash map over a keyed object returns an array, mapValues returns an object, so booksImported changes from array to object. It initializes to [] at line 154 and goes to ConfirmImportModalContent at line 623, whose propType at line 126 is arrayOf, so that's a propType warning. It still works because the consumer uses lodash find, which takes objects. Six of the seven chain rewrites in that commit wrap in values() correctly and this one doesn't, which is why I don't think that commit can be reviewed as renames.

Two smaller ones: jquery 3.7.1 is still in package.json line 58 with no imports left in frontend/src, and the sw.js comment at line 59 flags sub-path urlBase deployments as unhandled and needing live-server testing, so that's worth pinning down before it ships, though subdomain installs at the root are unaffected.

What I did not look at: the react-window migration, the 37 lazy routes and the react-query commit, which is 3,791 lines between them. Treat it as unreviewed. It's also the part most likely to change behaviour in ways that clicking through wouldn't catch. The Build Chaptarr workflow has also been sitting at action_required on both pushes, so someone needs to approve the run before CI has said anything either way.

Not my repo and not my call, but if jQuery to fetch and react-window went out as their own PRs with the row conversions kept separate, I'd happily review both properly. Is there a reason the two need to land together?
