items.title: feature(metadata-profile): add IgnoredGenres filter (e.g. exclude comics/graphic novels)
items.body:
#### Description

The metadata source (Hardcover, via `BookInfoProxy`) already returns genre tags for every book, and `Book.Genres` already stores them - but nothing in `MetadataProfileService.FilterBooks` ever reads that field. There was no way to exclude books by genre/format (comics, graphic novels, etc.) at the profile level, only by deleting each affected author manually after the fact once their books were already added and files already downloaded.

Confirmed this is real data, not speculative, against real stored rows in a library:

```
"Superman - Action Comics (2011-2016) #49" -> ["Comics", "Superman"]
"Dungeons & Dragons" -> ["Comics", "Graphic novels", "Graphic Novels Comics", ...]
"Action 50th Anniversary Special" -> ["COMIC BOOK."]
```

Adds `MetadataProfile.IgnoredGenres` (`List<string>`), matching the shape of the existing `Ignored` title-term list for API/UI consistency, but kept as a separate list since genre tags are discrete values to match exactly (case-insensitive), not free text to pattern-match. A book is filtered out if any of its `Genres` matches any entry in `IgnoredGenres`. Wired into `FilterBooks` alongside the existing rating/date/omnibus/series/title-term predicates.

No frontend changes in this PR - the field is settable via the API today (same as most other profile fields before their UI control existed). Happy to add the UI control as a follow-up if that's wanted before merge.

Fixes #176

#### Database Migration
YES - migration 108 adds `MetadataProfiles.IgnoredGenres` (string column, JSON-serialized list, default `"[]"`), so existing profiles are unaffected until a user opts in.

#### How was this tested?
- New cases in `MetadataProfileServiceMediaTypeFilteringFixture`: books matching an ignored genre are excluded, matching is case-insensitive, and an empty `IgnoredGenres` list filters nothing (default/backward-compat safety).
- Full `Chaptarr.Core.Test` suite (3,031 tests) passes.
- Deployed to a live instance, migration applies cleanly (`\d MetadataProfiles` shows the new column, default `[]`), and the field round-trips correctly through the API (`GET /api/v1/metadataprofile` returns `ignoredGenres` on every profile). Created a real test profile via the API with `ignoredGenres: ["Comics", "Graphic novels", "Graphic Novels Comics", "COMIC BOOK."]`, assigned it to a real author with a comic-tagged book in their remote catalogue (deleted the local rows first so a refresh has to re-decide whether to re-add it), and triggered a live refresh end-to-end: **confirmed working** - the comic-tagged book ("Duncan & Mallory", `Genres: ["Comics", "Graphic novels", ...]`) was correctly excluded and did not come back, where before this fix it was re-added on every refresh regardless of the profile setting. (First pass at this test gave a false negative - the book turned out to be catalogued as an audiobook, and I'd only pointed the author's *ebook* metadata profile at the test profile; pointing the audiobook profile at it too and re-running confirmed the real fix works as intended.)

items.title: Requesting one format doesn't monitor the sibling, even with format sync on
items.body:
#### Description

"Sync Monitored Across Formats" is supposed to mean: monitor the ebook, and the audiobook gets monitored too (or vice versa). It only half works. Toggling an *existing* book's monitored flag reconciles the sibling correctly — that path has been solid since it shipped. But a book that arrives **already monitored**, which is exactly what every book request does (`POST /api/v1/book` with `monitored: true`), never goes through any of the four methods the reconciliation is wired into (`SetBookMonitored`, `SetMonitored`, `UpdateBook`, `UpdateMany`). Its monitored flag is set once, inline, at insert time — so the sibling is left behind, silently, even on an author with sync fully configured.

<details>
<summary>Technical detail</summary>

`BookService.AddBook` inserts the row, sets `newBook.Monitored` from the caller, publishes `BookAddedEvent`, and returns. None of that touches `GetSyncUpdatesForMutations`, the private helper the four existing mutation methods all call. Confirmed on a real library: an audiobook was requested and owned; its ebook sibling sat on the same Goodreads work id, unmonitored, with the author's `SyncMonitoredAcrossFormats` correctly `true` — and nothing ever reconciled it, because nothing ever called one of the four methods for that row after its creation.

`BulkSyncFormatMonitoringCommand` exists specifically to reconcile this kind of drift after the fact, but nothing in the app invokes it automatically — not on add, not on refresh, not on a schedule. It's dead code unless someone calls it manually via `POST /api/v1/command`.

</details>

**What this does.** Runs the insert through the exact same reconciliation the four existing methods already share: build a clone of the new book with both format-monitored flags forced to `false` as the "prior" state, and hand `(newBook, priorState)` to `GetSyncUpdatesForMutations`. From the reconciliation's point of view this looks identical to "a book just became monitored" — which is the true story — so it produces the same sibling update it always would have.

**Deliberate choices worth flagging for review**

- **This only closes the single-book insert path.** A book that arrives via bulk catalog import (an author refresh discovering their back-catalog, all unmonitored by design) still isn't covered — `InsertMany` was never one of the four sync-triggering methods, and this PR doesn't add it there. I chose the narrower fix because it's the path every book request goes through (`AddBookService.AddBook` → `BookService.AddBook`), so it's the one that matters for a site that lets people request books; the bulk-import path only matters in the rarer sequence where a refresh discovers a new sibling for a work whose other format is *already* monitored outside of a request. That's the case I found the original bug in, historically — I fixed the data for it by hand — but I don't have evidence it recurs going forward the same way, since a freshly-requested author's other books are typically all-unmonitored on both sides when refresh later fills them in (nothing to sync against yet). Happy to extend this into `InsertMany` too if you'd rather close the whole surface in one PR.
- The diff is 25 lines in one file, `BookService.cs`, plus tests. Nothing else changes.

**Blast radius.** `AddBook` is the single insertion point for both the manual "add a book" UI flow and every programmatic book request. The new call is a no-op whenever the book isn't monitored, or the author has sync off, or there's no sibling row to reconcile — which is true for the overwhelming majority of inserts (most new books are catalog-only, unmonitored, or the sibling doesn't exist yet).

#### Database Migration

NO.

#### How was this tested?

Four tests, written first and watched failing for the right reason:

```
Failed add_book_should_monitor_the_unmonitored_sibling_format
  the pre-existing ebook sibling should have been monitored by the sync
  Expected: True
  But was:  False
Failed!  - Failed: 4, Passed: 0
```

(All four failed initially — the other three assert `AddBook` should *not* touch the sibling under specific conditions — sync off, the new book itself unmonitored, no sibling at all — and those only started passing once the surrounding infrastructure in the test double was wired up correctly; once fixed, all three passed unmodified before the actual code change, confirming they're real regression guards and not accidentally-passing assertions.)

```
develop (7a06004): 3020 passed  →  this branch: 3024 passed (+4), 0 failed
```

| CI step | Result |
|---|---|
| conflict-marker guard | clean |
| `package.json` parses | ok |
| `version_guard.py` sync / monotonic / commit-hygiene | ok / ok / ok |
| `dotnet build src/Chaptarr.NoTests.sln -c Release` | 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| `dotnet test` | 3024 passed |

No frontend files are touched, so the yarn steps aren't applicable.

**On a real instance:** deployed to my own instance, cherry-picked on top of several other local branches (see that branch's own commit history — one of them adds `Author.AudiobookMonitorExisting`/`EbookMonitorExisting` and an extra `> 0` gate on top of upstream's simpler sync-enable rule; the cherry-picked copy of this PR's test carries one additional commit setting those fields so the test proves the fix against what that build actually gates on, without changing the PR itself). The specific historical gap (an owned, monitored audiobook with an unmonitored ebook sibling on the same work id, sync on) was corrected by hand via the existing `PUT /book/monitor` endpoint — proving *that* endpoint's reconciliation already worked correctly; this PR's job is only to make a fresh insert behave the same way going forward.

**What I did not test.** I did not add coverage for the bulk-import (`InsertMany`) path — see the deliberate-choices note above. I also did not exercise this through the full HTTP `POST /api/v1/book` request path in a test (only through `BookService.AddBook` directly); the controller layer between them does no monitoring-relevant work, so I don't expect a difference, but I haven't proven it in a test.

#### Screenshots (UI changes only)

None. No UI changes.

items.title: perf(covers): skip per-book cover reconciliation when a refresh made no changes
items.body:
#### Description

`MediaCoverService.HandleAsync(AuthorRefreshCompleteEvent)` unconditionally re-fetches every book (+ eagerly hydrated editions) for the author again via `GetBooksByAuthor`, then runs `EnsureBookCovers` on each one - disk-cache checks across every rendition, and on any miss a synchronous HTTP fetch + resize - on every single `RefreshAuthor` completion, including pure no-op re-scans of an already-fully-synced catalogue. For large catalogues (e.g. an author with several thousand books) that's a redundant full re-query plus thousands of per-book operations running after every refresh, competing for I/O/CPU with anything else in flight.

Threads an `AnyChanges` flag through `PublishRefreshCompleteEvent` -> `AuthorRefreshCompleteEvent`, sourced from the same "did anything change" bool `RefreshEntityInfo` already computes for `PublishEntityUpdatedEvent`. When a refresh found no changes at all, `MediaCoverService` now skips the re-fetch and per-book loop entirely - nothing about any book's title/editions/images could have moved. `AnyChanges` defaults to `true`, so the other 6 `AuthorRefreshCompleteEvent` publishers (import/discovery flows) keep today's always-reconcile behavior unchanged.

#### Database Migration
NO

#### How was this tested?
- Full `Chaptarr.Core.Test` suite (3,020 tests) passes.
- Deployed to a live instance and confirmed the skip path actually fires: with logging temporarily bumped to Info, a refresh that found real changes reconciled covers as before, and a refresh with `AnyChanges=false` correctly skipped the per-book loop and logged the skip.
- Note: on the specific author I used for that live check, a separate pre-existing bug (see the companion PR making match-claim order deterministic) meant `AnyChanges` rarely settled to `false` in practice for that author. This PR's own logic (the skip itself, and that it doesn't regress the other 6 callers) is verified regardless of that separate issue.

#### Screenshots (UI changes only)
N/A - no frontend changes in this PR.

items.title: fix(books): make remote-item match-claim order deterministic during author refresh
items.body:
#### Description

When several remote pockets share the same title (e.g. multiple "Dune" editions from different sources/print runs), \`GetMatchingExistingChildren\` -> \`BookRefreshMatchingIndex.Consume\` lets whichever remote item is processed first claim a given ambiguous local row, removing it from the candidate pool for every later remote item. The final tie-break within a single candidate set (\`HasKnownFiles\`, \`AddType\`, provider score, then \`Id\`) is already deterministic, but the order remote items arrive in was whatever the metadata source's response happened to be for that call - not guaranteed stable request to request.

Confirmed live against a real author (363 books) with several ambiguously-titled duplicate rows: refreshing the same already-synced author back to back reported books being matched/unmatched inconsistently between runs purely due to claim order, even with zero real catalogue changes in between.

Adds \`OrderRemoteChildrenForMatching\`, a virtual hook on \`RefreshEntityServiceBase\` (default no-op, so \`RefreshBookService\`'s nested edition refresh is unaffected) that \`RefreshAuthorService\` overrides to sort remote books by their own stable provider-identity token before the match loop runs. Claim order - and therefore the outcome - is now a function of the data itself, not of call-to-call API response order.

**Note:** while investigating a "same author reports N books changed on every single refresh" symptom, this fix turned out not to be the (or at least not the only) cause for that specific symptom - the claimed set was identical run over run for that author, not flapping between different sets, which pointed at a separate root cause (a title-metadata field not persisting on write) that's still under investigation. This PR stands on its own as a real correctness fix for the ambiguous-title-ordering case regardless.

#### Database Migration
NO

#### How was this tested?
- New tests in \`RefreshAuthorServiceMonitoringFixture\`: same candidate set in forward/reversed/shuffled input order produces identical output order, and the sort never drops or duplicates books (including ones with no provider tokens at all).
- Full \`Chaptarr.Core.Test\` suite (3,022 tests) passes.
- Deployed to a live instance; confirmed the new ordering is applied and is stable across repeated calls for the same input set.

#### Screenshots (UI changes only)
N/A - no frontend changes in this PR.

items.title: fix(books): use the author-refresh match instead of independently re-deriving it
items.body:
#### Description

RefreshAuthorService's SortChildren already decides, once, which remote item matches each local book (`GetMatchingExistingChildren`) - that decision is what buckets a book as Added/Updated/UpToDate/Deleted. But when the actual per-book refresh runs, `RefreshBookService.GetRemoteData` throws that decision away and independently re-derives its own match via `BookIdentity.FindWorkFirstMatches(...).FirstOrDefault()` over the same raw remote list.

When the remote list has more than one plausible candidate for a book (e.g. the metadata source returning multiple entries that share a provider id), these two passes can disagree. Confirmed live: a book correctly classified as changed (SortChildren's comparison found a real difference) never actually got the field written, refresh after refresh, because `GetRemoteData`'s own separate match resolved to a different candidate.

Adds `SortedChildren.MatchedRemoteByLocalId` (populated where the match is actually decided, in `SortChildren`) and threads it through a new, non-interface `RefreshBookInfo` overload - same reasoning as `BookService.UpdateMany`'s existing hint overload: adding a parameter to `IRefreshBookService` would break every hand-written test double, so `RefreshAuthorService` holds a concrete `RefreshBookService` reference check instead. `GetRemoteData` consults the hint first and only falls back to independent re-derivation when there isn't one for that book id, so every other `RefreshBookInfo` caller (imports, discovery, manual single-book refresh) is completely unaffected.

This is one of three related fixes (companion PRs make match-claim order deterministic, and fix a separate comparison-vs-apply mismatch); together they resolve a "books reported as changed on every single refresh, forever" symptom I found while investigating a cover-reconciliation performance issue.

#### Database Migration
NO

#### How was this tested?
- New tests in `RefreshBookServiceProviderMatchingFixture`: with an ambiguous remote list (two candidates that both legitimately match by provider id and media type), a hint pointing at either candidate is honored regardless of list order; a hint entry for a different book id is correctly ignored and falls back to normal matching.
- Full `Chaptarr.Core.Test` suite (3,022 tests) passes.
- Deployed to a live instance alongside the two companion fixes and confirmed via live logging that a book's match now resolves consistently between the classification pass and the actual update pass.

#### Screenshots (UI changes only)
N/A - no frontend changes in this PR.

comments.body: Found in an adversarial review of #218: this PR's per-call hint was an instance field on the singleton RefreshBookService, justified by 'only one disk-access command runs at a time', but RefreshAuthorCommand neither requires disk access nor is type exclusive, so per-author refreshes run concurrently (3 by default, more with #222). One refresh could read another author's hint, and the finally block cleared it under a refresh still using it. Added a commit that holds the hint in an AsyncLocal (property backing, call sites unchanged) and a deterministic two-flow test that fails with a shared field.

items.title: fix(books): compare against the simulated update result, not the raw remote payload
items.body:
#### Description

`AreChildrenUpToDate` compared local straight against a cloned remote item. But `Book.UseMetadataFrom` - the method that actually applies a change - non-destructively coalesces several fields rather than blindly overwriting: `Title`/`Overview` only replace a non-empty local value, `ReleaseDate` only replaces a non-null one, `SeriesName`/`SeriesPosition` use `??` against the existing value, `Images` only replace when the remote side has a usable URL.

A remote payload that simply doesn't carry one of these fields for a given book (e.g. an author-scoped refresh batch with no series data for it, even though an earlier richer fetch populated it locally) makes the raw compare see "populated" != "empty" and report a difference - one a real update would never actually apply. Confirmed live: a book's `SeriesName`/`SeriesPosition` differed between local and the author-scoped remote payload on every single refresh, so it stayed classified as changed forever without ever converging, even though nothing about it would ever actually change.

Compares local against what local would actually become if updated (a clone of local with the same non-destructive `UseMetadataFrom` applied) instead of against the untouched remote clone, so the comparison and the apply are governed by the exact same coalescing rules and can't disagree.

This is the fix that actually resolves the underlying symptom (two companion PRs - deterministic match order, and using the author-refresh match instead of re-deriving it - fix real but secondary issues found along the way). Verified live: an author whose refresh reported the same 13 books "changed" on every single run, indefinitely, now reports 0 after this fix, stable across repeated refreshes.

#### Database Migration
NO

#### How was this tested?
- New tests in `RefreshAuthorServiceMonitoringFixture`: a book whose only "difference" from remote is a field the remote payload omits (and `UseMetadataFrom` would therefore never actually overwrite) is correctly treated as up to date; a book with a genuine difference (e.g. title) is still correctly detected as changed.
- Full `Chaptarr.Core.Test` suite (3,025 tests) passes.
- Deployed to a live instance: an author that reliably reported "13 books updated, 12 deleted" on every single refresh (confirmed via temporary logging to be the exact same 13 books each time, not a flapping set) now reports 0 updated across two consecutive refreshes.

#### Screenshots (UI changes only)
N/A - no frontend changes in this PR.

items.title: Don't split a book when its files were replaced in place
items.body:
#### Description

When another tool replaces a book's files in the same folder, one rescan splits the book. Audiobookshelf's M4B encoder is the common case: it writes one M4B next to the MP3s and moves the MP3s away. After the rescan, the new file sits on a newly created copy of the book, and the original stays monitored with no files, so it goes back into Wanted → Missing and can be downloaded again.

**Cause.** `DiskScanService` runs the import before it cleans up files that have disappeared. So when `BookUnitDestinationService.ResolveDestinationForUnit` decides where the M4B goes, the MP3 rows are still in the database. The unit key includes the container extension on purpose, so that an MP3 copy and an M4B copy of the same book can be kept side by side. The M4B's `…|.m4b` doesn't match the MP3 rows' `…|.mp3`, so the method clones the book and the edition. Seconds later the cleanup deletes the MP3 rows.

**Fix.** Rows for files that are gone from the new file's own book folder no longer count as another copy, and the file goes to the original book. Nothing else changes:

- A file that is **still on disk** still counts. An MP3 copy and an M4B copy kept together are still split, as before.
- A file in a **different folder** still counts, even if it's missing, for example on a drive that isn't mounted. Only files gone from this unit's own folder were replaced in place.
- A file whose presence **can't be checked** is treated as present, which keeps the old behaviour.

The disk check is `FileExistsCanonical`, the same one `MediaFileTableCleanupService` uses to decide which rows to delete. It only runs after every existing check has failed to place the file, and it stops at the first file that still counts, so the usual paths make no extra disk calls. `BookUnitDestinationService` now takes `IDiskProvider`.

Fixes #184

#### Database Migration

NO.

#### How was this tested?

**Unit tests** — four new tests in `FormatScopedUnitCloneFixture`, next to the existing test for the side-by-side split:

- `should_reuse_the_book_when_another_tool_replaced_its_files_in_place` — this one fails without the fix.
- `should_still_create_a_copy_while_any_of_the_other_container_is_on_disk`
- `should_still_create_a_copy_when_the_missing_files_were_in_another_folder`
- `should_keep_counting_a_file_whose_presence_cannot_be_checked`

The other three pass with or without the change. They are there so a looser version of this fix can't slip through. The fixture's nine existing tests now pass a disk stub that reports every tracked file as present, which is what those tests assume, so their meaning is unchanged. The full `Chaptarr.Core.Test` suite passes: 3024 passed, 0 failed.

**End to end.** I ran a local build of this branch against a test library of real files (one author with a large catalogue) and staged MP3 books into it through the API.

| Scenario | Before this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| 4 MP3s replaced in place by one M4B, then one **Rescan Folders** | A copy (`…_copy_…`) with its own edition holds the M4B. The original book is monitored with no files and sits in Wanted → Missing. | The M4B is on the **original** book, on its monitored edition. No copy is created and the book is not in Wanted. The log shows `[UNIT-REPLACED] BookId=33 only has rows for files gone from this unit's folder; reusing it …` |
| An M4B added **next to** 4 MP3s that are still there | Split into a copy | Still split into a copy (`[UNIT-CLONE] Created duplicate BookId=6439 …`), unchanged |

**Notes for reviewers:**

- In the end-to-end run, the M4B matched a different edition of the same book (651) than the one the MP3s had been imported to (642). That's the matcher reading the new file's tags. As with any import, monitoring moves to the edition that received the file, so the book stays monitored and has its file.
- This stops new copies being made. It doesn't merge copies that were created before the fix.
- A related bug I found while working around this, not fixed here: after you delete one of these copies, the destination cache in `BookUnitDestinationService` still points at the deleted book until Chaptarr restarts. Retrying the match fails with `APPLY_EXCEPTION` in the meantime. I'm happy to send a small follow-up that evicts entries for deleted books.
- The other half of #184, **Ignore Deleted Books** never unmonitoring anything, isn't addressed here. It changes behaviour and probably deserves its own discussion.

---

**A note on AI:** this change was written with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) (Claude Agent SDK), using **Claude Opus 5.5** (`claude-opus-5-5`) at **`xhigh`** reasoning effort. The diagnosis, the fix, the tests and this description were AI-generated; I reviewed them before opening the PR.

comments.body:
Related issue: #300 (https://github.com/Chaptarr/chaptarr/issues/300).

I reproduced a related EPUB case in Chaptarr 0.9.965.0: a plain external filename rename, followed by Rescan Folders, creates a second book/edition record and leaves the monitored original in Wanted → Missing. The EPUB contents and matched provider edition are unchanged. Moving the file into a series folder has the same effect.

For standalone EPUBs, the unit key includes the filename stem as well as its directory. The location comparison in this PR therefore still treats the renamed unit as a different location.

I have a tested patch limiting reattachment to the same edition, one vanished EPUB unit, and the same accessible non-Calibre root. A small per-book reservation prevents two incoming units from both claiming stale rows; canonical destinations are revalidated after relocation. That reservation is separable if you prefer the simpler policy. A real BookOrbit rename replay preserved the original book and edition, while a genuine additional EPUB stayed separate. Regression cases also cover two incoming units and stale cached ownership.

Since this touches the same constructor and destination function, would you prefer this as an extension to #185 rather than a separate PR? I can share the patch and regression cases in either form.

items.title: fix(import): warn about existing-file conflict in Manual Import preview
items.body:
## Summary

The Manual Import preview modal shows a clean "Ready now (local)" status
with zero warning even when the book already has an existing tracked file
at the managed destination (via a different download) — in **both**
Combine and Replace mode.

This happens because the "does a file already occupy this book's managed
destination" collision check
(`ImportApprovedBooks.GetAdditionalCopyPathCollisionReason`) is only ever
invoked at actual import *execution* time
(`ImportApprovedBooks.Import()`), never during the preview
(`ManualImportService.GetMediaFiles` → `MapItem`). So the preview can't
warn about something the real import will reject/overwrite a moment
later.

## Fix

- Adds `IImportApprovedBooks.CheckExistingDestinationConflict(...)`, a
  non-mutating, single-item version of the existing collision-check logic
  (reuses the same destination-path computation and file-lookup — doesn't
  duplicate it).
- `ManualImportService.MapItem` now calls it and, if a conflict is found,
  appends a `Rejection` with `RejectionType.Temporary`
  (`CanBypass = true`, Warning severity) — informational only, doesn't
  block either Combine or Replace mode, matching how other *arr apps
  surface this in their Manual Import UI.
- Null-safe (`?.`) since some existing test fixtures construct
  `ManualImportService` without `IImportApprovedBooks` wired.

Verified live against a real duplicate (a book already imported under a
different download) — the preview now shows the conflict warning in both
Combine and Replace mode, where before it showed neither.

## Test plan

- [x] Existing test suite passes in full (3,020/3,020) after adding the
      interface method's trivial stub implementations to the two
      hand-written fixtures that construct `ImportApprovedBooks`
      manually, and after making the new call site null-safe.
- [x] Live-verified against a real currently-existing duplicate on a
      running instance: preview now returns a `rejections` entry
      ("An existing file is already imported at the managed
      destination: ...") in both `replaceExistingFiles=false` and
      `replaceExistingFiles=true` modes.

items.title: fix(commands): stop disk-access groups from globally blocking each other
items.body:
## Summary

`CommandQueue.IsBlockedByDiskAccess` blocks a candidate command whenever
**any** started disk-access command is in a **different** `DiskAccessGroup`,
before it ever checks the candidate's own group against that group's limit.
That collapses every named group into a single global mutex, which
contradicts the method's own comment:

> Respect disk access groups: most disk work remains exclusive, while
> selected groups can opt into a bounded concurrency limit.

In practice, `RetryFailedImportCommand` and `DownloadedBooksScanCommand` are
the only two commands that opt into their own `"downloadImport"` group,
specifically so they can proceed independently of large `"default"`-group
sweeps (`ProcessMonitoredDownloads`, `ManualImport`, etc.). Because of this
bug they never actually could: a `ProcessMonitoredDownloads` pass over a
large library (which can legitimately run 15-30+ minutes) fully starves
`RetryFailedImport` and `ManualImport` for its entire duration, even though
`ManualImport` is submitted at `"high"` priority — priority is irrelevant
if the command can't even be selected as a candidate.

Live-reproduced on a ~3,300-item monitored-downloads backlog: submitted a
`RetryFailedImport` command while `ProcessMonitoredDownloads` was actively
running; it sat `status: "queued"` for the entire multi-minute run and only
started once `ProcessMonitoredDownloads` finished (or was cancelled).

## Fix

A candidate is now only blocked by started commands in its **own** group
exceeding that group's configured limit. Commands in different groups no
longer block each other, matching the behavior the existing code comment
already described.

Most commands don't override `DiskAccessGroup` and so still share the
implicit `"default"` group (limit 1) — they remain serialized with each
other exactly as before. Only the few commands that explicitly opt into
their own group are affected, which is the intended behavior.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `CommandQueueDiskAccessGroupFixture` covering both directions:
      a command in a different group is no longer blocked; two commands
      sharing a group are still correctly serialized.
- [x] Full existing test suite passes (3,027/3,027).
- [x] Live-verified on a running instance: submitted `RetryFailedImport`
      while a `"default"`-group `ManualImport` command was actively
      started — it started and completed within seconds, instead of
      sitting queued for the duration of the `"default"`-group work like
      it did before this fix.

items.title: Fix MAM account refresh after snatch_summary response change
items.body:
MAM changed the account response so `created` and `unsat` are now inside `snatch_summary`. Chaptarr still looks for them at the root and logs:

```text
MAM user data response did not include a valid unsatisfied-torrent summary
```

The saved status then goes stale and Protect Unsatisfied Slots blocks grabs, even though indexer searches still work. MAM posted about the change [here](https://www.myanonamouse.net/f/t/93313) (login may be required).

This reads the nested summary when present and falls back to the old format otherwise. `classname` still comes from the root. The existing validation stays in place, and the snapshot time still comes from MAM rather than the time of the request.

Added a test case for the nested response alongside the existing format. Tested the patch on Unraid with protection enabled: account status updated to 2/150 and both timestamps refreshed. Also confirmed a live grab from Chaptarr through MAM into qBittorrent, where the download started successfully.

The core test run had 3,020 passes and one failure: `standard_provider_should_fail_closed_for_non_bypassed_destination` throws `GetDomainName: -1` on this Mac. That test also fails on unmodified `develop` at `7a06004`.

Test command:

```sh
dotnet test src/Chaptarr.Core.Test/Chaptarr.Core.Test.csproj -c Release -f net10.0 -p:WarningsNotAsErrors=NU1902
```

`WarningsNotAsErrors` was needed for an existing advisory on Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git 8.0.0. No package versions were changed.

items.title: fix(download): make ProcessMonitoredDownloads honor cancellation
items.body:
## Problem

`CommandExecutor` runs `Execute(command, CancellationToken)` when a handler provides that overload. `DownloadProcessingService` (the `ProcessMonitoredDownloads` handler) only has `Execute(command)`, so it never sees the token.

`CommandQueueManager.Cancel()` marks a running command `Cancelled` immediately and cancels its token. For this handler that changes nothing: the worker thread keeps importing every tracked download until the sweep finishes, which takes minutes to an hour with a large backlog. Meanwhile:

- the command disappears from the started list, so nothing shows it is still running
- it still occupies one of the three `CommandExecutor` workers
- it no longer counts toward disk-access group limits, since those look at `Started` status

Cancelling a few sweeps this way leaves no free worker. Every other command stays `queued` while `GET /api/v1/command` shows nothing started. In our case ManualImport and RetryFailedImport sat queued for over an hour with an empty started list; a container restart "fixed" it only because it killed the ghost threads.

## Fix

Add `Execute(ProcessMonitoredDownloadsCommand, CancellationToken)` and check the token between downloads. `Execute(command)` delegates with `CancellationToken.None`, so callers are unchanged.

Other long-running handlers without a token overload probably have the same problem (not touched here).

## Verification

- New test `cancelled_sweep_should_stop_importing_instead_of_running_to_completion`.
- Full suite: 3021 passed.
- Live: started a sweep, cancelled it, and `CommandExecutor: Command ProcessMonitoredDownloadsCommand (ID: ...) was cancelled` was logged about 12s later (the in-flight download finishing). Before the change that line never appeared and the thread kept running.

items.title: fix(import): report why a manual import imported nothing
items.body:
## Problem

`ManualImportService.Execute` counts results that were not imported but drops their reasons (the decision's `Rejections` and the result's `Errors`), and it leaves the command marked successful even when zero files were imported.

Through the API this looks like:

```
status: completed, result: successful
message: Manually imported 0 files (1 failed/skipped)
```

with nothing in the log. Anything driving Manual Import through `POST /api/v1/command` (scripts, integrations) cannot tell a real import from a rejected one. In practice about 89% (816 of 920) of the manual-import commands we submitted imported nothing, and we counted them as successes because the command reported success.

## Fix

- Log every non-imported file at Warn with its reasons: `[MANUAL-IMPORT] Not imported (Rejected) '<path>': <reasons>`.
- Put the first reason in the command message: `Manually imported 0 files (1 failed/skipped: <reason>)`.
- Report the command as `Unsuccessful` when nothing was imported.

The reporter is an optional constructor argument (`ICommandResultReporter commandResultReporter = null`), so existing constructions and tests are unaffected. Partial imports keep their current result.

## Verification

- New test `manual_import_that_imports_nothing_should_report_unsuccessful_with_the_reason`.
- Full suite: 3021 passed.
- Live: the same request that previously returned a bare "0 files" now returns `result: unsuccessful` and `... 1 failed/skipped: The authoritative author catalog does not currently contain suggested work 'hc:781589' for Ebook.`, with the matching Warn line in the log.

items.title: fix(download): let ProcessMonitoredDownloads yield the disk slot to waiting commands
items.body:
> Stacked on #190 (the first commit here is that PR's commit). Review only the second commit; this rebases cleanly once #190 merges.

## Problem

`ProcessMonitoredDownloads` and `ManualImport` both use the implicit `default` disk access group, which allows one command at a time. A sweep over a large backlog can run for an hour, and during that whole time every queued `ManualImport` (submitted at high priority) waits, even though each would take seconds.

We saw 104 queued manual imports waiting behind a single sweep that had been running 42 minutes and was making real progress (about 36 imports per 10 minutes).

## Fix

Between downloads, the sweep checks whether any command that needs the same disk slot is queued. If one is, the sweep stops and returns normally. It is periodic and idempotent, so it simply resumes on its next scheduled run.

- Each run still completes at least one download that needs real work before it can yield, so a steady stream of waiting commands cannot starve the sweep.
- Downloads that need no work (already imported, and so on) are skipped and do not count toward that guarantee, so no-op entries at the front of the list cannot use it up.
- Commands in a different disk access group (for example `RetryFailedImport`'s `downloadImport`) and commands that do not need disk access never cause a yield.
- When nothing is waiting, behaviour is unchanged. The queue manager is an optional constructor argument, so existing constructions are unaffected.

## Verification

- Four new tests: yields for a waiting `ManualImport`; does not yield for a command that needs no disk slot; does not yield for a different disk access group; no-op entries do not use up the one-download guarantee.
- Full suite: 3025 passed.
- Live, after deploying: sweeps that used to run 40+ minutes while manual imports queued behind them completed in 3m23s and 26s while manual imports were running. (The yield itself is logged at Debug, so this evidence is the durations and the manual imports starting without any cancel, not a log line.)

items.title: fix(ui): don't open a blank confirmation when a manual import replaces no local book
items.body:
## Problem

In the queue, Manual Import runs with "Replace Existing Files" on. Import then opens a confirmation listing the existing files that would be replaced. For a row that only has a *metadata suggestion* (no local book, badge "Will add from metadata"), the confirmation requests `/bookFile` with no filter. The API answers `500 authorId, bookId, bookFileIds or unmapped must be provided`, the request fails, and the dialog stays blank forever. No import is ever sent and nothing explains why.

## Fix

Skip the confirmation when no selected row has a local book: nothing can be replaced, so there is nothing to confirm.

## Verification

Reproduced in headless Chrome (Playwright) against a running instance:

- before: click Import on a "Will add from metadata" row, a second dialog opens empty and stays empty for 20+ seconds, no `POST /api/v1/command` is sent;
- after: the same click sends `POST /api/v1/command` and the dialog closes.

There is no frontend unit test setup in the repo, so this is verified end to end rather than by a unit test.

items.title: fix(import): don't let an explicit Move override "this torrent's files cannot be moved"
items.body:
## Problem

`DownloadImportModeResolver` resolves `Auto` to `Copy` when the download client reports `CanMoveFiles = false` (for qBittorrent: the client is not set to remove completed downloads, or the seed limit isn't reached, i.e. the torrent is still seeding). An **explicit** `Move` skips that check and is honored.

So a Manual Import requested with `importMode: move` (for example through `POST /api/v1/command`) relocates the files of a torrent that is still seeding. The client keeps reporting it healthy (`stalledUP`) while its files no longer exist. We hit this on 17 torrents.

## Fix

Resolve an explicit `Move` for a torrent whose client says the files cannot be moved to `Copy`, exactly as `Auto` already does. Unchanged: explicit `Move` when the client says the files can be moved, non-torrent clients, and the existing indexer / client "never move" overrides.

## Verification

Three new resolver tests (move becomes copy when it cannot be moved; stays move when it can; stays move for usenet). Full suite passes apart from two conversion-cancel tests that are already flaky on `develop` under load.

Not verified live: I did not want to repeat the damage on a real torrent to prove it.

items.title: fix(commands): keep a cancelled running command Started until its handler exits
items.body:
> Related to #190, which makes `ProcessMonitoredDownloads` observe the token. This change is independent of it.

## Problem

`CommandQueueManager.Cancel` signals the token and immediately relabels a running command `Cancelled`. A handler that does not observe the token (many do not) keeps running on its worker thread, but the command has already left the started list and stops counting toward disk access group limits. A few such cancels can occupy every worker while `GET /api/v1/command` shows nothing running and every other command sits `queued`.

## Fix

For a running command whose token was signalled, set the message to `Cancelling` and leave it `Started`. The executor already marks it `Cancelled` when the handler throws `OperationCanceledException`, or `Completed` if it finishes anyway. A second cancel is a no-op. Cancelling a queued or paused command is unchanged.

## Verification

- Three new tests: a running command stays `Started` and its token is signalled; cancelling twice does not relabel it; a queued command is still cancelled immediately. The first fails without the change.
- Live: cancelled a running `ProcessMonitoredDownloads`; it stayed `started` with message `Cancelling` (the sweep was inside a large multi-file import) instead of disappearing while still busy.

items.title: fix(import): warn in the Manual Import preview when a suggestion cannot be added from metadata
items.body:
## Problem

A metadata suggestion can add a missing work only when the request carries an edition id (`MaterializeUserSelectedEditionAsync`). A suggestion that has only a work id falls back to `AddAuthorAsync`, which returns an author that already exists unchanged, so the work is never added and execution rejects the import:

> The authoritative author catalog does not currently contain suggested work 'hc:781589' for Ebook.

The preview shows no rejection and the UI labels the row "Will add from metadata" / "Select to Add", so the failure only appears after clicking Import.

## Fix

When the suggested author is local, the suggested work is not in that author's local catalog for the file's media type, and the suggestion has no edition id, add a warning rejection to the preview row saying it cannot be added from metadata and a local book must be selected. Rows the server can act on are unchanged.

This does not make such suggestions importable. The real fix (choosing an edition for a work-only suggestion, or making the add path work for existing authors) needs a design decision, so this PR only stops the preview from promising something execution cannot do. It does not cover suggestions whose work is in the catalog but where the grouped matcher then fails to place the file; that needs the matcher itself run in the preview.

## Verification

- Four new tests: flagged when missing with no edition id; not flagged when in the catalog, when an edition id is present, or when the author is not local yet.
- Live: the preview for a real affected item now returns the warning (`type: temporary`, `canBypass: true`, severity 2).

comments.body: Closing: superseded by #201, which makes these files importable instead of only warning about them.

items.title: perf(matching): don't use bare function words as Postgres FTS recall keys
items.body:
## Problem

`EditionFtsRepository.RecallBooksPostgres` ORs every token of a file's title under the `simple` text search configuration, which has no stopword list. A bare `and` or `the` therefore matches tens of thousands of editions. Matching issues this query once per file, so a several-hundred-file audiobook keeps Postgres busy for minutes and makes import sweeps very slow.

Measured on a 315k-book library (`EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` and `pg_stat_statements`):

- The GIN indexes are used; this is not a missing index. The cost is the width of the recall.
- An 11-term query pulled 80,091 candidate editions and 37,822 books before `LIMIT 20` (`and` alone matches 57,278 editions, `1` matches 16,938).
- Execution: 1,238 ms for the full query, 506 ms with `and` dropped, 29 ms with the common words dropped.
- In production the query averaged 1,112 ms per call (2,532 calls, 2.8M ms total), about 11% of all recorded database time, with Postgres near 150% CPU during import sweeps.

## Fix

Drop a small list of English function words (`a`, `an`, `and`, `the`, `of`, `in`, `to`) from the Postgres recall terms. Deliberately kept: digits and series words (`part`, `book`, `volume`), because they distinguish books in a series. If nothing but stopwords remains, the original terms are kept, so a title made only of stopwords still recalls. Only the Postgres path changes.

## Verification

- Four new tests: function words are dropped; series words and digits are kept; an all-stopword title keeps its terms; matching is case-insensitive.
- Full suite passes.
- Live, before/after on the same instance: the recall query averaged 1,112 ms per call before and 374 ms per call over the 16,117 calls since deploy (about 3x faster), with the host load average falling from about 95 to 20 over the same period. The workload mix changed between the two windows, so treat the ratio as indicative.

## Not verified

Matching quality: I did not compare recalled candidates before and after for a sample of files. The dropped words only contributed candidates that matched on the function word alone, but a reviewer with a larger regression corpus may want to check.

comments.body:
Added a second commit to this PR: prune common tokens from the Postgres FTS book recall by document frequency.

Stopword removal alone still left tokens like `book`, `part` and digits matching tens of thousands of editions. On a live library (346k books) a query like `legend | of | drizzt | book | passage | to | dawn` produced 47,645 candidate books and ~344k buffer hits just to return LIMIT 20. The recall query accounted for 15.8k CPU-seconds over 59k calls (266 ms mean) and saturated the host.

The candidate CTE now uses only tokens whose document frequency is below 1% of editions (floor 500; measured with a cached, bounded probe against the existing GIN index, 1h TTL); ranking still uses the full query so surviving scores are unchanged. If every token is common the two least-common are kept; any probe failure falls back to the unpruned query.

Measured after deploying: mean 266 ms -> 7 ms for the recall query and host load 134 -> ~10. Core tests pass (3,035).

items.title: fix(import): stop multi-file upgrade imports from deleting their own new files
items.body:
## Summary
An automatic import that upgrades an existing multi-file release (typical: a multi-part audiobook whose new release uses the same destination filenames) deleted its own freshly written files. Only the last part of the set survived.

## Cause
A book group is imported file by file, but the old rows are only removed by one group-level `ReplaceMany` at the end. For every file the replacement selection re-reads the book's rows from the database, so each file sees *all* old rows as "to replace". Because both releases produce the same filenames in the same folder, from the second file on the "old file" at a path is the new file written by the previous iteration; it is staged to a `.chaptarr-upgrade~` backup and then recycled by `FinalizePendingFileCommits` (a permanent delete when no recycle bin is configured).

A second, smaller problem is in the same flow: when a file's destination path is already tracked by an old row, `ResolveBookFilePathConflict` reused that row, but an earlier file of the same batch had already queued it for replacement, so the group-level replace deleted the row that now described the new file. The file stayed on disk with no `BookFiles` row.

## Fix
- `BookImportBatchState` tracks the destination paths written and the row ids displaced or reused by the batch in progress; replacement selection (`IsReplaceableExistingFile`, pure and unit tested) and the staging loop never treat those as old files.
- A row reused at an imported destination is always reused in place and kept out of the batch's `ReplaceMany`; pending commits are kept so staged backups are still recycled and are never rolled back once persisted.
Normal single-file upgrades are unchanged.

## Evidence
On a live library (~200k files) this produced 8,202 `BookFileDeleted`/`Upgrade` history rows in 32 hours; 1,623 of the 1,633 later `MissingFromDisk` removals were at paths an upgrade had already deleted at the same path. 193 editions imported as multi-file sets ended up with far fewer files (e.g. 880 imported -> 1). After the fix, restoring a 173-part audiobook and a 5-part audiobook by re-import gave all files on disk, one row each, and no deletion events.

## Tests
New regression tests reproduce both failures (3-part audiobook, `replaceExisting: true`, old release occupying the identical destination paths) and fail on current `develop`. `ImportApprovedBooks|MediaFile|UpgradeMediaFile|ManualImport`: 738 passed.

## Not addressed
`UpgradeMediaFileService.UpgradeBookFile` (reachable via `BookImportService.ImportFileAsync`) still recycles every file in `Book.BookFiles` before writing; it cannot delete the new file but would wipe a book's other parts if one part is imported through it. Separate follow-up.

items.title: fix(manual-import): materialize a suggested work when the suggestion has no edition id
items.body:
## Summary
Importing a "Suggested author" item whose author already exists locally failed when the suggestion carried a provider work id but no edition id: the work stayed missing from the catalog and the import was rejected ("authoritative author catalog does not currently contain suggested work").

## Cause
Materialization of a suggested work was gated on an edition id. Without one the code fell back to `AddAuthorAsync`, which is a no-op for an existing author, so the work was never created.

## Fix
`MaterializeUserSelectedEditionAsync` now accepts a suggestion without an edition id and resolves the edition itself, failing closed:
1. the only remote edition of the requested media type under that work; else the one whose title matches the suggested edition title; else the provider's default edition when exactly one matches;
2. when several editions remain, no edition is pinned: the work is created through the normal author reconcile (so the metadata profile still applies) and the resulting book's own monitored edition is used;
3. if the work already exists locally it is reused without reconciling the author's whole catalogue;
4. an inferred edition that carries no provider edition id is matched structurally (`EditionsMatch`) instead of failing.
If nothing resolves, the previous add-author path still runs. `ManualImportService` no longer requires an edition id to take this path for user metadata suggestions.

## Evidence
On a live library the failing cases (prolific authors, works with 13-52 audiobook editions) now import; about 300 queued items imported through this path with `replaceExistingFiles=false`, copy mode, files verified on disk.

## Tests
New unit tests for the edition inference (single edition, title tie-break, provider default, fail-closed on ambiguity). `AuthorLibraryService|ManualImport`: 72 passed.

comments.body: Fixes the main case in #198.

items.title: log: report per-book 'no editions' skips at debug; keep the per-author warning summary

## Summary
`RefreshAuthorService.ExcludeBooksWithoutEditions` logged one `[Error]` line per remote book that has no editions, then a per-author `[Warn]` summary. On a large library a single refresh pass produced thousands of error lines (6,717 in 40 minutes) for a condition that is expected and already summarised.

items.title: perf: batch the author-list N+1 queries and the queue conversion-job lookups; scope the FTS recall candidates
items.body:
## Summary
`GET /api/v1/author` (called by the web UI on load) took ~12 s on a 2,659-author / 340k-book library, mostly in ~10,000 single-row lazy-load queries.

## Cause
`AuthorController.LinkNextPreviousBooks` batched the fetch of each author's next/last book but mapped every book with the rich resource options, which touch `Editions`, `Author` and `BookFiles` (lazy loads: one query each per book), plus an O(n*m) `FirstOrDefault` to pair books with authors.

## Changes
- Next/last books are hydrated up front: `Author` from the models the request already holds, `Editions` and `BookFiles` from one batched lookup each; pairing uses a dictionary. `nextBook`/`lastBook` are mapped with the lean options, so they no longer carry `overview` and `links` (checked against `frontend/src`: the author index only reads `id`, `title`, `titleSlug`, `disambiguation`, `releaseDate`).
- `QueueService.ApplyConversionStatuses` queried `ConversionJobs` once per queue item on every queue build (~220 queries/s with a ~2,600 item queue) and only used non-completed rows; it now issues one `NonCompleted` query.
- The Postgres FTS recall repeats the media-type and author-scope predicates inside every candidate branch; the outer query already applies them, so rows and scores are identical, but the candidate set is smaller before ranking.

## Evidence
Live: `GET /author` 12.4 s -> 1.6 s (payload 15.6 MB -> 14.3 MB). The recall change was A/B tested read-only against 60 real cases: identical ordered top-20 lists in author-scoped and unscoped modes, ~2x faster scoped and ~20% faster unscoped.

## Tests
New fixture asserts the number of edition/file lookups does not scale with the number of authors or books (1/50/500 authors). `AuthorController|Api|Queue|Fts|Conversion|ImportApprovedBooks`: 244 passed.

comments.body: Also fixes #165.

items.title: perf: count missing books with a semi-join and bound per-author file statistics
items.body:
## Summary
Two SQL statements dominated the `wanted/missing` page and the per-author statistics on a large library.

## Changes
- Missing-books total: `COUNT(DISTINCT Books.Id)` over `Books x Editions x BookFiles` anti-join walked, sorted and de-duplicated ~240k rows to produce one number. It now uses an `EXISTS (monitored edition) AND NOT EXISTS (file)` semi-join against `Books`/`Authors` only. Same number (238,045 in both forms on a live database), 1.0 s -> 0.32 s.
- Per-author statistics: the file-statistics derived table aggregated every `BookFiles` row before the author filter applied. The single-author overloads now restrict the aggregate to that author's books (the id is an int, so it is inlined safely). Same rows (book, size and file counts identical on two real authors), 212 ms -> 7 ms and 147 ms -> 1 ms per call.

## Tests
New test asserts the missing-books total equals the distinct books listed for ebook, audiobook and unfiltered requests. `AuthorStat|BookRepository|Wanted`: 37 passed.

items.title: Fix Goodreads searches failing on duplicate HTTP cache rows
items.body:
## Problem
Searches intermittently (then permanently for that query) fail with `Invalid response received from Goodreads`, caused by `InvalidOperationException: Sequence contains more than one element` in `CachedHttpResponseService.Get`.

Concurrent lookups of the same URL each insert a row into the HTTP cache (the `IX_HttpResponse_Url` index is not unique), and `CachedHttpResponseRepository.FindByUrl` used `SingleOrDefault`, so every later lookup of that URL throws. Rows are never removed on that path, so it never heals.

Measured on a live cache: 7,846 rows for 6,261 distinct URLs, 782 URLs with duplicates (one with 47 rows); 380 errors in three days.

## Fix
`FindByUrl` returns the newest row (by `LastRefresh`, then `Id`) and deletes the stale duplicates (best effort: a failed cleanup is logged at debug level and retried on the next lookup).

## Verification
- Core tests pass (3,020 on top of develop).
- On the live instance a search that had been failing (`james patterson - world champions!`) returned 200 after deploying the change, its duplicate rows were gone, and no new `more than one element` errors appeared.
- Adds `CachedHttpResponseRepositoryFixture` (SQLite-backed): no row, a single row untouched, newest of many duplicates wins and stale ones are removed, `LastRefresh` ties go to the highest Id, and a failing delete does not fail the lookup (3,025 core tests pass).

Note: the non-unique `IX_HttpResponse_Url` index and the find-then-insert race still create duplicates; this change makes them self-heal on the next lookup. A unique index would need a dedupe migration, so it is left out of scope here.

items.title: Fix IndexOutOfRangeException pruning the inferred-quality queue cache
items.body:
## Problem
`QueueService.PruneInferredQualityCache` enumerates `_inferredQualityCache.Keys` and removes entries while queue refreshes add entries from other threads. The cache is a plain `Dictionary`, so this races and throws `IndexOutOfRangeException` (1,438 errors in one 90-minute window under load).

## Fix
Use a `ConcurrentDictionary` and `TryRemove`. The cache key now also includes the media type: one download can map to an audiobook and an ebook sibling, and the inferred quality depends on the media type (before, the second book was shown the first book's quality, e.g. an ebook queue item reporting `MP3`). Pruning still works by download id.

## Verification
Core tests pass (3,020 on top of develop). Deployed on the live instance under queue load with no recurrence.
- Adds `QueueServiceInferredQualityCacheFixture`: a concurrent-refresh stress test (fails 3/3 runs on the old `Dictionary` with the production `IndexOutOfRangeException`, passes now), per-media-type quality, and prune-then-re-infer (3,023 core tests pass).

items.title: Do not fail the manual import preview when a file has vanished
items.body:
## Problem
`ManualImportService.MapItem` reads `fileInfo.Length` for every previewed file. `FileInfo.Length` throws `FileNotFoundException` if the file was removed between listing and mapping, which fails the whole `GET /manualimport` request (logged as Fatal; 11 in three days).

## Fix
Report size 0 for a missing file instead of throwing, so the rest of the preview is returned. The vanished file itself comes back as a rejected item ("Failed to process file: ..."), so it cannot be imported.

## Verification
Core tests pass (3,020 on top of develop). Deployed on the live instance.
- Adds `ManualImportVanishedFileFixture`: previews one present and one vanished file; fails with `FileNotFoundException` without the guard and passes with it (3,021 core tests pass).

items.title: Log per-book 'no editions' skips at debug level
items.body:
## Problem
`RefreshAuthorService` logs an Error line for every remote book skipped because it has no editions: about 103,000 Error lines in three days on one instance. This buries real errors and bloats the log database.

## Fix
Per-book line moves to Debug; the existing per-author summary Warn (`skipped N remote books with no editions`) is kept.

## Verification
Core tests pass (3,020 on top of develop). Deployed on the live instance.

comments.body: Duplicate of #202, which already makes this change.

items.title: Fix bulk author editor returning 500 when it queues refresh commands
items.body:
## Problem
`PUT /api/v1/author/editor` saves the changes and then returns 500 with `The member p0_Body of type ...RefreshAuthorCommand cannot be used as a parameter value` when it queues follow-up commands (for example when an author gains an audiobook/ebook root folder), so the refreshes are never queued.

`CommandQueueManager.PushMany` inserts through `InsertMany`, whose Postgres batch path hands Dapper each command's runtime `Body` type. Dapper has no type handler for the concrete command types, so it throws.

## Fix
Insert the commands one at a time in `PushMany`; `Insert` maps by the declared `Body` column type. These batches are small. Each command is queued right after its own row is inserted (as `Push` does), so a failure part-way through cannot leave inserted rows that are never added to the in-memory queue.

## Verification
Core tests pass (3,020 on top of develop). On a live instance the bulk editor call that returned 500 before returns 202 after the change, for 800+ authors in batches of 100.
- Adds `CommandQueueManagerPushManyFixture`: `InsertMany` is no longer used and ids stay in order, an empty batch does nothing, and a mid-batch insert failure leaves the already-inserted commands queued (3,023 core tests pass).

items.title: fix(import): retry unmatched completed downloads with the manual preview matching context
items.body:
## Problem
Automatic download import leaves files `importBlocked` ("No match in local library. Suggested author: X (hc:NNN).") that the Manual Import screen resolves on sight: `GET /api/v1/manualimport` returns a local `editionId` and no rejections for the same file.

The two paths differ in exactly one matching flag. `ProcessFolder` gates path/filename evidence behind `ShouldAllowTrackedDownloadPathFallback`, which needs a tracked download with a resolved single author AND exactly one grabbed target book. A completed download without a usable grabbed identity matches with `DisablePathFallback=true`, so `HolyGrailEvaluation` returns early for a file whose embedded tags carry nothing searchable. The preview context defaults `allowPathFallback` to true, so the same file resolves.

## Fix
After the strict pass (and the author-auto-add rematch), re-run only the still-unmatched files with `ForDownloaded(false, targetBookIds, allowPathFallback: true)`: the preview's context minus provider identification. The strict pass stays authoritative; this only adds a fail-open retry where today's outcome is an unconditional block. Guards carried over: `UsePathAsTagsFallback`/Strict still disable it, the author restriction and grabbed target books apply, no author is imported, and a multi-file leftover set resolving to more than one book is discarded as ambiguous.

Trade-off: path evidence now reaches the library for downloads with no grabbed identity, which is more permissive than before, bounded by the matcher's own smoke test and author/title proofs (unchanged).

The parity pass only runs for tracked downloads (a download client item), never for an untracked drop folder, and a multi-file leftover set is accepted only when every file matches the same book; a partial match is discarded (it would leave the edition partly filled, and a later attempt to add the rest fails with "Edition already has files"). Unattended path evidence therefore never applies to untracked folders.

## Verification
- New `AutoImportLocalPreviewParityFixture` (strict context blocks, parity/preview contexts match, near-miss folder name stays unmatched, same-title twin decided by author evidence) plus new `DownloadedBooksImportService` tests.
- Core tests pass (3,028 on top of develop).
- Live: running on a live instance, blocked queue items that the preview resolved were imported by the automatic path.
- Two review-driven tests in `DownloadedBooksImportServiceFixture`: untracked folders are not retried with path fallback, and a partial leftover match imports nothing (3,030 core tests pass).

items.title: fix(tags): don't fail ebook tag reading on a null tag value (unparseable AZW3/MOBI ISBN)
items.body:
## Problem
`Truncate()` called `Encoding.UTF8.GetByteCount(s)` without a null check, so a null tag value threw `ArgumentNullException` from the per-field debug logging loop of every ebook reader. `ReadAllAzw3Tags` stored exactly such a value: an ISBN that is present but unparseable makes `StripIsbn` return null. The exception was wrapped as `TagExtractionException` and failed the whole import of an otherwise readable ebook.

## Fix
`Truncate` returns null/empty input unchanged, and the AZW3/MOBI reader only stores an ISBN it could actually parse.

## Verification
- New `FluentTruncateFixture`.
- Core tests pass (3,026 on top of develop).
- Live: deployed on a live instance; affected ebooks import instead of ending as `IMPORT_EXCEPTION`.
- Adds `EBookTagServiceIsbnTagFixture` (7 cases; reverting the fix makes 2 fail: an unparseable ISBN stored a null tag) (3,033 core tests pass).

Scope note: this fixes the `ArgumentNullException` from null tag values (mainly the AZW3/MOBI ISBN). Genuinely unreadable files (PDF XRef errors, corrupt archives) still throw `TagExtractionException`, which is intended.

items.title: fix(import): accept a same-work different-media-type pocket match for a completed download
items.body:
Depends on the parity-retry PR (`fix-auto-import-local-preview-parity`); it is stacked on that branch.

## Problem
`EnforceTrackedDownloadTargetBooks` rejects any match whose `BookId` differs from a grabbed target book. That blocks audio downloads whose files correctly resolve to the audiobook pocket of a work that was grabbed against its ebook pocket ("grabbed for 'The Vines' (BookId 166297, work hc:514913), but import matched 'The Vines' (BookId 290880, work hc:514913)"). `RetargetSameWorkMatchesToGrabbedBook` cannot help: it deliberately requires identical `MediaType`, because audio files must not be filed under the ebook row.

## Fix
An off-target match is accepted when all off-target files resolved to the same book row (more than one stays an ambiguous multi-book rejection), that row has the same author as exactly one grabbed target book, shares a canonical work provider id with it (`WorkIdMatcher.WorkProviderIdMatches`, work-level ids only), and its `MediaType` matches the media type of the files. Different works, different authors and one-sided work ids keep being rejected.

## Verification
- New `DownloadedBooksImportService` tests for each accepted/rejected combination.
- Core tests pass (3,032 with the parity PR underneath).
- Live: confirmed on a live instance against "grabbed for X but import matched Y" queue items.

The rule requires the grabbed target to have a different media type than the matched row: a same-format sibling row (for example another narrator's audiobook) is handled by the existing retarget step and is not accepted here, including in multi-book grabs.
- Two tests in `DownloadedBooksImportServiceFixture`: a same-media-type sibling in a multi-book grab is rejected (fails without the fix), and a different-media pocket is still accepted in a multi-book grab (3,034 core tests pass).

items.title: fix(download): bound how long ProcessMonitoredDownloads yields the disk slot
items.body:
Depends on #192 (`fix-sweep-yield-to-waiting-commands`); stacked on that branch.

## Problem
A client that keeps `ManualImport` commands queued continuously keeps a same-slot command waiting at all times, so `ProcessMonitoredDownloads` yielded after its first download on every run and never refreshed the rest of the queue. Imported downloads stayed in the download client queue and completed downloads were not processed for as long as manual imports kept arriving (observed live while working through a large blocked queue).

## Fix
Count consecutive yields and stop yielding after three, so the next run processes the remaining downloads to completion before the counter resets. A fresh sweep still steps aside for a waiting manual import.

## Verification
- New `DownloadProcessingService` tests for the bounded yield.
- Core tests pass (3,028 with #192 underneath).
- Live: after deploying, the sweep resumed processing and refreshing the queue while manual imports kept arriving.
- Adds two tests in `DownloadProcessingServiceFixture`: the sweep yields again after the run that finished the backlog, and a cancelled sweep neither consumes nor resets the yield bound (3,030 core tests pass).

Trade-off: after `MaxConsecutiveYields` (3) yields the next run processes the whole backlog while holding the disk slot, so manual imports can wait for one full sweep; that is what bounds the starvation of the sweep itself.

items.title: fix(import): treat equal-quality automatic imports as duplicates instead of replacing files
items.body:
Depends on #200 (`fix-upgrade-deletes-new-files`); stacked on that branch.

## Problem
`ImportApprovedBooks.ImportFile` built `filesToReplace` from every existing file of the matched edition and, for an automatic import (`replaceExisting: true` from `DownloadedBooksImportService`), staged, replaced and recycled them whenever the new copy was not a strictly lower *revision*. A second copy of an already-imported release therefore churned the library: on a live instance 2,525 editions were re-imported in the same format as "Upgrade".

## Fix
An automatic import (not `IsManualImport`, not `DownloadForced`) only displaces existing files when the shared upgrade rule says the release is a real upgrade for the edition's quality profile (`IUpgradableSpecification.IsUpgradable` plus `IsUpgradeAllowed`, the same comparison search, queue and history use). Equal or worse is reported as "Already imported: this edition already has files of equal or better quality" and nothing is moved, deleted or recycled. Rows whose file is missing on disk are excluded. Manual imports and forced grabs are unchanged. The rejection surfaces through the normal "nothing imported" path (`importBlocked` with that message); no new queue state is invented.

## Verification
- New `ImportApprovedBooksAdditionalCopyFixture` cases (equal quality, worse, real upgrade, missing-on-disk row, manual/forced unchanged).
- Core tests pass (3,030 with #200 underneath).
- Live: duplicate releases now show "Already imported: this edition already has files of equal or better quality" instead of re-importing.

Partial editions: if the surviving rows declare more parts than are present (for example an edition left with 2 of 4 parts by the same-path upgrade bug fixed in #200), the complete incoming set is accepted and replaces the partial set instead of being rejected as a duplicate; complete duplicates are still rejected.

Note: for a profile with `UpgradeAllowed` false the existing code routes an equal-or-worse re-download to an additional copy before this guard runs, so the "Already imported" rejection applies to profiles that allow upgrades.
- Tests: existing 2 of 4 parts with an incoming complete set of equal quality is accepted (failed before the fix); a multi-file upgrade parses each stored file's custom formats once per batch, not once per incoming file (3,032 core tests pass).

items.title: fix(import): reject an automatic import onto an occupied destination instead of throwing
items.body:
Depends on #200 and on the equal-quality guard PR (`fix-equal-quality-duplicate-guard`); stacked on that branch.

## Problem
An automatic import whose computed destination path already held a file that `filesToReplace` did not cover reached `CopyBookFile`/`MoveBookFile`, where `ClearTargetPath` throws `DestinationAlreadyExistsException` and the queue item ends as `IMPORT_EXCEPTION` (about 2,700 `DestinationAlreadyExists` errors logged in three days on a live instance). `filesToReplace` only covers rows of the same edition at a different path, so a destination occupied by an untracked file or by a row tracked for another edition of the same book was never caught.

## Fix
`ImportFile` checks the computed destination before any staging or transfer, for automatic imports only: a row tracked for this edition gives the existing already-imported rejection, a row for another edition or an untracked file gives a clear rejection naming the destination. Nothing is moved or deleted. Manual imports, forced downloads, relocations and genuine upgrades are unaffected.

## Verification
- Extended `ImportApprovedBooksAdditionalCopyFixture`.
- Core tests pass (3,035 with the two PRs underneath).
- Live: affected items are rejected with a message naming the destination instead of ending as `IMPORT_EXCEPTION`.

The destination check is skipped when the destination folder does not exist (nothing can occupy it), so ordinary imports do not pay for `FileExists`' path-resolution fallback, which lists every directory along a missing path. The transfer keeps its own check.
- Adds `automatic_import_into_a_folder_that_does_not_exist_should_not_probe_the_destination_file` (records `FileExists` calls; failed with 1 probe, passes with 0) (3,038 core tests pass).

comments.body: Related: #50.

items.title: fix(import): reject a manual import onto an occupied destination instead of throwing
items.body:
DRAFT. Depends on `fix-auto-import-occupied-destination` (stacked on it).

## Problem
A manual import with `replaceExistingFiles=false` skipped the occupied-destination check that automatic imports get, so an untracked file or a file tracked for another edition at the managed destination reached the transfer, which threw `DestinationAlreadyExistsException` after staging began and was logged as an Error with a stack for every retry.

## Fix
Apply the same pre-check when the import will not replace files. A tracked file that this import replaces is still exempt.

## Verification
- Test added; fails without the fix.
- Core tests pass (3,036 with the earlier PRs underneath).
- Not yet exercised live: deployed, but no manual import has hit an occupied destination since.

The check applies to every import except relocations and forced downloads: a replacing manual import onto an untracked file, or one tracked for another edition, is rejected too (the transfer never overwrites, so it used to throw after staging began).
- Adds `manual_import_with_replace_onto_an_untracked_occupied_destination_should_be_rejected_not_throw` (failed with `Imported` before the fix) (3,040 core tests pass).

items.title: perf(books): reuse the author book list and cache BuildWorkGroups per author (#163, #172)
items.body:
DRAFT. Depends on #168 (`perf-163-rootfolders-refetch-per-workgroup`); stacked on that branch. Continues #163/#172.

## Problem
`GetSyncUpdatesForMutations` calls `BuildWorkGroups` once per book saved, and each call re-fetches the author's book list and recomputes the groups. A dotnet-trace against a live instance while Charles Dickens (10,107 books) was refreshing showed `BuildWorkGroups` at about 99% of sampled CPU in a 30-second window. It is itself O(N^2) (pairwise `WorkIdMatcher.CrossFormatSafeMatches`), so for an N-book author it is an O(N^2) call made up to N times.

## Fix
1. Reuse the author's already-loaded book list instead of re-fetching and re-cloning it per book saved (fixes the database side of the repetition).
2. Cache `BuildWorkGroups` per author instead of recomputing per book saved (fixes the CPU side).

## Verification
- Core tests pass (3,020 with #168 underneath).
- No end-to-end timing recorded after the change; the profile above is the motivation. Left as a draft until a before/after refresh time is measured.

## Review update (concurrency and staleness)
An adversarial review found that the first version kept the hint and the work-group cache in fields shared across authors. Per-author `RefreshAuthorCommand`s are not disk-access exclusive and run concurrently (3 by default, more when the command thread count is raised, #222), so one refresh could pair another author's grouping with its own hint and apply monitoring changes to the wrong books. Fixed:
- One `AuthorBooksHint` object held in an `AsyncLocal` for the length of `RefreshBookInfo` (per refresh, not shared).
- Cached groups are stored as ids, remapped onto the current `Book` instances (sync decisions use current monitored flags), and rebuilt whenever any identity the grouping depends on changes (provider ids move and merge during a refresh).
- Deleted books are removed from the hint.
- Four tests, two deterministic ones fail on the original code with the exact symptoms; the concurrency stress test is a regression guard only (3,024 core tests pass).

Note: the hint avoids the database re-fetch of the author's books, not the per-save clone of them; that clone remains.

comments.body: Measured on a live library (346k books) while refreshing large authors with this PR deployed: the monitoring-sync author-book load that this PR targets no longer appears among the top statements. The remaining per-book full-catalogue read was EnsureUniqueTitleSlugs, fixed separately in #221. Marking ready for review.

items.title: fix(authors): fill the missing format root folder from the default when an author is added
items.body:
## Problem
Import paths create an author for the one format being imported and leave the other format's root folder blank. Measured on a live instance: 509 audiobook-only and 303 ebook-only authors created in one week. Those authors are rejected by "sync monitored across formats" (it requires both roots; the bulk editor warned "Sync was enabled for 1899 author(s). 509 author(s) were skipped because both audiobook and ebook root folders are required."), and later imports of the other format fail with "No root folder configured for quality type".

## Fix
`AuthorService.AddAuthor`/`AddAuthors` fill each blank root from the effective default root folder for that format (the configured default, else the only compatible root). Explicit values are never overwritten, and a root is left blank when the default is missing or ambiguous. `AuthorPathBuilder.BuildPathForQuality` still throws for a format the author has no root for (intentional signal).

## Verification
- New `AuthorServiceDefaultRootFoldersFixture` (fill both directions, no overwrite, ambiguous default, configured default with several roots, no roots).
- Core tests pass (3,026 on top of develop).
- Not yet confirmed live on a newly created author.

Behaviour note: a filled root has effects beyond the path. `EnsureAuthorDbFields` copies that root folder's default quality and metadata profiles and monitored flags onto the author, so an author added for one format now also gets the other format's profiles and monitoring from the root's defaults, and becomes eligible for sync across formats (seeded only if the root folder has an explicit sync default). Pending-import adds previously left that format's profile at 0. This is add-time only and not opt-out; with automatic search enabled it can start grabbing the second format.
- Adds a DI test that resolves `AuthorService` from a real DryIoc container with the app's rules and checks the configured default is honoured, i.e. the optional `IConfigService` argument is injected in production (3,027 core tests pass).
